**2026-09-25 — SLICE 64: A BUDGET ALERT LINKS TO THE MONEY PAGE ONLY WHEN THAT PAGE WOULD OPEN (founder decision C34).**

**ASKED AND ANSWERED straight after slice 63's review raised it:** a budget alert keeps its project's name and drops its link when the receiver cannot open the Money page. That covers Time switched off, and a receiver without the page's codes. Budget alerts go to the budget's notify list or the project lead, not to holders of those codes.

**WHAT SHIPPED.**
- **`src/modules/time/money-codes.ts`**, a module with no imports:
  - `PROJECT_MONEY_CODES` (`time:view_team`, `rate:view_bill`). `projectMoney` now asks these in turn, and the inbox asks the same list.
  - `BUDGET_ALERT_ENTITY`, which `budgets.ts` emits and the inbox matches, so the string lives in one place.
- **`src/notify/inbox.ts`:** `InboxSubject.href` may be null. `resolveSubjects` asks the Money codes on all four gates when a page holds a budget alert, and links only a row naming that entity.
- **Both inbox views** (the list and `/home`'s card) render a linkless subject as plain text, truncated with its full value as `title` (UI.md §10.12).
- **`projectMoney`'s three-leg `Promise.all` now runs in sequence**, because the inbox's test calls it.
- **Tests:**
  - `money-codes.test.ts` pins the list: exactly these two codes, catalogue codes, and no ✦.
  - A dbtest case holds the link to the PAGE ITSELF: in every state, the link is absent exactly when `projectMoney` rejects with an `AuthzError`. The states are the owner; an employee without the codes; a manager with ONE of the two revoked, which is how it tells "every code" from "some"; and Time switched off, on `/home`'s card too.

**THE REVIEW: 1 fresh agent, about 0.21M subagent tokens. No high, no medium.** Fixed:
- The leaf file's stated reason, "an import cycle", was false.
- A stale comment.
- The test could not tell `.every` from `.some`.
- The truncated plain name had no `title`.
- The link was offered for EVERY non-task row, not just budget alerts.
- The docs trailed the code.

**THE FIX REVIEW: 1 fresh agent, about 0.23M. No high, no medium.** Fixed:
- The leaf file's SECOND stated reason ("the inbox is on every render, and `money.ts` would drag the rates in") was also false, because the layout already loads the whole time module through `./time/actions`. It now says only that the notify layer depends on a contract rather than on service code.
- Nothing pinned the list itself: dropping `time:view_team` would have passed every test and opened the page to a role holding `rate:view_bill` alone. `money-codes.test.ts` now pins it.
- The test restored the revoked row with a different `source`. It now revokes the product's way (`source` → `TENANT_REVOKE`) and puts the row back exactly.
- `"ProjectBudget"` existed twice, unguarded.
- Sequencing `projectMoney`'s batch.

Noted: `permissionsVersion` is written but read by nothing, so `search.dbtest.ts`' comment that bumping it matters is wrong. That predates this slice.

**2026-09-25 — SLICE 63: WITH WORK SWITCHED OFF, THE INBOX STOPS NAMING TASKS (founder decision C33) — and C32 recorded beside it.**

**THE FOUNDER ANSWERED slice 62's two questions the same afternoon** — asked in plain words, both with the recommendation.
- **C32:** Settings → Time stays in the menu. Nothing built.
- **C33:** the inbox hides a task's name and link with Work off.

**THE REASON GIVEN FOR C32 WAS WRONG, and the review caught it.** While writing the question I read `noticeRequiredFor`, which answers "not required" when no staff notice is published. From that I told the founder that hiding the page would force "switch on, then write the notice", with a window where people track uninformed. There is no such window. Every tracking write (`startTimer`, `clockIn`, `createEntry`, `copyWeek`) first runs `ensureTimeDefaults`, which seeds and PUBLISHES a default notice, and a member tracking their OWN time must acknowledge it (`createEntry` for someone else does not ask — `forOther`). The real stake is only that members who track before the workspace publishes its own notice may acknowledge the default first and the workspace's text again later. The decision stands on that smaller reason, and the founder was told. **The lesson: a function read alone is not a flow. `noticeRequiredFor` was true, and the conclusion drawn from it was false, because its callers run a seed before it.**

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `resolveSubjects` (`src/notify/inbox.ts`), which resolves `/inbox`'s rows and `/home`'s inbox card, asks `accessibleCodes` — all four gates — instead of the permission gate alone. With Work switched off, a notification about a task keeps its row and its kind and loses its title and link, exactly as a task the member may not see already did; the backlog the link opened would have refused, and search already hid tasks in that state. A project's subject (a budget notification) is unaffected: `project:view` is core. The extra cost is the Work module's three gate reads, and they happen only when a row on the page IS a task and the member holds `work_item:view`. From the review: each scope is now resolved only when there are ids to look up, which pays that cost back on a page with no tasks, and `inboxGlance`'s two-leg `Promise.all` — `/home`'s card, the plain-read shape of AGENTS.md's trap — now runs in sequence. A new `inbox.dbtest.ts` case pins it (the task row loses its subject in the list and in the glance, the budget row keeps its project); a mutant reverting to the permission-only call turns it red ("expected { title: 'Work is off', … } to be null"). UI.md §3.1's Inbox row says so.

**THE REVIEW: 1 fresh read-only agent (correctness and authorization combined — proportionate to a one-call change), about 0.20M subagent tokens. No high. One MEDIUM, in the docs: C32's reason was wrong** (above) — corrected in OPEN_QUESTIONS and here, and the founder told. Fixed from the lows:
- `inboxGlance`'s two-leg `Promise.all` now runs in sequence.
- Each scope is resolved only when there are ids to look up.
- `work_item:view` is asked only when a row is a task.
- "board" → "backlog".

**THE FIX REVIEW: 1 fresh agent over the fix round, about 0.18M. No high, no medium.** Fixed:
- The corrected C32 still said `createEntry` demands the acknowledgement. It does not when a member writes for someone else (`forOther`), so it now reads "their own time".
- "Members acknowledge the default first" became "may": only members who track before the workspace publishes its own notice are affected.
- A task row's project is no longer loaded when no task subject can use it.

**DISPOSITIONED:**
- *(a)* Three more plain-read batches, `resolveScope` first. Now in item 4's list.
- *(b)* **A budget alert's LINK has the same dead end with Time switched off** (`/projects/KEY/money` refuses). The title is fine, because `project:view` is core. It is the same question as C33. **It was asked, and the founder answered straight away: DROP THE LINK** whenever the receiver cannot open the Money page — with Time off, or without the codes that page needs. That is `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` C34, built as its own slice rather than widening this one.

**2026-09-25 — SLICE 61: NO PERMISSION CHECK FANS OUT ON ONE TRANSACTION — the owed item 4, nine reads rather than eight, and a tripwire so the shape cannot come back.**

**FIRST, C31 WAS ASKED AND ANSWERED** (the block above): "Cancelled" for agreed work, the build held for the founder's model — recorded in `f102fb4`.

**WHAT SHIPPED.**

1. **Nine reads.** Item 4 named eight: the shell's `layout.tsx`, `inbox.ts`' `resolveSubjects`, `/members`, `/settings/roles`, `/files`, a project's Time and Money tabs, and `projectRollup`. The layout was the worst of them: one `isAuthorized` per gated nav code plus the unread count, ten reads at once on EVERY authed render. The ninth is **search's `allowedTypes`**, which item 4's grep could not see because it fanned out `requireAccess`, not `isAuthorized`: four codes at once, each up to four reads. A scan of every `Promise.all` block for any gate call found it. Each read now resolves ONCE (`authorizedCodes`) or awaits its checks in turn. One connection runs one statement at a time whatever the code says, so nothing got slower, and the layout now does two reads in sequence where it did ten at once.
2. **`resolvePermissions(tx, actor, codes) → { allowed, afterStepUp }`** (`src/authz/authorize.ts`); `authorizedCodes` returns its `allowed`. `afterStepUp` means exactly "a ✦ code refused now that a fresh factor would allow". So `/members` and `/settings/roles` offer their ✦ editors on `allowed ∪ afterStepUp`, which is the step-up the save demands. They used to read the raw `effectivePermissions` set, which an impersonating admin's view-only limit never touched. That was unreachable, because nothing sets `impersonated` today.
3. **`src/authz/authz-batches.test.ts`, a repo-wide tripwire.** It parses every product file and checks every call to a per-code check: `isAuthorized`, `authorize`, `requireAccess`, `hasAccess`, `flagEnabled`, `preferenceEnabled`, the scope helpers and `authorizePortal`. It fails on such a call if it is:
   - inside a `Promise.all`, `allSettled`, `race` or `any`;
   - inside a callback that an array method calls per element; or
   - not awaited or returned where it is made — and the same goes for any once-callback it sits in, such as `guarded`.

   A call inside a callback that opens its own transaction (`withTenant`, `withPlatform`, `withUser`, `withPortalRead`, `runGuarded`) is outside those rules. On the pre-slice tree it flags exactly the 15 calls in the nine files. On this tree it flags none, with no false alarm across 507 files. ONE resolution may still be one leg, which is the shape `listItems` and `getItemDetail` settled on. AGENTS.md's trap now says both things.
4. **`src/authz/authorized-codes.test.ts`.** `authorizedCodes` and `resolvePermissions` answer each code exactly as `isAuthorized` does, over the whole catalogue plus an unknown code, four holdings and six postures, and they read the roles once. Before this, that was a docblock's promise that nothing checked, and three more reads now rest on it.
5. **Search.** A dbtest that a module the tenant switched off drops its types while core types still answer. A pin that every `PERMISSION_BY_TYPE` entry is a catalogue `:view` code, because a typo would drop a type for everyone without a word: `requireAccess` refuses an unknown code silently. The old comment that said such a code "must surface" was false, and is corrected.

**WHY IT MATTERED MORE THAN A LATENT CRASH.** Both first-round reviewers made this point, and it is the strongest argument for the slice. `requireAccess` reads a flag, the tenant's entitlements and a preference before the permission, and all three read a missing answer as ON (`flagEnabled`'s `!flag`, `parseEntitlements(undefined)`, `preferenceEnabled`'s `!pref`). So a `requireAccess` leg whose read lost the race and came back `undefined` would have let a module the tenant had switched off into search. Only the permission read fails closed, by throwing.

**THE REVIEW: 2 fresh read-only agents (correctness; security and authorization), about 0.47M subagent tokens by their own usage reports. No high, no medium: every site answers as before for every actor.** Fixed:
- The first cut's exported `authorizedCodesFrom(actor, held, codes)` answered for whatever set it was handed, on a page that holds every member's roles (both lenses). Replaced by `resolvePermissions`, which reads its own.
- The ✦ editors read the raw set, past the impersonation limit (security). Now `afterStepUp`.
- The tripwire missed a hoisted array (`const checks = codes.map(…)`) and a check started early and awaited later (correctness). Rules 2 and 3 now catch both. `flagEnabled` and `preferenceEnabled` joined its list.
- Search's gates 1–3 had no test. That is item 5 above.
- "TWO STATEMENTS" and "ten statements at once" counted Prisma operations, not SQL. There is no `relationJoins`, so a nested select is several SELECTs. Now "reads".
- Smaller: two pages claimed "one resolution" where the page gate is a second; a comment probe sat outside any batch and could never fail; "600-odd files" (it is 507); a shadowed `prefs`; a stale "batched … two more codes".

**One reviewer broke its read-only rule.** It wrote and ran a node script from its scratchpad. The script failed at once (it could not load `typescript`) and changed nothing. Recorded because the rule exists to protect the founder's machine.

**THE FIX REVIEW: 1 fresh read-only agent over the whole diff, about 0.28M subagent tokens. No high, no medium; 5 low, 2 nits.** Fixed:
- AGENTS.md's new sentence said "a permission check is never a leg", over code that runs one `resolvePermissions` as a leg. It also did not say that one resolution answers the permission gate only, so it never replaces `requireAccess` where the module gates matter. Reworded.
- The tripwire walked through a once-callback without asking whether the callback's own call was awaited, so `const gate = guarded(async () => requireAccess(…))` passed. Rule 3 now covers each such host, with a self-test, and `Array.from` joined the per-element list.
- A docblock sentence said an opener's callback was exempt from all three rules, while the code scans inside it.
- Smaller: the unknown-code log's prefix, and the inbox comment's reach.

**Dispositioned:**
- Items 5 and 6 of the next-session block: the rail's module gates, and the impersonation list.
- `requireAccess` answers a MISSING tenant row with the everything-on default, where `resolvePortalModuleGates` fails closed. Not changed here, for three reasons:
  - The row is always visible to a member principal (`tenant_self_select`), so it only guards an invariant violation.
  - Gates 1 and 3 cannot fail closed on a missing row at all, because an absent row IS "enabled".
  - Which error to raise is a decision of its own.

**2026-09-24 — SLICE 59: C30, MEMBER ACCOUNT RECOVERY — all five parts, and a fresh review that broke the first cut's answer to the pre-account takeover.**

**WHAT SHIPPED.**

1. **A member can reset a forgotten password** — `/reset-password` (an address, one answer for every address) and `/reset-password/[token]` (a new password twice; then signed in, or "saved — sign in" for a member with a second factor). The member plane's `/request-password-reset` and `/reset-password` came OFF `src/auth/closed-endpoints.ts` deliberately, with everything slice 58 said a re-opened reset owed: the mail after the response (`deliverMemberReset`), a one-second floor on the route (`isMemberFlooredRequest`), the link naming our screen, the token stored as `pwreset#<sha256>` through a `storeIdentifier` override for that prefix ONLY (`src/auth/reset-identifier.ts` — never `reset-password:<hash>`, which the library's plain fallback would let a reader of the table redeem), and a re-read before sending. **A console principal is declined** on request, burned on redemption (`refuseResetOfConsolePrincipal`, any token shape, body or query) and shown the dead-link page: one `account` row serves both planes. A completed reset kills every other reset link and any two-factor challenge in flight, keeps trusted devices and the factor, and **confirms the address** (the link was read in that mailbox). The library's GET callback `/reset-password/:token` stays refused.
2. **An unconfirmed member who signs in with the right password is mailed a fresh link** (`sendOnSignIn`), and `/login` says so (`login.unconfirmed`); the link keeps the `next` of the `/login` page it came from (`nextOf`, from the referrer — an invitee whose first link lapsed would otherwise land on an empty dashboard). The 403-vs-401 difference this needs is now kept ON PURPOSE (SECURITY T6).
3. **Both mails are capped at three an hour per RECIPIENT** in a ledger of their own, `auth_mail` (migration `20260924120000_auth_mail`, AUTH class, DDL only): attempts not surviving links, under the user row's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` lock on the database clock with a link-scaled lock wait, pruned per person, a failed send giving its slot back. Counted there because neither mail can be counted where it lives: a confirmation link is a JWT, and a reset link shares `verification` with two-factor challenges and trusted devices under the same user id.
4. **Confirming an address takes the link AND the account's password, and then signs in** (`confirmMemberEmail`, `src/auth/member-screens.ts`; the page's server action `confirmEmailAction`, limited per network like sign-in). Better Auth's own `/verify-email` is refused on the member plane now too — it confirmed on the link alone, on a bare GET a mail scanner performs — and slice 58's change-email-link refusal went with it (`isSignUpLink` stays, failing closed, for the page's holder). The mailed link is the confirmation PAGE, which changes nothing on GET. `autoSignInAfterVerification` is off as belt and braces.
5. **An operator script for a forgotten console password**, `scripts/reset-ops-password.ts` (+ `src/jobs/reset-ops-password*.ts`): the password from stdin only (`--password` refused), a confirmed SUPERADMIN only, 12–128 characters, one `withPlatform` system job that sets the credential, ends every session on both planes, cancels challenges and reset links, leaves the factor and trusted devices, and writes `platform.password_changed` `{via: "operator"}` with SYSTEM as actor; `--dry-run` writes nothing but the seam's own read row. `create-test-member.ts` now refuses a console principal. RUNBOOK §8 has the procedure.

**Also:** the member AND platform instances state `minPasswordLength: 12` (`src/auth/recovery-policy.ts`) — the forms always asked for twelve over a service that took eight, and one credential row serves both planes; `/login` split into a server page and a client form that never shows the library's English and survives a network failure; `/signup` the same, with its done state announced; the invite page gained a sign-in door; `useFocusHeadingOnChange` moved to `src/components/use-focus-heading.ts`; `sweep-dbtests` now also collects the DB suite's bare users (`DBTEST_USER_PREFIXES`) and the platform audit rows naming them; five new visual stops.

**THE ORCHESTRATION, recorded because it is the first slice built this way:** a six-reader recon workflow (about 1.3M subagent tokens) mapped Better Auth's reset, verification and two-factor internals, the DB plumbing, the surfaces, the platform plane and the written record BEFORE any design; the core auth was written in the main session, and the screens + copy, the operator script and the e2e harness by three agents on disjoint files in parallel (about 0.7M). The recon is what found the two facts the design turned on: that a hashed prefix must never be `reset-password:` (the plain fallback), and that the library's `/verify-email` confirms on a mail scanner's GET.

**THE REVIEW: 6 read-only lenses (security, library truth + concurrency, UI/i18n/a11y, tests, the record, blast radius), severity-scaled verification — 17 agents, about 2.8M subagent tokens. 32 findings: 21 survived, 11 refuted. ALL 21 FIXED or dispositioned.** The one that mattered, found independently by two lenses (medium): **the first cut's answer to the pre-account takeover did not hold for its likeliest victim.** It had turned auto-sign-in off and put a Confirm button behind the mailed link with "only confirm if you created this account". But an owner who signs up at an address a stranger already registered gets the library's silent stand-in answer and NO mail — while the stranger, by signing in (this slice's own `sendOnSignIn`), keeps a fresh link in the owner's inbox that reads exactly like the owner's own. The owner presses it in good faith, the stranger's password goes live, the stranger enrols a factor, and the owner's reset ends at a code screen. **Fixed by making confirmation prove both halves** (item 4): the stranger lacks the mailbox and the owner lacks the stranger's password, so neither can confirm a pre-registration; the owner's password is refused with a link to "Choose a new password", which replaces the stranger's. The residual lockout the first cut had recorded is gone with it. **And the rest, fixed:** the console guard filtered tokens by shape while the library consumes any string (a planted odd-shaped link slipped past); the operator job's `FOR UPDATE` held a racing sign-in's session insert until after its purge (now `NO KEY UPDATE`, bounded, the claim narrowed); a long address pushed the login callout sideways on a phone; `/signup` hung on a network failure, announced nothing and showed library English; a sign-in's link dropped `next`; the ledger's lock wait was not link-scaled; the console's own `/change-password` still took eight characters for the shared credential; seven test gaps (each stored form of a console link alone — the old test could not fail for the plain form — the query-string token, the 12-character floor, a failed confirmation send's slot, and more); no sweep for the DB suite's bare users; and the record (AGENTS counts, DATA_MODEL's "No RLS" in two rows, the schema comment, a two-factor claim). **Dispositioned:** the name a stranger typed at sign-up survives the owner's reset (RUNBOOK §8 tells the operator to say so; a memberless account cannot edit its name yet); the applied migration's header overstates which two-factor sign-ins leave rows (Prisma checksums an applied migration, so it is corrected in `mail-budget.ts` instead); `onExistingUserSignUp` stays unconfigured (the password-gated confirmation removed the reason to mail an existing address, and it would be another unauthenticated mail trigger).

**THE FIX REVIEW: 3 fresh lenses over the fix round, same scaled verification — 7 agents, about 1.1M subagent tokens. 12 findings, 10 survived, 2 refuted — ALL LOW, and nothing defeated a control.** Fixed: the confirmation action's limiter had no test (now pinned by a source scan that fails if `allowStrict` stops preceding the password check — mutation-checked); the e2e spec's header and four docblocks still described the first cut; `DBTEST_USER_PREFIXES` missed two sign-up-made users (`auth-`, `e2e-member-`) and its recipe could not find them; the new sweep left the operator suite's audit rows; this PLAN entry did not exist yet.

**GATES (local, final tree).** typecheck ✅ · ESLint `src e2e scripts --max-warnings 0` → 0 ✅ · unit **85 files / 1399 passed / 1 skipped** ✅ (HEAD had 83 / 1352: `reset-ops-password.test.ts` and `confirm-action-guard.test.ts` are new) · `pnpm exec next build --webpack` ✅, on the fix round's tree — what changed after it is comments, one unit test and the e2e sweep · **full `test:db` 51 files / 798 passed, `EXIT=0` read from the log itself** ✅ (HEAD's CI had 49 / 752: `member-recovery.dbtest.ts` and `reset-ops-password.dbtest.ts` are new) · `sweep-dbtests`' new bare-user pass is typechecked and NOT run against the dev database, which holds nothing for it to take · **mutation-checked, twenty-three, each turning the dbtest that names it red** — the storage override, the reset re-read's console check and its address check, the redemption guard unwired, its plain-form lookup, its shape filter restored, its query-string branch, the reset's challenge purge and its address confirmation, the hourly cap, the ledger's row lock, prune and failed-send release, the confirmation's password check, `/verify-email` re-opened, the holder's sign-up-link, HS256, expiry and console checks, `sendOnSignIn`, both instances' 12-character floors, the referrer fallback — plus the action's limiter scan. **Browser (own port 3457, own webpack build):** `member-recovery.spec.ts` **3 passed**; the visual walk **6 passed in 13.8 min, 61 stops / 244 shots** measured from the run's own files, the five new stops looked at in both themes at both widths. The dev database was checked afterwards: no `e2e-` tenant and no fixture user left.

**2026-09-24 — SLICE 58: THE MEMBER AND PLATFORM PLANES' MAIL ENDPOINTS — closed rather than hardened, and a fresh review that found the first cut's headline control recognisable half the time.**

**THE CALL, and why it is not what the previous next-session block said.** That block (written at the end of slice 57) said to harden the two planes' reset endpoints with the portal's shapes — the after-response send, the hashed tokens, the per-recipient cap — keying the hashing on the `reset-password:` prefix so the two-factor challenges in the same table were untouched. A five-reader recon found three things that block assumed away: **neither plane has a reset screen, and the link the library mailed led nowhere a person could use**, so hardening would have been careful delivery of a dead link; **the portal's cap and purges count and delete by `value` = the principal's id**, which on the shared `verification` table also matches two-factor challenges and trusted devices; and **the platform instance answered for every user in the shared table**, mailing "reset your Fortleva platform password" to members. The project's own rule is "enable nothing unused", so the endpoints are refused instead — and a member forgot-password flow becomes a product item with the design already worked out (C30).

**WHAT SHIPPED.**

1. **`src/auth/closed-endpoints.ts`** — both instances refuse, in `hooks.before` and before their limiter, `/request-password-reset`, `/reset-password` and `/reset-password/:token`, with one 404 for every address. The member plane also refuses `/send-verification-email` (no caller: sign-up sends its own mail; it mailed any unverified user on a stranger's say-so and 500'd for exactly those addresses with no transport) and `/change-email` (no screen, and its confirmation callback was named with a key 1.6.26 does not read, so the old address was never told — the `user.changeEmail` block is gone too). **The platform plane also refuses `/verify-email`**: the two instances share `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, emailed links are JWTs with no plane claim, so the console accepted member-signed links — and for a change-email link it minted a PLATFORM session and rewrote the address with no password. Keyed on `ctx.path`, the endpoint's declared path, which `disabledPaths` cannot express for the token route and does not apply to `auth.api.*`. `sendResetPassword` is removed from both instances; `revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` and `onPasswordReset` stay, so re-opening reset can never forget them — and the list, not the missing config, is the control: `/reset-password` consumes any `reset-password:` row whether or not reset is configured.
2. **Member sign-up gives every address the same answer** (`src/auth/sign-up-answer.ts`). Every successful sign-up answers `{token: null, user: null}`; input the database would refuse is refused before the library branches; the route holds `/sign-up/email` to a one-second floor (`response-floor.ts`, generalised); the verification mail goes after the response (`src/auth/after-response.ts`, extracted from `portal.ts` so both planes share one copy).
3. **The member plane's `/verify-email` refuses a change-email LINK** (review finding). It stays open for sign-up, but for a link carrying `updateTo` it creates a session for the named user with no password and no factor — and with `/change-email` refused, the only such link that can arrive is one signed by whoever holds the secret.
4. **THE RECORD, corrected where it was dangerous.** `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is the key Better Auth encrypts every TOTP secret and backup code under — not `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — and RUNBOOK told the operator that rotating it "signs everyone out; no data loss". Replacing it strands every factor, the sole operator's included. RUNBOOK §5 now says not to replace it as hygiene, never to set `BETTER_AUTH_SECRETS` (it overrides the portal's own secret too), and what to do when it has LEAKED; §8 signs everyone out by deleting rows as `app_runtime`, trusted devices included, and gives the operator's remedy for a member stuck before verifying. The same false claim sat in SECURITY.md (six places, one of them a planned re-encryption job that would have bricked every factor), DATA_MODEL, the schema comment and `field-encryption.ts`. All corrected.

**THE REVIEW: 5 read-only lenses (security, library claims, tests, the record, blast radius), 2 refuters for high, 1 for medium, 1 batch per lens for low — 31 agents, about 3.2M subagent tokens. 35 findings, 33 survived, 2 refuted, collapsing to about 20 distinct items.** The two that mattered most were both about the headline control:

- **The stand-in's uuid v7 was still recognisable** (high, both refuters upheld). Prisma's generator seeds its sequence so the hex character after the version digit is always 0–7; ours left it random, so half of all stand-ins proved the address belonged to a member. The fix is not a better mimic — mimicking another library's id layout is the same mistake as counting its queries — so the answer now names nobody, and `src/lib/uuid-v7.ts` is deleted.
- **Hostile input was a second oracle** (high, rated medium by one refuter). A NUL byte in the name or a non-string `locale` reached the INSERT on the new-address branch only: 422 there, 200 for a registered address, nothing written or mailed. Refused before the branch now, and the dbtest sends each hostile input to both kinds of address side by side.

**AND THE REST, fixed:** a leaked secret had no procedure, and the new sign-out advice did not contain one (a forged change-email link was a session for any member) → the link refusal and RUNBOOK §5's leaked-secret steps; `BETTER_AUTH_SECRETS` would silently re-unify the portal's secret; the sign-out left 30-day trusted devices standing and named no role under FORCE RLS; SECURITY.md's six TOTP claims; `after-response.ts` justified a lost mail with "the person asks again", which on the member plane they cannot → the dead end is stated, RUNBOOK §8 has the operator's remedy, C30 owns the fix; the stated reason for not using `disabledPaths` was wrong and "does no work at all" overstated; comments implied an unconfigured feature is unmounted; DATA_MODEL's attempt-counter value and sweep; the platform comment's "the console still demands the factor" (not of a SUPERADMIN who has not enrolled); T6 credited the dbtest with pinning the duration; assertions that could never fail and a title the test never exercised; the fixture registered its user after creating it and used a password printed in this public repository; PLAN §0 still listed the endpoints as next. **One claim in a finding was false and is not acted on:** that moving the mail off the response made a transport failure newly silent — the library swallowed it before too.

**DISPOSITIONED, three:** *(a)* **a two-request oracle remains** — sign an address up with your own password, then sign in with it: 403 "not verified" if it was new, 401 if not. It creates an account for the address and mails its owner, so it is neither silent nor cheap, and closing it means sign-in lying to every member who has not clicked their link; stated in T6 and `sign-up-answer.ts`, and it belongs to C30. *(b)* The verification mail is proven "not awaited" on `afterResponse`'s fallback branch only — a dbtest runs outside any request — the same limit slice 57 recorded for the portal. *(c)* The source-scan tripwires can be defeated by reformatting; they are tripwires, and the dbtests prove the wiring.

**THE FIX REVIEW: 3 fresh lenses over the fix round, the same scaled verification — 15 agents, about 1.7M subagent tokens. 18 findings, 16 survived, 2 refuted. It found BOTH of the first round's high fixes defeatable:**

- **The input check covered the name only**, and a lone UTF-16 surrogate in `callbackURL` — which `encodeURIComponent` throws on AFTER the user row is written — was still a 500-for-new, 200-for-registered oracle (both refuters upheld). Every string field must now be well-formed, tested with the same `encodeURIComponent` the library runs.
- **The change-email link check failed OPEN.** A payload beginning with a UTF-8 byte-order mark made our decode throw — and "let the library refuse what we cannot read" let it through — while jose strips the mark and verifies. **Measured, not argued:** with the check put back to fail-open, a link signed with the real secret and prefixed with the mark rewrote the member's address and minted a session. It fails closed now: only a token that reads as a plain sign-up link passes.

**Also fixed:** the stranger's sign-up was called a "nuisance" in C30 when it is a pre-account takeover — the owner clicks the stranger's link and is signed in to the stranger's password — restated in C30, T6 and RUNBOOK §8, with a remedy option in C30; RUNBOOK §8's `NOT EXISTS (member)` guard is inert under FORCE RLS as `app_runtime` (it sees no `member` rows at all), and the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` foreign key is the real guard, now said; the leaked-secret steps did not say every outstanding sign-up link dies with the secret; `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` had no custody line; the answer was one shared mutable object; comments overstated which fields reach the INSERT, and one test case pins the allowlist rather than an oracle (now titled so); a dozen sign-ups from one "unknown" IP that a provisioned limiter would throttle (each request now has its own documentation-range address); four more "configuring X mounts Y" sentences; the two edited dbtests still used a published literal password, and `auth-audit`'s cleanup skipped the user when provisioning failed; the new refusal was English shown verbatim → `signup.invalidInput` in both catalogues, the page mapping the code, a source check keeping them in step. **Dispositioned:** two simultaneous sign-ups of one new address — the INSERT race's loser answers 422 — added to the stated residuals.

**AND A THIRD PASS over round three: 2 lenses, 9 agents, about 1.0M subagent tokens. 13 findings, 11 survived, 2 refuted — and for the first time in this slice, NOTHING defeated the code.** The security lens tried both fixes again (every step after sign-up's branch point, every decoder difference between Node and jose) and came back with nothing above low. What it did find was the record, and one of them was high: **RUNBOOK §8's stranger-sign-up remedy could not match the case it was prescribed for** — once the owner clicks the stranger's link the account is confirmed, `AND NOT email_verified` deletes nothing, and the bullet never said to read the count (both refuters upheld). §8 now has a statement for each case, both with the count to expect; the `ON DELETE RESTRICT` key still refuses either for an account with a membership. **Also fixed:** the leaked-secret steps now review accounts made or confirmed while the secret was out, and say that the secret plus a database read forges every live session's cookie (which SECURITY §3.3's summary had understated); C30's "a second factor stops that" was backwards (only the stranger can enrol one) and its option (d) needs (a) beside it; the refusal copy said "under 200" and "special characters", and neither was the rule; the BOM test had no proof in itself that its hand-made signature verifies — `verifyJWT` now checks it first; `portal.dbtest.ts`, in this diff, still created credentials with literal passwords; and PLAN had not recorded round three's evidence or C30's (d). One pre-existing thing is recorded rather than fixed: `portal.dbtest.ts` provisions its tenant as `e2e-portal-…`, the browser harness's age-swept prefix, which AGENTS.md says a dbtest must not use. **And because operators act on it, one more fresh agent checked only the rewritten RUNBOOK and C30 text against the schema, the migrations and the library:** every table, column, grant, policy and foreign key held; it found the leaked-secret step (4) pointing at the statement that skips confirmed accounts, and asking a membership question `app_runtime` cannot see (medium), plus a case-sensitive address match, a C30 row claiming §8 covers a forgotten password, and "any other role" where only the table owner matches zero rows (low). All fixed.

**C30 WAS SETTLED THE SAME EVENING, with the recommendation** ("I go with your recommendations"), so it heads the next-session block above.

**A HARNESS EVENT, recorded because it is unexplained.** The full `test:db` over the round-one tree came back **47 passed, 1 failed, 1 worker exited unexpectedly — and the background-task notification said "exit code 0" over a log whose own last lines said `EXIT=1`**, the exact trap AGENTS.md describes. The failure was `projects.dbtest.ts` on the 5000 ms interactive-transaction budget (7.2 s; untouched code, while 31 review agents were running). The worker that died was not named and 4 tests went unreported; the three 4-test files that could be it, and `projects.dbtest.ts`, then passed 25/25 on the same tree.

**GATES (local, final tree).** typecheck ✅ · ESLint `src e2e scripts --max-warnings 0` → 0 ✅ · unit **83 files / 1352 passed / 1 skipped** ✅ (HEAD had 81 / 1287: `closed-endpoints.test.ts` and `sign-up-answer.test.ts` are new, the member route's floor wiring and matcher joined `response-floor.test.ts`) · `pnpm build` ✅ · **full `test:db` 49 files / 752 passed, `EXIT=0` read from the log itself** ✅ — CI's 733 plus `plane-endpoints.dbtest.ts`'s 19, with no worker crash this time; the round-one run's failure and crash above did not recur. **Mutation-checked, thirteen, each turning the dbtest that names it red:** unwiring the refusal on the member instance, and on the platform instance; dropping the constant sign-up answer; dropping the input check; dropping the change-email link refusal; narrowing it to `requestType` (the legacy `updateTo`-only link then passes); putting it back to FAIL-OPEN (the BOM-signed link then rewrote the member's address — the state assertion, not the status, is what caught it); dropping the well-formedness check; awaiting the verification mail; reopening the console's `/verify-email`; reopening `/reset-password/:token`; reopening `/change-email`; reopening the member's `/send-verification-email`. **Not run locally, on purpose:** the browser harness. **2026-09-24 — SLICE 57: THE PORTAL'S PASSWORD RESET — two screens, and a fresh review that found the first cut of the controls behind them wrong in four ways.**

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `/portal/reset-password` (an address, and one confirmation for every address) and `/portal/reset-password/[token]` (a new password twice, over the address it is for; then signed in and on `/portal`). A "Forgot your password? Choose a new one" link in the sign-in form's footer. Both public through `src/proxy.ts` — an exact entry for the bare path and a segment-anchored prefix for the token, exactly the invitation's shape — and neither has a Server Action: both forms call the portal auth API from the browser, so the exemption opens a render and nothing else. Three proxy cases, three visual stops (`portal-reset-request`, `portal-reset` over a seeded link, `portal-reset-unavailable`), and one e2e test in the `portal-invite.spec.ts` serial chain that drives the whole loop from the sign-in form's link, through the mailed URL as sent, to `/portal` and back to the dead-link state.

**THE SCREENS WERE THE SMALL PART. The endpoints behind them had been live since the portal instance was mounted on 2026-09-20, and a screen would have advertised every defect in them:**

1. **THE RESPONSE TIME SAID WHO WAS A CLIENT.** Better Auth awaits `sendResetPassword`, so an ACTIVE contact's request waited for a mail-transport round trip and an unknown address's did not — and in a production build with no transport `send()` threw, which the library logged and swallowed *after* the delay. The constant BODY was defeated by a stopwatch. **Fixed twice over:** the decision and the send now run after the response (`deliverPortalReset` through Next's `after()`), and the route holds `/request-password-reset` to a **one-second response floor** (`src/auth/response-floor.ts`), because the library's found and not-found branches still issue different statements. The first cut claimed, here and in a comment, that what remained was "one INSERT against one SELECT"; the review counted, and the hashing below had made the gap WIDER. A floor does not depend on counting anybody's queries.
2. **LIVE RESET LINKS SAT IN `contact_verification` VERBATIM**, while `DATA_MODEL.md` described the table as holding "(hashes)". `verification.storeIdentifier: "hashed"` — the invitation's rule, "raw tokens never touch the database", applied to the other token.
3. **A PAUSED CONTACT'S LIVE LINK COULD TAKE THE SUSPENDED CREDENTIAL BACK** if the pause's purge ever missed it — and the purge's first version matched zero rows. `/reset-password` takes the UPDATE branch on an existing credential, which the credential trigger (BEFORE INSERT) never sees. A `hooks.before` now burns **every** reset row of a contact who is not ACTIVE and lets the library refuse with its own `INVALID_TOKEN`, byte-identical to an expired link.
4. **A PORTAL RESET WROTE NO AUDIT ROW.** The instance had no `onPasswordReset`, and the shared `passwordResetHookFor` handed its sink an id where the portal sink finds its tenant on the USER row. It passes the user now: `auth.password_changed` `{via: "reset"}`, the CONTACT as actor.
5. **NOTHING BOUNDED THE MAIL.** **3 mails per contact per hour, counted in Postgres and keyed on the RECIPIENT** (`RESET_MAILS_PER_HOUR`) — SECURITY.md §4's "3 / h per email", written in Phase 0 and never built. Counted by CREATION ORDER, so a burst of overlapping requests mails exactly the first three. A declined request's row is deleted, so a flood aimed at a paused address grows nothing.
6. **`/send-verification-email` MAILED THE CLIENT LIST** — found while reading the library for this slice, the same class by a second door. It is unauthenticated and mailed any UNVERIFIED contact, i.e. every one an agency had merely recorded, a link to a `/verify-email` that fails on this plane by design; with no transport, the rethrown failure made those addresses answer 500. The portal's `sendVerificationEmail` now sends nothing.

**AND THREE MORE THINGS THE FLOW NOW DOES.** A successful reset **kills every other link** the contact was sent. **Changing a contact's address kills every link mailed to the old one** (`updateContact`) — without it the old mailbox could open its link, read the NEW address off the page, set the password and be signed in. And the mailed link is **built on the server** (`portalResetUrl`), so no caller-supplied `redirectTo` reaches a mail.

**THE REVIEW: 6 read-only lenses (security, correctness, library claims, tests, UI/i18n, the record), verification scaled to severity — 2 refuters for high, 1 for medium, 1 batch per lens for low — 27 agents, about 3.0M subagent tokens against 16.6M for slice 56's. 42 findings, 38 survived, which collapse to 22 distinct items; 4 refuted. 21 FIXED, 1 DISPOSITIONED.** The fixes got a second, smaller fresh pass of their own before the commit; its result closes this entry.

**WHAT IT CAUGHT THAT MATTERED — four of the first cut's own controls were wrong:**

- **The timing fix was not a fix** (three lenses independently): the claim above, and the widened gap. → the response floor.
- **The mail was a bare `void promise`** on a production target (Vercel, ARC-01) where the function may be frozen the moment the response goes, and ARC-21 rejects "fire-and-forget from the request" BY NAME. → `after()`. **The outbox was considered and rejected on purpose:** it would hold the raw token in `email_outbox.params` until the drain ran, undoing the hashing. `after()` is not durable either, which ARC-21 also says; a person whose link never arrives asks again.
- **A link survived a change of address**, and would have shown the new address to the old mailbox. → the purge in `updateContact`, with a dbtest.
- **`referrer: "no-referrer"`, which I had put on both token pages, did harm and no good** (three lenses): under it a browser sends `Origin: null` on a non-CORS POST — a native form submission before hydration — and Next refuses that Server Action, so the INVITATION form would have failed for anybody who pressed it before the page's script loaded; while the token reaches our access logs on the page's own GET regardless. → removed from both.

**AND THE REST, all fixed:** the burn missed rows stored in the pre-hashing plain form (lookup falls back to them) → burn by contact, with a test; both forms — and the sign-in form they copied — hung disabled forever on a network failure, because the auth client THROWS rather than returning `{ error }` without `catchAllError`; the cap raced itself into declining a whole burst; the replaced views (sent, saved, dead link) were silent to a screen reader with focus dropped on `<body>` → a live region and focus to the new heading; "a link is on its way" was untrue for a fourth request → the copy states the cap; a long address pushed a phone-width page sideways → `wrap-anywhere` on `AuthShell`'s description (the invitation page had the same flaw); the e2e rebuilt the reset URL from a path instead of opening the mailed one; SECURITY.md said the off-response-path send was pinned and mutation-checked when nothing pinned it → a transport that never answers now does, and the mutation was run; SECURITY.md and AUTHZ §8 still said the credential trigger is proven through the real endpoints, which this slice's own guard now stops short of → pointed at the direct test; the session table called 2 days the shortest of three planes (the platform's is 8 h — and its row said 12 h / 7 days, now corrected from `platform.ts`); comments stating the plain identifier shape, a wrong SECURITY section number, "SMTP" where no SMTP exists, `AuthShell`'s "the only one that takes a write", AUTHZ's "THIRD point", DATA_MODEL's "first invite token".

**THE ONE DISPOSITIONED, and it is an OPEN ITEM, not a scope note: the MEMBER and PLATFORM planes' reset endpoints have three of the defects this slice fixed on the portal.** Both instances configure `sendResetPassword`, so `/request-password-reset` and `/reset-password` are mounted and answer anyone with curl — send awaited (the timing oracle), tokens verbatim in `verification`, no per-recipient cap — and neither plane has a screen, which is not a control. The member plane's `/send-verification-email` belongs to the same item (the next-session block has it). Not fixed here because it is two other planes, and hashing the member `verification` table touches every flow that shares it (two-factor challenges among them), which is a slice with its own gates and review. The platform plane is the most privileged of the three, so it should come first. Recorded in SECURITY.md §4's reset row too.

**TWO THINGS OUTSIDE THE SLICE'S OWN FILES.** *(a)* **`src/lib/safe-next.ts` was a BINARY FILE to git** — raw NUL and DEL bytes inside its regex, the Write-tool JSON-escape trap in memory, so every diff of the product's one redirect guard showed as `- -` and no reviewer has ever seen one. Rewritten as `/[\x00-\x20\x7f]/` — the same character class, in characters a diff can show. *(b)* AGENTS.md's screenshot count, measured: see the gates.

**THE FIX REVIEW: 3 fresh lenses over the fix delta (security + correctness, UI + tests, the record), same severity-scaled verification — 10 agents, about 1.3M subagent tokens. 14 findings survived, 0 refuted, 12 distinct, ALL FIXED.** None was high. The ones worth remembering: *(a)* **a reset request could still race an address change** — Better Auth reads the contact when the request arrives, and a row written after `updateContact`'s purge would have been mailed to the old address — so the delivery now re-reads the contact and sends only to the SAME address of a still-ACTIVE contact; the residual is a member's own open transaction. *(b)* **A failed send left its row live and counted against the cap**, so three transport failures would have locked a person out of reset for the hour — the opposite of the "they simply ask again" that justifies `after()` over the outbox. A failed send deletes its row now. *(c)* **Half of one of my new tests could not fail** — a THROWING transport, which the library swallows whether or not the send is awaited — so it is gone, with a note saying why. *(d)* **The floor's WIRING was untested** (unwiring it in `route.ts` failed nothing) — a source check pins it now, mutation-checked. *(e)* **The open item blamed the member and platform `/request-password-reset` for a 500 they cannot produce** — the library swallows that failure — while the real 500 is the member plane's `/send-verification-email`, which the item now names. *(f)* "We could not reach the server" was untrue of a lost response, and on the reset form sent the person to a spent link over a saved password; the copy now says the password may already be saved and to try signing in. Also: a fallback from `after()` that was silent in every case (it logs now unless the cause is being outside a request — no test can tell the two paths apart, which is stated rather than hidden), the schema's own model comment still describing plain identifiers and invite tokens, a claimed production measurement that nobody took, a stale test comment, the member session row's unenforced 30-day ceiling, and Swedish that read "to where" instead of "to that address".

**AND A THIRD PASS over the second round of fixes: 2 lenses, 10 agents, about 0.8M subagent tokens, 8 findings, all low, 0 refuted, ALL FIXED.** The two that were not wording: a failure removing an unsent row inside the send's own `catch` would have REPLACED the transport error it was cleaning up after (the cleanup is caught and logged separately now); and the re-read's STATUS half was untested — the address race pinned only its other half, and the early non-ACTIVE check it superseded had quietly become impossible for any test to catch, which made one of my sixteen mutations a claim rather than a check. It has its own test and mutation now. The rest: two comments still crediting the address purge alone for what now takes the purge AND the re-read, a decline count one short, the open item's "every defect" (the other planes' resets ARE audited), the schema calling a chosen omission "structural", and three new files that were untracked rather than intent-to-added — so a reviewer reading only `git diff` would have missed `response-floor.ts` (the first review predates it; the second was pointed at it by name).

**GATES (local, final tree).** typecheck ✅ · ESLint `src e2e scripts --max-warnings 0` → 0 ✅ · unit **81 files / 1287 passed / 1 skipped** ✅ (+1 file and +12 over HEAD's 80 / 1275: three proxy cases, eight for the floor's behaviour, one for its wiring) · `pnpm build` ✅ (through the harness's own build, three times), both routes dynamic (ƒ) · `test:db` over every file the slice touches — `portal.dbtest.ts` **25**, `contact-access.dbtest.ts` **28**, `clients.dbtest.ts` **10**, `portal-identity.dbtest.ts` **24** — **87 passed** ✅. **Mutation-checked, seventeen in all, each turning the test that names it red:** dropping the hashing, the redemption guard, the user in the audit hook, the post-reset purge, the cap, or the expiry check; dropping the delivery's STATUS re-read (the early non-ACTIVE decline it replaced as the authority can no longer be caught by any test, which is why the mutation moved to the re-read); reverting `setContactPortalAccess`'s purge to its old address-keyed shape; awaiting the delivery; counting the cap without creation order; burning by the hashed identifier alone; dropping the address-change purge; restoring the verification mail; unwiring the floor from the route; dropping the delivery's ADDRESS re-read; keeping a failed send's row; and building the mail's link on Better Auth's callback instead of the screen. Browser (own port, 3457): before the fixes, `portal-invite.spec.ts` + `visual.spec.ts`, **9 passed, 12.4 min**, all four walks over **56 stops / 224 shots**, a count measured from the run's own files (AGENTS.md said 51 / 204, slice 56 below says 54 / 216, HEAD had 53) — the three new stops looked at in both themes at both widths; after each round of fixes, `portal-invite.spec.ts` **3 passed** through a fresh production build, the reset loop 6.1 s with the one-second floor in it. The visual walk was not re-run after the fixes: they change no layout except `wrap-anywhere` on `AuthShell`'s description, which moves nothing that fits.

**2026-09-23 — SLICE 56: THE PORTAL INVITE FLOW, SURFACES (commit 2 of 2) — the portal has a door, a doorbell and a key, and the review found that the lock had no pins in it.**

**WHAT SHIPPED, against the four things the brief owed.**

1. **`/portal/invite/[token]`** — `page.tsx` + `accept-form.tsx` + `actions.ts`. A password and a confirmation over the AGENCY's name, the contact's own name and the address it was sent to (decision 1). Both fields controlled, because React 19 resets a `<form action>`. The action signs the contact in afterwards through `portalAuth.api.signInEmail` — `acceptContactInvite` deliberately mints no session — and `redirect`s to `/portal`; if that sign-in fails, the password is still set and they go to the sign-in form instead, which is one of the reasons that form had to exist.
2. **`PORTAL_INVITE_PREFIX` in `src/proxy.ts`** — a `startsWith`, not a `PUBLIC_PATHS` entry, because the token is a path segment and `PUBLIC_PATHS.has()` could only ever exempt the bare path. Below the host/plane branches, so the ops host still sweeps it under `/ops`. Three cases in `proxy.test.ts`: it passes, `/portal/invitations` and `/portal/invite` do not, and the ops host redirects. The docblock that promised the path was withheld is rewritten.
3. **A RATE LIMIT THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS**, which took more than a bucket — see the next block.
4. **THE CONTACTS TAB'S FIVE VERBS**, offered strictly by `portalStatus` so no control is drawn that the service would refuse, and the add-contact form's **"invite this person to the portal" tick** (decision 3's "it is both in the end").

**AND THE e2e MAKES THE CLAIM NO dbtest CAN** (`e2e/portal-invite.spec.ts`, two tests, `mode: "serial"`): a member adds a person with the tick, the row goes INVITED, the raw token is read out of `.dev-outbox`, an empty browser context opens the link, sets a password and lands on `/portal` — then the consumed token and a token that never existed are asserted to render **byte-identical** pages, which is decision 2 as a test rather than as a comment. The second test ends the access and deletes the record through the real row menu, which is the only coverage those two verbs have.

**SIX THINGS THE BRIEF DID NOT ASK FOR. Three are judgement calls the founder may want to reverse; three are defects the slice could not ship around.**

1. **`/portal/login` IS A REAL FORM.** Its own docblock said it was locked "because there is no invite flow yet"; both halves have now shipped. Without it the invitation was a ONE-SHOT door — `contact_session` lasts two days and an ACTIVE contact cannot be re-invited — and it is the only destination the acceptance page's dead-end state can offer, which `PageState` requires. Email + password, one message for every failure (the instance checks admission in a `session.create` hook precisely so a refusal cannot be used to ask whether an address belongs to a contact), no sign-up link, no second factor, no reset link yet.
2. **THE MAILER MAY WRITE TO THE DEV OUTBOX IN A PRODUCTION BUILD**, behind `MAIL_DEV_OUTBOX=1` **and** a loopback `APP_URL`, set in `playwright.config.ts`'s `webServer.env` and nowhere else. `next start` runs as production, where `send()` throws — so **every mail-sending flow was untestable from a browser, not just the mail**: `inviteContact` sends after its transaction commits, so pressing Invite would write the row and then 500, and the token exists nowhere but that message.
3. **FIVE REFUSALS BECAME REAL `DomainErrorCode`s** — `CONTACT_NOT_INVITABLE`, `INVITE_IN_FLIGHT`, `ACCESS_TRANSITION_INVALID`, `CONTACT_HAS_ACCESS`, `CONTACT_HAS_HISTORY`, plus the archived client moving to the existing `ARCHIVED`. All six were `INVALID_INPUT`, which renders as "Invalid input." — harmless while the server half had no caller, and the single biggest gap between it and a usable surface. Both dbtests pin the codes now rather than the class.
4. **`minPasswordLength: 12` IS STATED ON THE PORTAL INSTANCE.** Better Auth's default is 8 while `/signup` and the change-password form have always put `minLength={12}` on the input — a UI asking for twelve over a service taking eight. `acceptContactInvite` reads that config and is the sole path that ever sets a portal password, so the number there was the only policy there was. No contact has ever held a portal credential, so raising it stranded nothing.
5. **THE FIXTURE HAS A THIRD CONTACT** — Carina Ek, INVITED, carrying a seeded PENDING invitation whose raw token is `seed.contactInviteToken` — and the walks have **two new stops**, `portal-invite` and `portal-invite-unavailable`. The tab now shows three of the five statuses instead of one, and the acceptance page has an address that stands still to be photographed at. **The sweep is 216 shots after this commit** (54 stops × light/dark × desktop/phone — measured, and note AGENTS.md's "204 / 51 stops" was already stale before this slice), and `client-contacts` changes because the tab has a third row.
6. **ONE TRUSTED IP DERIVATION, `src/lib/client-ip.ts`** — forced by the review, see below.

**THE REVIEW: 9 read-only reviewers, 3 adversarial refuters per finding, 214 agents. 37 CONFIRMED (7 high), 10 plausible, 21 refuted. 33 of the 37 are fixed and the other four are dispositioned below. It found more than the implementing session did, and the most important one defeated the slice's own headline control.**

**THE HIGH FINDING THAT MATTERED MOST: the rate limit was keyed on a header the caller writes.** `clientIp` read `x-real-ip` FIRST and fell back to the LEFTMOST `x-forwarded-for` hop. RUNBOOK's documented self-host deployment forwards `x-forwarded-for` and nothing strips an inbound `x-real-ip`; nginx's standard `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` *appends*, so the leftmost entry is the client's own contribution. `curl -H 'X-Real-Ip: <random>'` in a loop was therefore a brand-new subject with a brand-new budget on every request — **the whole in-process floor, the thing this slice added because `allow()` is a no-op without Upstash, never refused anything.** And `src/lib/request-context.ts` had a SECOND derivation with the OPPOSITE precedence, so a request could be limited under one address and audited under another, and the forged header never appeared in the trail. Both now go through one pure function that counts from the RIGHT by the number of proxies the deployment declares (`TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`, default 1), never reads `x-real-ip`, bounds the value's length (the subject becomes a Map key an unauthenticated caller can create), and refuses a chain shorter than declared. `client-ip.test.ts` pins it across hop counts; **two cases in `request-context.test.ts` had been pinning the old behaviour and are now annotated with why they changed.**

**THE OTHER SIX HIGH FINDINGS.** *(a)* **Archiving a client removed the only control that ends portal access** while leaving that access live — `editable` gated the whole row menu, and an archive is very often exactly when somebody wants that verb. The page computes **two gates** now: `manageable` (the permission) for the verbs that take access away and for erasure, `editable` (permission + a live client) for Invite and for changing records. *(b)* **"Pause access" never asked its question** — `rowActionNeedsConfirm` asks only for a `tone: "danger"` item, so the `confirm` string was dead and one menu click killed the contact's sessions. The confirm is gone rather than the tone added: a pause keeps their tasks and Resume is one click, so it acts like Resume. *(c)* **The suspend/revoke path's reset-token purge matched ZERO ROWS** — Better Auth keys a reset row `identifier = "reset-password:<token>"` with `value = <contact id>`, so a purge keyed on the email deleted nothing and a paused contact's outstanding reset link stayed live. A write that can only ever match nothing is the same class of defect as a write that can only ever be undone. *(d)* **`MAIL_DEV_OUTBOX` was a lone env flag**, which is the shape `next.config.ts` argues at length is FORGEABLE — both `next start` and `playwright.config.ts` load `.env.local` first. It now additionally requires a loopback `APP_URL`, which is structural rather than typed. *(e)* **`localHits` was bounded in entry COUNT but not in bytes**, and the key embedded that same unvalidated header. *(f)* And, from the plausible list, **`MAIL_DEV_OUTBOX=true` crashed the whole application at import** — it was `z.enum(["0","1"])`, so the value anybody would actually type made `envSchema.parse` throw at module load.

**WHAT IT FOUND IN THE PROSE, which is this repository's recurring finding.** My `accept-form.tsx` said Sonner is not mounted on the portal; `<Toaster>` is in the ROOT layout, above all three route groups. (`request-form.tsx` carries the same wrong claim — another feature's file, recorded here rather than edited silently.) My SECURITY.md paragraph called the accept page "the only route that takes input from somebody with no session" — `/invite/[token]` has done that since Phase 1 — and claimed its two buckets are "the only limits that hold with Upstash unprovisioned", which the portal request budget's Postgres counter falsifies. Its table row asserted a window the code does not have. **AUTHZ.md §8's "no contact can sign in today" is falsified by this commit and is now marked CLOSED.** All corrected.

**THREE MORE WORTH NAMING.** *(a)* **`previewContactInvite` did not apply the email binding `acceptContactInvite` enforces**, so the page drew the whole password form for a token the action was always going to reject — and drew the contact's CURRENT name and address, teaching whoever still held the link mailed to the OLD address what the new one is. It answers `null` now, indistinguishable from every other dead token. *(b)* **A mail-transport failure escaped `runForm` untyped**: the invitation commits, `messageForError` rethrows anything that is neither an `AuthzError` nor a `DomainError`, so the member got the error boundary over a row that HAD changed. `inviteContact` returns `{ inviteId, mailed }` now and the surface says which. *(c)* **The safe-`next` guard was going to be a third copy**, and it turned out only one of the three had any check at all: `/login?next=https://evil.example` signed a member in and then `router.push`ed them off-site. One `safeNext` (`src/lib/safe-next.ts`, 7 cases) now guards all three sign-in forms, which **closes a member-plane open redirect that predates this slice**.

**FOUR CONFIRMED FINDINGS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED.** *(1)* **"Remove contact" is offered to a REVOKED contact who has written in the portal, where `deleteContact` always refuses.** Hiding it needs a per-contact "has written anything" count on the hottest read of this page; the refusal says the answer a member needs either way (`CONTACT_HAS_HISTORY`: the record is kept and cannot be deleted) — and deliberately does NOT advise ending their access, because that guard is reachable only for somebody who has none. *(2)* **An invitation issued before a client is archived still mints access**, because acceptance does not consult the client's archived flag — a founder call, not a bug to close quietly. *(3)* **The `(portal)` route group has no error boundary**, so the acceptance action's deliberate rethrow lands on Next's built-in English full-document error page. A portal error boundary is its own small slice. *(4)* **`clients.contacts.portalStatus.*` is a dead duplicate of `states.portalStatus.*`** in both catalogues — pre-existing, and deleting keys risks a dynamic read I cannot prove absent. *(5, from the low list)* **The invitation email is English-only**, so a localised acceptance page is reached through an untranslated message; `Contact.locale` exists and mail i18n does not.

**AND ONE THING THE REVIEW MADE ME CHANGE MY MIND ABOUT.** The badge vocabulary and the verbs were three different words for one act, and Swedish `Återkallad` already means "the invitation was revoked" in `states.inviteStatus`. `states.portalStatus` now reads **Paused / Ended · Pausad / Avslutad**, matching "Pause access" / "End access" — and both are SHORTER than what they replace, so the 11rem trailing track and the Swedish width walk are not at risk.

**FOUR TRAPS THIS SESSION PAID FOR.**

1. **~~`REVOKED` IS TERMINAL AND NOTHING SAYS SO TO A MEMBER.~~ SETTLED AND FIXED, 2026-09-23 — OPEN_QUESTIONS C28.** `inviteContact` admitted only `NO_ACCESS` and `INVITED`, so a contact whose access had been ended could never be invited again — and `deleteContact` refuses anybody who has written in the portal, so **a returning client contact who once left a comment had no path to portal access at all.** The row simply stopped offering Invite and nothing said why. The founder settled it the other way: **ending access is not forever.** `INVITABLE_PORTAL_STATUSES` (`src/clients/portal-status.ts`, a LEAF so the browser module may read the same literal the service does) admits `REVOKED`, the Contacts tab offers Invite on such a row, and it mints a FRESH invitation rather than a resend. `ACTIVE` and `SUSPENDED` are still refused — a paused contact is RESUMED, because re-inviting one would undo the pause through a door that audits `contact.invited` and leaves `RESUME` throwing. **The released assignments do NOT come back**: restoring access is not restoring history, and a dbtest pins that.
2. **A PIPED `tail` HID A FAILING TEST AND LIED ABOUT THE EXIT CODE.** `pnpm test:db 2>&1 | tail -60` gave no interim output for 34 minutes and then reported **exit 0 while vitest had exited 1** — bash reports the last command in a pipeline, so the harness notification and the log's own last line both said 0, directly under `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1`. Only reading the text caught it. This is AGENTS.md's standing trap and it cost nothing only because the failure text fell inside the last 60 lines. **Run it unpiped, or append `; echo "EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"`.**
3. **A SECOND TEST FILE PINNED A REFUSAL CODE I CHANGED.** `clients.dbtest.ts:166` asserted `INVALID_INPUT` for `deleteContact`; I had updated only `contact-access.dbtest.ts`, the file I had read. Grep every test for a code string before changing it — the other 20 hits were unrelated time-module validations.
4. **THE i18n PARITY TEST TREATS A PLURAL BRANCH'S FIRST WORD AS AN ARGUMENT NAME.** `icuArgs` in `src/i18n/messages.test.ts` matches the first token inside any `{...}`, so `=0 {no tasks came back}` / `{inga uppgifter…}` fails as a mismatched ICU argument between locales. Every plural in the catalogue starts its branches with a digit or `#`, which is why nobody had hit it. A zero case belongs in the ACTION as its own message (`accessRevokedNone`), which is better copy anyway.

**GATES.** typecheck ✅ · ESLint `src e2e scripts --max-warnings 0` → 0 ✅ · unit **80 files / 1275 passed / 1 skipped** ✅ (from 77/1241: `+client-ip.test.ts`, `+safe-next.test.ts`, `+ratelimit/local.test.ts`, plus the config and proxy cases) · `pnpm build` ✅ with `/portal/invite/[token]` and `/portal/login` both dynamic (ƒ). **Mutation-checked, because a passing test is not evidence until it has been made to fail:** reverting the delete-then-set on `allowLocal`'s refused path fails the eviction test; the previous version of that test inserted 200 subjects against a cap of 20 000 and so asserted nothing about eviction at all. **`test:db` 48 files / 710 tests, 710 passed, exit 0** (2057 s — run UNPIPED, see trap 2; `ordering.dbtest.ts` clean). **Browser harness 147 passed / 1 skipped, exit 0**, and the count is the proof the new tests ran: 145 → 148 collected. Both `portal-invite.spec.ts` tests green, which means the whole chain is proven end to end — a member's click, the mail, the outbox, the token, the acceptance page, a password, a session, `/portal` — and then End access and Delete record through the real row menu. The Swedish width walk passed, so the two new stops and the relabelled badges fit their track.

**2026-09-23 — SLICE 55: THE PORTAL INVITE FLOW, SERVER HALF — the slice every portal slice before it was dark without.**

**WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIZE.** Nothing in the product wrote `Contact.portal_status` until this commit. Every contact on every live tenant sits at the `NO_ACCESS` default, so **no client has ever held a portal session** — which means slice 6a's request intake, 6b's triage lane and 6c's hand-over have all been working code that no real person could reach, and 6c's hand-over allowlist (`ACTIVE` or `INVITED`) refused every contact there is. This is the writer. After it, Phase 3's DoD is reachable.

**WHAT LANDED.** `ContactInvite` (migration `20260923020000`, class A — `tenant_isolation` + `portal_deny`, registered in both registry lists; DDL only, **no `neon-smoke` dispatch owed**). `inviteContact` / `previewContactInvite` / `acceptContactInvite` / `setContactPortalAccess`, plus `releaseContactAssignments` in the work module. Raw tokens never touch the database — sha256 stored, the link carries it once — and **re-inviting SUPERSEDES**, so there is one live token per contact and a forwarded link dies the moment a new one is sent.

**THREE FOUNDER DECISIONS, 2026-09-23, and two went against the recommendation — which is now five of eight across three slices.** *(1)* **Removing access returns the work**: the tasks that person held come back to the agency unassigned. An assignment to somebody who cannot see the task is not an assignment, which is the rule `changeItemVisibility` already applies. *(2)* **BOTH a pause and a removal** — I recommended one verb; the founder wants a pause that resumes in one click (parental leave, a contractor between phases) and a removal that ends it. They differ in exactly three things: the credential, the tasks, the audit action. *(3)* **Inviting is a choice on the add-contact form** — I recommended a separate button. It is both in the end: the tick is the shortcut for the common case, and the row still needs a verb because every contact that exists today has no access.

**A PAUSE KEEPS THE WORK AND A REMOVAL RETURNS IT**, and that follows from what each verb is for rather than from symmetry: a pause is "they will be back", so taking their tasks away would make the one-click return a lie.

**THE ERASURE CONTROL WAS A TRAP WAITING TO SPRING.** `deleteContact` refused anything but `NO_ACCESS`. The moment `portal_status` had a writer, a REVOKED contact became permanently undeletable — a person's record unerasable because the agency had deliberately ended their access, which is the wrong direction for an erasure control to fail. It accepts `NO_ACCESS` or `REVOKED` now; `INVITED`, `ACTIVE` and `SUSPENDED` are still refused. The sweep is the other half: `work_item.assignee_contact_id` is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so without it a removed contact holding a task blocks the delete at the database — the residue slice 6c's review named, closed by the slice that first writes the column it depends on.

**THE SEAM RULE MOVED THE FEATURE RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY ROUND.** `withPlatform` is platform-plane only, and ESLint refused it in a tenant-plane file. The acceptance path genuinely needs it — a contact presenting a token has no session, no tenant and no client, so there is nothing to open `withTenant` for, which is exactly the justification the rule's own allowlist gives for `members/invites.ts`. Rather than add the whole feature to that list, the two token halves went into `contact-invite-token.ts` and **only that file is exempt**; the four member-driven writers stay under the rule. **Then belt two caught it independently** (`src/db/import-boundary.test.ts` pins the same allowlist), which is the two-belt design doing its job.

**A DEAD WRITE, FOUND BY THE TEST, AND ITS TWIN IS STILL IN `members/invites.ts`.** The expiry branch stamped `status: EXPIRED` and then refused — but the refusal THROWS, the transaction rolls back, and the stamp goes with it. A write that can only ever be undone is dead code that reads like a fix. `expires_at` is the authority and every reader derives expiry from it. Removed here; **the member invitation's `acceptInvite` has the identical shape and its stamp does not persist either** — left alone as another feature's file rather than edited silently, and recorded here so it is not rediscovered.

**AND ONE CORRECTION TO THIS SESSION'S OWN PLAN.** I had said the slice owed `waitingOnClient` a predicate to HIDE a paused contact's tasks, by analogy with the `portalEnabled` fix. That was wrong: with the portal switched off nobody can see the project and the row is noise, but a paused or not-yet-accepted contact genuinely holds the task and the agency genuinely is blocked — what is missing is a REASON. Hiding would take the work off the only surface that tracks it. The card labels the row instead ("invitation not accepted yet" / "access paused"), which is the thing a member can act on.
