**2026-09-22 — SLICE 53 (memo slice 6c, SECOND COMMIT): THE AGENCY HANDS WORK OVER — and a review finding, acted on, uncovered a transaction race that had been hiding behind it.**

**WHAT IT IS.** `assigneeContactId` finally has a surface. The item rail's `A` picker grows a second group — the item's client's own people — and picking one hands the task over. Nothing else: no new control, because `work_item_single_assignee` is `num_nonnulls(…) <= 1`, so "who is doing this" has one answer and a second control beside the first would be a second answer the row cannot hold. Taking a task back is the same picker's Unassign, which is `assignItem`'s job and clears the contact and any claim in one statement.

**THE LESSON WORTH THE MOST, and it is now an AGENTS.md standing trap: a `Promise.all` inside a Prisma INTERACTIVE transaction is not safe to GROW.** The code review asked me to drop a redundant `assertInScope` from `getItemDetail` — it can never deny, which both reviews proved independently from opposite directions, and it cost a whole uncached `resolveScope` on every panel open. Dropping it was right. But that assertion had been *accidentally serialising* the contact read, and without it the read became a fifth concurrent leg of a four-leg batch — at which point **`readItemComments`, a function this slice never touched, threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` on its own `findMany`**. Prisma over the `pg` driver adapter does not serialise concurrent statements on a transaction's one connection (`pg` says so itself), so the legs share it and a loser resolves `undefined`. **The blast lands in the leg that LOSES, not the one you added, so the stack names innocent code** — and it fired in one test of a full file and never when that test ran alone. A new read inside an existing transaction goes in SEQUENCE, after the batch, never into it.

**THE REVIEWS: 3 security findings + 13 code findings, every one dispositioned. The security review found NO confidentiality issue and no bypass** — it re-derived the CHECK, the permission split, and independently proved there is no publish cascade (`work_tree_guards` *refuses* a client-visible child under an internal parent rather than cascading), and confirmed `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS` and `PORTAL_NEVER_SELECTED` byte-identical to HEAD. The code review's three substantive ones were all real and all mine, and they are **one defect in three places: the pair did not reach every surface that names an assignee**.

- **The board card's meta row was gated on `assigneeMemberId`**, so a title-only task handed to a contact drew no assignee at all — the exact "a row that is assigned saying it is not" this commit exists to end, surviving inside its own fix. It worked only on cards carrying some other meta, which is why the new e2e — asserting the BACKLOG row — sailed past it. The spec now asserts the card.
- **Group-by-assignee and the assignee filter put contact-held work in "Unassigned"**, beside work nobody holds; filtering for any real person made it vanish from every lane. New `WITH_CLIENT` bucket: one lane between the team and Unassigned, drawn only when it has work, and one filter row offered only where the surface holds such a task. ONE bucket and not one per contact — a lane per contact would need the client's roster plumbed into the two hottest reads in the product; the lane answers "is this with us?" and the card still names the person. Safe as a lane because a card can only be dragged within its own (`canDrop` compares `laneKey`), so it is never a reassignment target.
- **A contact-held SUBTASK showed a blank** in the Subtasks list under its parent — the one list neither the board nor the backlog covers, and `assignItemToContact` handles a subtask explicitly (it takes the parent's rank lock).

**AND ONE I HAD ARGUED MYSELF INTO, fixed before the reviews ran.** The first cut offered the contact rows to a member without `work_item:change_visibility`, on the written grounds that "the surface cannot resolve it per row". It can: the rule is about THIS row and the panel holds both the cap and the visibility. The group is hidden now (§3.1: hidden, never disabled) and comes back the moment somebody shares the task — the same shape the 6b reviews corrected in the triage lane one day earlier.

**TWO DECISIONS THE REVIEWS FORCED INTO THE OPEN, both recorded in UI.md §5.2 rather than left in the code.** *(a)* **`portalEnabled` is not a gate here, but it changes the sentence.** UI.md's `A` row used to say "contacts (portal-enabled projects only)" and the first cut DELETED that qualifier rather than implementing it — caught by the review. The hand-over stays offered on a portal-off project, for consistency with its sibling flip (`changeItemVisibility` has never consulted `portalEnabled` either: visibility is the ROW's flag, the switch is the PROJECT's, and refusing here would mean a member may share a task but not hand it over on the same project). What was false was the warning — `portal_gate` ANDs the two — so there are two sentences now and the column picks which. *(b)* **The warning is a warning, not an "offer to make it CLIENT_VISIBLE"**: the flip is not optional, so an offer would be a confirmation step on a verb whose one outcome the member has just been told, and the consent that matters is the C M A code the group is hidden without.

**THE GATE ASYMMETRY BOTH REVIEWS FOUND, kept deliberately and now pinned by a test.** The picker's ROSTER needs `client:view`; the assignee's NAME on the board, the backlog and the rail does not. That is the rule and not an oversight: naming the person attached to a row the member is already reading is part of reading the row — the door comment bylines, activity refs and the triage lane's `reportedBy` have always used — while listing the client's people is a directory of a company the member may have no business browsing. Gating the name too would put "Unassigned" back on the board for exactly the seat that can see the task. A dbtest now fails if anyone applies the other resolution.

**ALSO FIXED:** the rail's trigger said "Assignee: Astrid Lindqvist", byte-identical to a colleague's, with the distinguishing glyph `aria-hidden` — so to a screen reader the task was with the team; the INTERNAL → CLIENT_VISIBLE flip was announced by NOBODY (the visibility island announces only its own commits), and the commit's `shared` flag now speaks it; `assigneeContactName` joined `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS` before the portal half can copy the shape across (the equality pin made that a two-place change, exactly as 6b built it to); the ACTIVE/INVITED allowlist became ONE `ASSIGNABLE_PORTAL_STATUSES` instead of two literals a thousand lines apart; a group heading could render over a lone group; the dbtest recorded a PLATFORM-level `user` id only after six statements that can throw; and two seat docblocks described seats the code no longer builds. **The `work_item_single_assignee` CHECK is "at most one", NOT an XOR** — verified against `20260820170000` — and every claim this slice makes about it now says so; the older shorthand elsewhere predates the slice and was left alone.

**2026-09-22 — SLICE 51 (memo slice 6c, FIRST COMMIT): A TASK THE AGENCY HANDS TO THE CLIENT — and the founder's answer went against the recommendation again, which is twice in two slices.**

**THE QUESTION AND THE ANSWER.** `assigneeContactId` has existed since 2W with **no writer at all**, and AUTHZ §8's row for `portal.work_item.act` read *"brokered state change to the project's DONE-category state"*. Taken literally that lets the **least-trusted principal in the product enter a state an EMPLOYEE cannot** — the seeded `DONE` carries `requiresApproval`, and `work_item:approve` is C M A. Asked plainly; answered: **the tick moves NOTHING.** It stamps `work_item.contact_completed_at`, notifies the agency, and the agency closes the task itself. `DONE` now means one thing for everyone — work the agency has accepted — and a client's tick is a CLAIM: a fact about what the client SAYS, not about the state of the work. AUTHZ §8 is amended in place; DATA_MODEL §6.14 and UI.md §11 carry the rule. *(My recommendation was the literal reading, on the grounds that the approval gate is about the agency's own work. The founder's is better, and it is the cheaper direction too: a claim is one nullable column, where a state change would have been a second meaning for `DONE`.)*

**THE SECOND DECISION: HANDING A TASK OVER IS A SHARE, AND IS GATED AS ONE.** `work_item_contact_assignee_visible` (a CHECK since 2W) admits no third answer — a contact-assigned row MUST be CLIENT_VISIBLE — so `assignItemToContact` on an INTERNAL row demands **`work_item:change_visibility` (C M A)** on top of `work_item:edit`, and audits `work_item.visibility_changed` with `via: contact_assignment`. An employee can still hand over a task the client can already see. The alternative would have made the C M A code a speed bump for the one act it governs, which is the shape of the `work_item:triage` bug the 6b reviews found the day before.

**WHAT LANDED (server + portal read only; the surfaces are the SECOND commit).** Migration `20260922180000` — one nullable column and one CHECK (`contact_completed_at IS NULL OR assignee_contact_id IS NOT NULL`), DDL only, **no `neon-smoke` dispatch owed**, no grant (table-level since 2W), no RLS change (the read gate has no assignee term, so "which are mine" is a PROJECTION change; the write gate refuses a contact principal outright, so the tick is brokered). · `assignItemToContact` and the claim-clearing writers in `items.ts`. · `transitionState` clears a claim **on ARRIVING at DONE or CANCELLED and not before** — an ordinary live move keeps it, because the agency picking the work up is not an answer and clearing there would silently delete the client's own statement. · `setPortalTaskDone`, a TOGGLE, in `portal-writes.ts` — the retraction is not a nicety: nothing on the member plane can clear a claim except answering it, so without an untick a mis-tick would stand as a falsehood only the agency could remove, by finishing work that is not finished. · `PortalScopeRef` gained its **`work_item`** kind, the debt that type's own docblock recorded — and it is the strongest of the three, because `work_item`'s `portal_gate` carries the row's own `visibility`. · `writeContactActivity`, the brokered twin of `writeActivity` over ONE shared insert, so the portal-safe decision is plane-independent. · Two audit actions, one notification kind (INSTANT — the whole point of assigning a task to a client is that the agency is BLOCKED until it comes back), and `contact-tasks.dbtest.ts` (prefix `ctask-`, registered in `DBTEST_PREFIXES`).

**THE REVIEWS: 5 code findings + 2 security findings on the feature, then 10 more on the FIXES. Every one dispositioned; all real, all mine.** The fix pass earned itself twice over — see the second bullet.

- **THE SAFETY LEVER WOULD HAVE 500'd, and both reviews found it from opposite directions.** Giving `assigneeContactId` a writer made the 2W CHECK **reachable for the first time**: "Make private" on a handed-over task raised a bare 23514 that `db-errors.ts` does not map. So the one flip whose entire purpose is to stop showing a client something failed with a generic error and **left the row published**, while the member worked out for themselves that they had to unassign first. `changeItemVisibility` now ends the assignment in the same statement — cleared rather than refused, because this lever must always work and an assignment to somebody who can no longer see the task is not an assignment.
- **AND MY FIX FOR IT BROKE THE LEVER A SECOND TIME.** The history row was written against the item as it WAS, reasoning that it should be client-visible and would be flipped later by the downgrade trigger. `work_item_activity_denorm_guard` re-reads the item's LIVE visibility and refused it, rolling back the whole flip. **Only the dbtest caught it** — invisible to typecheck, to ESLint and to every unit test. It is written against the post-update row now, and the test's own comment that repeated the wrong model was corrected with it.
- **A CONTACT ID IN A MEMBER-RESOLVED FIELD.** `assignItem` put the contact id into an `assignee` history row's `oldRef`; `readItemActivity` resolves that field against the MEMBER table, so taking a task back from a client rendered **"unassigned Unknown"** — an attribution lost in the trail, eight lines from the comment in `activity.ts` promising it could not happen. Two rows now, one per field.
- **A DENYLIST WHERE THE CODEBASE SAYS ALLOWLIST, TWICE, IN AS MANY WORDS** (`policy.ts`, `portal-gate.ts`). The assignee check refused `SUSPENDED` alone and admitted the other four statuses — including `REVOKED` and `NO_ACCESS`, which is the column's **DEFAULT** and therefore what every contact on a live tenant holds until an invite flow ships. Each would have published the task to the client for somebody who can never open it, and `deleteContact` (which permits deleting only a `NO_ACCESS` contact) would then have hit the RESTRICT FK — **an erasure control broken by a task nobody can see**. Now `ACTIVE` or `INVITED`. *The residue is named in the code: nothing clears the column when a status changes LATER, so the slice that ships "revoke access" owes a sweep.*
- **A LOCK PLAN READ OFF THE UNLOCKED PROBE.** The rank-queue decision tested `probe.visibility`, which can go stale. Worse than stale: `work_item_parent_guard` fires on **SET-list membership**, not on the value moving, so a subtask's contact assignment share-locks the parent EVERY time — a two-row writer that could have run with the queue never taken. `probe.parentId` alone now, and `rank-lock.ts`'s own list of queued writers was wrong in exactly the way that caused it. **Condition a queue decision on what your statement WRITES, never on what the row currently holds.**
- **THE TRIPWIRE CAUGHT MY COMMENT, not my code.** The text tier fired on `portal.ts` because a comment I wrote there SPELLED the forbidden member-assignee column while explaining why the contact one is not forbidden. That is the property that makes the list worth having; the comment was rewritten so it cannot name it. *(The same class as 6b's own pin catching itself.)*
- **Also fixed:** the item panel printed a raw column name for both new fields (new sentences, a `contact` lookup separate from `member`, two rail glyphs, property labels, en + sv); the Swedish read in the present tense among thirty preterite siblings on a dated rail; `changeItemVisibility` ended a client assignment **silently** (it now returns `endedContactAssignment` and audits it, the mirror of `shared`); a mis-cited migration; a shared fixture mutated without `try/finally`; two stale sentence counts.
- **AND A TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE LANDMINE, found by the slice rather than by a review.** `import-boundary.test.ts` **timed out** under the full unit suite while passing in 2.0 s alone — about 1500 added lines was the difference. Several tripwires here AST-parse **every file under `src/`**, so their cost grows with each slice while vitest's 5 s default does not. Raised to 30 s (`hookTimeout` with it, as `vitest.db.config.ts` already pairs them), because a timeout is not an assertion and the failure mode it prevents is the dangerous one: **a whole-tree security tripwire that starts going red for a reason it is not about, gets called flaky, and gets deleted.**

**WHAT THIS COMMIT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT HAVE.** No member surface — nothing calls `assignItemToContact` or `setPortalTaskDone` outside the dbtest, and neither is on the module barrel, which BOUNDS the blast radius of everything above. No portal Done tick. No `/home` "waiting on client" card. No e2e: the member→client round trip is worth one spec and belongs with the UI that can drive it. Contacts still have no notification channel, so a client learns they have been asked only by opening the portal.

**2026-09-22 — SLICE 50 (memo slice 6b, SECOND COMMIT): THE LANE ITSELF — and the tripwire caught the same class of mistake twice in one slice, from opposite directions.**

**WHAT LANDED.** `/projects/[key]/triage` — a route, a tab hidden without `work_item:triage`, the four verbs with their dialog, the `triage` keyboard scope, and an e2e that drives the whole round trip. Plus the drop-target fix the first commit made urgent.

They cannot both be live, because `S` is "Move to…" on the board and "Snooze" here. One surface, one meaning — recorded in UI.md §6 so the next reader does not re-derive it.

**THE TRIPWIRE, AGAIN, AND THE RIGHT ANSWER WAS NOT TO WIDEN IT.** The lane's READ began life inside `triage.ts` — which the FIRST commit had just added to `portal-projections.test.ts`'s structural tier — and failed on `descriptionText`, `snoozedUntil` and a `$queryRaw`. All three are legitimate for a MEMBER-plane projection and forbidden for a file feeding the contact plane, which is precisely what the failure was saying: **keeping both in one file means relaxing one of the two sets of rules.** So the read moved to `triage-lane.ts`, the way `portal.ts` and `portal-writes.ts` are already split, and for the same reason — *which plane a piece of code serves should be a property of where it lives.* (The `$queryRaw` went too: it asked Postgres for `now()`, which buys nothing when both sides of the comparison are app clocks.) **Twice in one slice the tripwire was right and the feature was wrong.**

**THE E2E FOUND A FLAKE IN ITSELF, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN A GREEN RUN.** First pass: 2 of 3, failing on `Expected: "CANCELLED" / Received: "TRIAGE"`. Opening `error-context.md` FIRST (the standing order) showed no page snapshot at all — the failure was a DATABASE assertion, not a locator — so both candidates AGENTS.md names were ruled out in one read. The cause was the test racing its own action: the lane removes a row OPTIMISTICALLY, so `toHaveCount(0)` is satisfied before the server is asked, and the next line read the row. **The accept test passed for exactly the reason the decline test failed** — it happens to wait for the success toast first. The fix is not a `waitFor`: the toast is the only member-visible signal that the write landed (a refusal toasts an error and puts the row back), so waiting on it is the correct assertion. 3/3 after.

**WHAT ONLY THE BROWSER COULD SAY:** `J` then `A` answers the focused row. The `triage` scope had been declared and empty since 2W and this is the first surface to mount it — whether the dispatcher routes a bare letter to a `run: null` binding on the focused row depends on guard order, on `G` not being armed and on no Radix layer holding the keyboard, none of which is visible from the source. This repo's standing note applies: two review verifiers once traced cmdk's source to the opposite of what a headless browser showed.

**THE DROP-TARGET FIX, which PLAN §0 owed and the first commit made urgent.** `canEnterState` takes no item, so it could not express "not INTO cancelled, for a REQUEST" — the first rule in this product about the thing being MOVED rather than its target. New `canItemEnterState` beside it; the board answers it in `canDrop` **per drag** (`kind` rides with the drag data) rather than per column; the panel's `S` picker and the backlog's select pass the item's kind; and the bulk bar drops the target whenever the SELECTION holds a request, because `bulkChangeState` is all-or-nothing. This needed `kind` on `ItemListEntry` — one more column on a select the whole product already runs — and the compiler found every site.

**TWO SMALLER DECISIONS WORTH THE INK.** *(a)* **The empty lane offers a real verb.** §5.8 requires `variant="empty"` to offer the verb that changes it, and no member can create a request — the portal's own empty state hit this wall and took `forbidden`. But there IS a next step here: an empty lane usually means the portal is off or nobody has been invited, so a member who can manage it gets a link to the Portal tab, and one who cannot gets the `forbidden` shape with an INBOX glyph rather than a shield (a shield says "you are blocked", which is not what an empty queue means). *(b)* **Snooze resolves a chosen day to 09:00 LOCAL, not midnight** — midnight today is already past, so the service would refuse it with nothing on screen explaining why, and a snooze is a working-hours promise anyway.

**THREE MORE FOUNDER DECISIONS, ASKED AND ANSWERED 2026-09-22 — and two of them went AGAINST the recommendation, which is why they were worth asking.**

1. **ONLY MANAGERS MAY DECLINE.** New code `work_item:triage_decline` (**C M**, TEMPLATE_VERSION → 6, catalogue 98 → 99). It SUPPLEMENTS `work_item:triage` (C M E) rather than replacing it — the shape `work_item:approve` takes over `work_item:edit` — so an employee keeps Accept and Snooze and loses Decline and Duplicate. *Duplicate is covered because from the client's side it IS a decline: `portal.ts` renders both as "Declined" with the reason, so a permission guarding one word would guard nothing.* The two buttons and the `D`/`U` keys are HIDDEN without it (§3.1: hidden, never disabled), off a `canDecline` flag the lane's own read carries, so the surface never offers a verb that would be refused. *(My recommendation was to leave it open to employees; the founder's reasoning — publishing prose to a client in the agency's name is a delivery lead's call — is the same one every other row of AUTHZ §3.2's portal column already follows, and `project_update:publish`, this product's only other member-prose-to-client code, is C M too.)*

2. **WHAT THE CLIENT WAS TOLD IS KEPT**, as a `triageReason` row in the task's own history. It is INTERNAL — the AGENCY's record of what it said; the client reads the live answer through the projection, never through history. The audit row still carries no free text (SECURITY.md §7 minimisation), which is exactly why this was needed: nothing anywhere held the words, and they are REPLACEABLE, because reopening a decline clears the column and it can be declined again with different text. "What did we tell them in March" had no answer at all.

3. **AN ANSWERED REQUEST OUTLIVES THE ARCHIVE.** `archivedAt` moved from the whole `where` into the LIVE-WORK branch only. Archiving still hides a task in progress, as it always has; it no longer deletes the explanation a client was given. The PROJECT's archive is untouched and still hides everything — switching a project off is a decision about the relationship, not about one row. *(My recommendation was to leave it; the founder's is better, and it closes the last door the silent-vanish had left open.)*

**AND A SEEDING BOUNDARY WORTH WRITING DOWN, because it is the first code bump since the agent rules were tightened.** `prisma/seed.ts` has two halves: the global `Permission` catalogue upsert (platform-level, idempotent, additive) and B3 template propagation, which writes `RolePermission` rows into **every existing tenant's roles, `naxdor` included**. AGENTS.md forbids an agent the second half outright. Only the FIRST is needed to make tests runnable — `src/members/templates.ts` grants a role its codes BY CODE, so a throwaway tenant provisioned after a catalogue addition silently misses the new one — so that half now lives in **`scripts/seed-catalog.ts`**, which ran (99 codes, 1 new) and says in its own header what it deliberately does not do. **THE RELEASE OWES A FULL `prisma/seed.ts` RUN**, and it is the founder's: without the propagation, an existing tenant's owners and managers do not hold a code the code path now requires.

**THE REVIEWS OF THIS COMMIT: 18 code findings (three HIGH) + 9 security findings. Every one dispositioned; the HIGH three were all real and all mine.**

- **HIGH — a rejected action bricked the lane.** No `try`/`catch` around the server action. `runAction` rethrows anything that is not an Authz/DomainError, and a server action also rejects on transport failure — so `setBusyId(null)` never ran and the optimistic removal never rolled back: **the row vanished with no toast and every button and key on the surface stayed dead until a manual reload.** A failure rendering as a success and then freezing the page, three lines under a comment quoting the trap it broke. Caught now, with the same `.catch` shape `backlog-table.tsx` already uses; the picker's own read got one too.
- **HIGH — the duplicate picker was broken three ways**, and it was the one verb the e2e did not drive. cmdk's `value`/`onValueChange` were wired straight to the CHOSEN id — the exact thing AGENTS.md's cmdk note forbids (*a row cmdk lights by itself is a highlight, never a selection*) — so the dialog opened with a target nobody picked, typing silently re-pointed it, and a search matching nothing called back with `""`, leaving the confirm button enabled over a submit that did nothing. The search also scored typing against UUIDs (`shouldFilter` defaults TRUE and each row's `value` was an id), and `CommandEmptyState` — a plain div with no logic, for callers that own their filtering — sat permanently above the populated list. Rebuilt on `PropertyPicker`'s shape, and **`e2e/triage.spec.ts` now drives it**.
- **HIGH — the roving branch skipped `focusedKeyGuards`.** The guard inputs were computed and then used only by the verb branch. `Ctrl+J` moved focus and was preventDefaulted; worse, an armed `G` was consumed here and **LEFT ARMED**, because this handler runs before the dispatcher and `preventDefault` makes `decide()` bail before `clearPending()`. `G` then `J` therefore ate the member's next key too, in silence. Both reference surfaces call that guard; everything had been copied from them except the line that matters.
- **TWO FALSE CLAIMS I HAD WRITTEN INTO CODE *AND* INTO UI.md**, which is worse than either: (a) `run: null` + `enabled: false` does NOT swallow a key — `decide()` skips a `run: null` binding BEFORE it reads `enabled`, as that field's own docblock states; (b) "the backlog's state select passes the item's kind" — it did not. **A doc that overstates a guard is worse than no doc.**
- **THE CARD-LEVEL DROP TARGET BYPASSED THE COLUMN FIX ENTIRELY.** Pragmatic-dnd SKIPS a target that refuses and hands the drop to the next one under the pointer, so dropping a request onto any CARD in the Cancelled column ran the move anyway. Also missed: the board's **MovePicker** (the documented keyboard/mobile twin of the drag) and the backlog's per-row select. All fixed; `kind` now rides with the drag data.
- **BOTH REVIEWS INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE SAME ASSURANCE GAP:** `listTriage` shipped with **no test of either gate** — deleting `requireAccess` or `assertInScope` left every suite green. That is the identical vacuous-test shape the FIRST commit of this slice was corrected for, one day earlier, in a different file. Now eight dbtests, on seats chosen so exactly ONE gate can be the one refusing: admin has scope and not the permission (FORBIDDEN), employee has the permission and — on a project it is not assigned to — no scope (NOT_FOUND), plus positive twins so a refusal cannot pass for a broken read. *The employee had to be GIVEN a `MemberProject` to prove the new Accept/Decline split, which removed the only seat that had the permission without scope — hence the second, unassigned project. A fixture that can no longer distinguish two gates is a fixture that has stopped testing one of them.*
- **AND MY OWN NEW PIN CAUGHT ITSELF.** The security review asked for a structural guard on who may import the lane's read (`triage-lane.ts` is the first file created deliberately OUTSIDE the tripwire's structural tier, so its safety was inferential). The first version matched any file MENTIONING `triage-lane` or `listTriage` and flagged two innocents — a sentence in `notify.ts` and a `data-testid` on the lane's own component. That is this file's own standing lesson about text-tier matching, applied to itself. It matches the import specifier now.
- **Also fixed:** a refusal destroyed the member's reply (the reply now lives in the lane, not the dialog); focus dropped to `<body>` after every verb (it moves to the next row, and only the ACTING row's buttons disable — `queue-rows.tsx` records why disabling a focused button is its own bug); the snooze field offered days the service refuses (`min`/`max` are now the service's own bounds, and `min` is TOMORROW because a day resolves to 09:00 local); the truncation sentence counted the client-filtered list; `answered` ids were never pruned, so a reopened request stayed invisible; the lane listed anything in a TRIAGE state rather than requests; the duplicate picker's read was uncapped and offered DONE work; a missing `handleAuthzRedirect`; and Swedish called one surface two names (`Sortering` vs `Triage`) with `Ta emot` for Accept.
- **DISPOSITIONED, NOT FIXED:** the Triage tab is gated on **gate 4 only**, which matches Board and Backlog on the same `work` module rather than Portal's all-four `hasAccess`. Left as-is and the misleading comment corrected: Board and Backlog are UNCONDITIONAL on that module, so a `work`-off tenant meets that wall two tabs earlier, the denial is uniform (404, never 403), and changing it is a behaviour change for the module that belongs in a slice which can test it — the same disposition Time already carries.

**GATES ON THIS COMMIT:** typecheck ✅ · ESLint (`--max-warnings 0`) ✅ · unit **77 files / 1233 passed / 1 skipped** ✅ · `e2e/triage.spec.ts` **4 passed**, exit 0, on `E2E_PORT=3457` ✅ — and because the harness runs `pnpm build && pnpm start`, that run is also the **build gate**. The two affected dbtest files **60 passed** ✅. Full `test:db` and the full browser harness are owed before the push.

**2026-09-22 — SLICE 50 (memo slice 6b, FIRST COMMIT): THE TRIAGE LANE'S SERVER HALF, AND THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THAT WAS OWED.**

**BOTH OWED DECISIONS WERE ASKED AND ANSWERED BY THE FOUNDER, 2026-09-22.** Owed item (0) is CLOSED, and a second question that had to be settled in the same breath was asked with it:

1. **A client's requests ARE visible to their colleagues.** `work_item`'s `portal_gate` is client-scoped and stays that way — it has no `reported_by_contact_id` term, so every ACTIVE contact of a client reads every request that client submitted. The reasons, recorded because this is the file a future reader greps: a `Client` is a COMPANY and the agency's counterparty is the company, not the individual; a request only its submitter can see is orphaned the day they leave; `work_item` would otherwise be the ONE table whose portal gate differs from every sibling, and asymmetry in the gate is the risk class this product fears most; and a request a MEMBER files on the client's behalf has `reportedByContactId = NULL`, which a per-contact predicate would have hidden from everybody. **No policy change was needed and none was made** — the decision is recorded in `20260922120000`'s own comment, in `portal.ts`'s header and in UI.md §11.
2. **A declined request is SHOWN to the client, with the agency's reason.** This is the other half and it is what the slice is mostly about — see below.

**WHAT LANDED (server + portal only; the member-side lane is the SECOND commit of this slice).**
- **`src/modules/work/triage.ts`** — the four verbs (Accept / Decline / Duplicate / Snooze) behind `work_item:triage`, which **leaves `enforcement.test.ts`'s `DECLARED_AHEAD` list** in this commit. It was the oldest name on it; 36 remain. Accept resolves the project's DEFAULT state and clears every triage column (so `TriageStatus.ACCEPTED` is now **never stored** — DATA_MODEL §6.14 amended in place); Decline and Duplicate move to the CANCELLED state carrying a reason; Snooze does not move the row at all and writes an INTERNAL activity row, because a client must not read "they put this off".
- **`work_item.triageReason`** (migration `20260922120000`, DDL only — no DML, so **no `neon-smoke` dispatch is owed**). `VARCHAR(500)`, plus two CHECKs: `work_item_triage_reason_iff_outcome` (a biconditional — a DECLINED/DUPLICATE row must carry a non-blank reason, and nothing else may) and `work_item_triage_duplicate_has_target`. **Both were applied and VALIDATEd against the real Neon dev rows**, which CI — migrating from EMPTY — structurally cannot do.
- **The portal's fifth category, `DECLINED`.** `portal.ts` mapped CANCELLED to nothing, so the one row on a client's list they had SUBMITTED THEMSELVES vanished silently the moment the agency said no — the failure that file's own header called "indefensible" and handed to the founder. A cancelled `kind = REQUEST` now comes back as `DECLINED` with `declinedReason`; a cancelled TASK or BUG is still invisible.
- **`transitionState` now owns the triage columns**, which is a CORRECTNESS FIX as much as a feature. Leaving TRIAGE was already an ordinary move (dragging a request into "To do" IS accepting it) but **nothing cleared `triage_status`** — the row sat in To do still marked `PENDING`, where the lane's own query would have found it for ever. All five entry points (drag, inline, palette-via-`changeState`, bulk, create-into-state) reach that one function, so the clear covers every door. It also **refuses a move from TRIAGE into a CANCELLED state** unless the caller is the triage verb, because that is the one move that makes a client's request disappear and only the member doing it knows why.

**THE THING THE TRIPWIRE CAUGHT, and it was right.** The first cut of the projection selected `kind` to decide the category. `kind` is on `portal-projections.test.ts`'s **NEVER-SELECTED** list — the agency's vocabulary for its own process — and the test failed. The fix was not to widen the list: the `kind = 'REQUEST'` term moved into the `where`, so a cancelled TASK never leaves Postgres at all, and `portalCategory` maps CANCELLED→DECLINED unconditionally **with that clause as its stated precondition**. Strictly stronger than a `continue` in a loop, and the pairing is pinned from the outside by a `portal.dbtest.ts` fixture whose two rows differ in nothing but `kind`. *Do not weaken a tripwire to fit a feature; move the feature.*

**THE ONE RULE THIS SLICE EXISTS TO HOLD**, at three layers on purpose: the service's parser refuses a blank or whitespace reason; `transitionState` refuses every OTHER route from triage into Cancelled; and the CHECK constraint makes a reasonless DECLINED row unwritable by anything — a future import, a fixture, a hand-written UPDATE. Each has its own case in `triage.dbtest.ts`.

**A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING RATHER THAN DISCOVERING:** `bulkChangeState` is ALL-OR-NOTHING by documented design, so a backlog selection that contains a pending request and is moved to Cancelled now refuses the WHOLE batch with `INVALID_INPUT`. That is the safe direction and the member is told, but it is a behaviour change to a shipped surface.

**WHAT THIS COMMIT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT HAVE.** No member-side surface — the `triage` scope is still declared and empty, and UI.md §6 now says why the lane cannot simply be a mode of the board (`SCOPE_ORDER` makes `triage` a PEER of `board`, and peers "never mount together"; `S` is "Move to…" there and "Snooze" here). No notification to the submitting contact: contacts have no notification channel in v1 and inventing one here would mean designing their whole email identity in passing. No e2e — the member→client round trip is worth one spec and it belongs with the UI that can drive it.

**THE TWO FRESH REVIEWS RAN AND THEY EARNED THE RULE ALL OVER AGAIN — 18 findings, and the two HIGH ones were the same bug found independently from opposite directions.** `/code-review` and `/security-review`, both read-only, both against the staged diff with no sight of the implementing reasoning.

**THE BUG BOTH FOUND — the guard was keyed on the wrong column, and the slice's own promise leaked through the gap.** `transitionState`'s refusal keyed on `item.stateCategory === "TRIAGE"`, so it guarded only the ONE-STEP route out of the lane. Two ordinary two-step routes walked past it:

- **Accept, then drop.** A request accepted into "To do" and cancelled weeks later — an entirely ordinary agency workflow — reached the projection cancelled with `triage_reason = NULL`, and `portal.ts` announced **"Declined" in the agency's name with a blank under it**. The database CHECK does not catch it (no status, no reason: the biconditional is satisfied), the state machine did not, and the parser was never reached.
- **Decline, reopen, re-cancel.** Leaving CANCELLED cleared nothing, so a reconsidered decline kept `DECLINED` and its text on a LIVE row; the next ordinary cancel **republished those words as the answer to a decision nobody had made**. Worse than the first, because it is wrong rather than empty.

The security review sharpened *why* it matters beyond honesty: a member holding only `work_item:edit` reached the same end state in two drags, which made **`work_item:triage` a speed bump rather than a gate** for the one outcome it exists to govern. And three places in the diff asserted this could not happen — the `PortalTask` docblock, `transitionState`'s "true by construction" comment, and a new dbtest that encoded the intended invariant and passed because no fixture exercised either route.

**THE FIX IS FOUR PARTS, and it changed the slice's semantics rather than patching the symptom.** (a) The refusal keys on **`item.kind === "REQUEST"`**, not on the category being left: a request is a thing a client asked for for as long as it exists, so ending one always owes them an answer, whenever it happens. (b) `transitionState` clears the triage columns when a row leaves TRIAGE **or CANCELLED**, so a reopen drops the stale answer. (c) **DECLINE and DUPLICATE became LIFECYCLE verbs** — they apply to a request in any live state, not only in the lane — because otherwise (a) would have made an accepted request uncancellable. ACCEPT and SNOOZE stay lane verbs. (d) The projection gained `triageReason: { not: null }`: the write path now guarantees the reason, and the READ path independently refuses to publish a decline it cannot explain — which also closes the retroactive case (F5), since a pre-6b cancelled request stays hidden rather than appearing as a bare "Declined" at deploy.

**THE SECOND HIGH: THE PERMISSION TEST DID NOT TEST THE PERMISSION.** `work_item:triage` is **CME — owner, manager, EMPLOYEE** — so the employee seat the test used *holds it*. The refusal it observed came from `assertInScope` (`setupTenant` writes no `MemberProject`, and `client:view_all` is CMA), so **deleting the `requireAccess` line left the test green**: the headline gate of the slice, the reason the code leaves `DECLARED_AHEAD`, had no test at all. Now driven through the **admin** seat — CMA reaches the row and is excluded from CME — asserting `reason === "FORBIDDEN"`, with the employee kept as a NOT_FOUND control so the two refusals are told apart rather than conflated. *The lesson generalises: a dbtest seat proves what it proves only if exactly one gate can be the one refusing.*

**THE REST, ALL FIXED:** `removeTenant` in `e2e/fixtures/seed-cli.ts` never cleared `duplicate_of_id`, whose FK is `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — and since `sweepDbtests` loops with no try/catch, **one orphan holding a duplicate would have aborted the whole sweep** and left every later stale tenant uncollected (the diff's own residue (iii) said this bit only the Phase-8 purge job: true of `src/`, false of the harness this commit enrols the suite into). · The DUPLICATE branch is the module's **first two-row `work_item` writer** and had no lock-order analysis; a concrete cycle with `moveItem` exists, so it takes `retryOnDeadlock` — the cure `rank-lock.ts` already chose twice for the same shape — with the analysis written into the docblock. · `TRIAGE_REASON_MAX`/`TRIAGE_VERBS` sat in a module that reaches `@/db`, which is the **third instance** of the `"use client"` trap and would have bitten the very next commit; they moved to `triage-limits.ts`, the leaf shape `request-limits.ts` established. · SNOOZE gained a no-op guard (a double submit wrote two audit events and a history row whose old and new values matched). · Swedish `Avböjd` → **`Avböjt`**, to agree with its neuter siblings (`Planerat`, `Klart`, `Avbrutet`). · Two stale "four categories" comments. · An ACCEPT test whose name claimed four columns while measuring one. · `ParsedInput` collapsed to an alias, `Target` reuses `TriageWrite`, `resolveDuplicate` excludes archived targets.

**AND THE TRIPWIRE GOT THE TWO THINGS THE SECURITY REVIEW ASKED FOR.** `triage.ts` joins `STRUCTURAL_ONLY_SURFACES` — which that file's own docblock had **PREDICTED** one slice earlier, in as many words: *"a select-less `findFirst` … added there **when the triage verb lands** would trip nothing."* It landed. (That forced an explicit `select` on the workflow-state read, so `StateRow` narrowed from the whole row to the six fields `transitionState` actually reads — `changeState`'s select-less read still satisfies a `Pick`.) And **`PORTAL_NEVER_SELECTED` now has the pinning-equality test `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS` always had**: a name quietly deleted from it would have weakened the tripwire with nothing failing, which is exactly the property this file denies to everyone else. It matters more now that `duplicateOfId` is written over real data for the first time.

**ONE FINDING IS NOT FIXED AND IS FOR THE FOUNDER (security review F6): `work_item:triage` is CME, so an EMPLOYEE-template member can write free text straight onto a client's portal screen** — no `work_item:change_visibility` (CMA), no MFA step-up, no rate limit. The catalogue decision predates this slice; the consequence is new, because before it no employee-reachable code published member-authored prose to a contact. **Should the decline reason require a higher bar than the verb itself?** Recorded as owed rather than decided.

**AND ONE THE REVIEWS RAISED THAT DECIDES A PUSH, NOT A LINE OF CODE.** Between this commit and the lane's UI there is **no way at all for a member to decline a request**: every route through `transitionState` now refuses it and the verb has no surface. The refusal is the right behaviour (the old route lied to the client), but `main` must not carry that window — **so these two commits push together, not separately.**

**WHAT NEITHER REVIEW FOUND, stated because it is the point of running them:** no confidentiality leak. The security review enumerated exactly which rows the new predicate admits and independently re-verified every claim the migration makes about grants, policies and CHECK NULL-semantics against the migrations themselves rather than the new file's comments. `portal-projections.test.ts` is untouched by the diff — neither list was weakened.

**GATES ON THIS COMMIT (after the fixes):** typecheck ✅ · ESLint (`--max-warnings 0`) ✅ · unit **77 files / 1229 passed / 1 skipped** ✅ · the two affected dbtest files **50 passed** (42 before the fixes; 8 new cases, of which four drive the two-step routes) ✅ · full `test:db` **46 files / 627 passed, 0 failed** in 28.7 min ✅ (45/597 at slice 6a — the +1 file is exactly `triage.dbtest.ts`).

**AND A PROCESS NOTE THAT COST TWO DBTEST RUNS, worth the lines because it will happen again.** Three `test:db` runs were launched against the SAME log path — the first abandoned because `src/` was edited mid-run (which makes a run measure no tree at all), the second because the review fixes superseded it. **`TaskStop` ends the TASK, but each run's file handle keeps its own offset**, so the three interleaved into one file: three summary blocks at lines 475 / 622 / 655, a corrupted byte boundary where two writers overlapped, and a trailing exit-code line that could have been written by any of them. **The near-miss is the lesson: the two ABANDONED runs each printed a clean `Test Files N passed (N)` summary AND exited 1** (`Worker forks emitted error`) — so in this harness a passing summary and a zero exit are INDEPENDENT facts, and the summary alone certifies nothing. That is AGENTS.md's “check exit codes, not just output” in a shape the original note does not cover. The numbers above come from a clean re-run to a unique log with the exit code written to its own file. **A dbtest log path must be unique per run, and the exit code must be captured where nothing else can append to it.**
