**2026-09-21 — SLICE 49 (memo slice 6a): PORTAL REQUEST INTAKE — THE FIRST TIME A CLIENT WRITES TO THE AGENCY'S DATABASE, AND THE AUDIT ROW WOULD HAVE SAID NOBODY DID IT.** `/portal/requests/new` lets a contact submit a `WorkItem(kind = REQUEST, source = PORTAL)` that lands CLIENT_VISIBLE in the project's hidden TRIAGE state. The memo's slice 6 is three features (request intake, contact "Done", comments); this is the first, split out because each needs its own census check, its own fresh review and its own CI read. Gates, decisions and what is owed are below. Both fresh reviews have run and their record is below.

**THE FINDING WORTH THE INK: `record()` DERIVES THE ACTOR FROM THE TRANSACTION'S PRINCIPAL, AND A BROKERED WRITE'S PRINCIPAL IS `system`.** AUTHZ.md §8's brokered-write rule says the write carries "an `AuditEvent` naming the contact as actor". It could not: `withTenant(tenantId, {type:'system'})` is what "brokered" MEANS, so the row would have come out `actorType: SYSTEM, actorId: null` — in the ONE event family whose actor is not an employee, on the only thing a client can do in this product. Closed by `AuditInput.brokeredForContactId`, honoured **only inside a system transaction and throwing otherwise**: a member passing it would be attributing their own act to a client, in the one table SECURITY.md §7 treats as evidentiary. Both directions are measured (`portal-writes.dbtest.ts`), because a deny-only test would pass just as well if the field had been deleted.

**FIVE DECISIONS TAKEN WITHOUT THE FOUNDER — the session is non-interactive and the alternative was delivering nothing. Each is one edit from being inverted.** *(1)* **The rate limit is a Postgres count, not `src/ratelimit`.** That limiter fails OPEN when Upstash is unconfigured, which it is and is documented to be, so keying the intake on it would have shipped a control that does nothing in the only deployment that exists, with a green test beside it — and `src/ratelimit`'s own header names the alternative for exactly this case ("the fail-CLOSED budgets in this product are the Postgres counters"). Five per contact per fifteen minutes, counted in the writer's own transaction behind a per-contact advisory lock so two simultaneous submits cannot both see N−1. *(2)* **The form is a ROUTE, not a section of `/portal`.** `/portal`'s body is `<PortalHome>`, the component `/view-as` renders too and byte-compares in CI; a form there would show a MEMBER a submit button that can only bounce them to the client sign-in page. The LINK is shared (a link is genuinely part of what the client sees) and renders only when the submit would work. *(3)* **The body is PLAIN TEXT, never ProseMirror JSON.** The editor's schema check runs in the member app, not on this plane, so admitting a document would mean admitting whatever a client's browser sent into a `jsonb` column employees render; it lands in `descriptionText` and `description` stays NULL. *(4)* **The row is born CLIENT_VISIBLE** — the only row in the product that is, and deliberate rather than an exception to the INTERNAL default: a request the submitter cannot read back is a form that ate their words. *(5)* **Notification receivers are the project's `MemberProject` members plus its lead, ACTIVE only.** A tenant whose members reach projects through a tenant-wide role has none, so a request there lands in triage with nobody TOLD — recorded as owed rather than widened, because "every member who could read the project" means resolving scope for a whole tenant inside an intake transaction.

**THE TRIPWIRE FORCED A FILE SPLIT, AND THE SPLIT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER RATHER THAN AN EVASION.** `portal-projections.test.ts` greps the TEXT of every portal-surface file — `portal-writes.ts` included, since slice 46 — for internal column names, and `stateId` is on that list. A create that lands a row in a workflow state has to name one. So the INSERT lives in `src/modules/work/requests.ts` (beside the other work services, where the member-side triage verb will join it) and `portal-writes.ts` keeps the part that must be read as a unit: who is allowed, under which principal, with which trail. Keeping the forbidden list ABSOLUTE was judged worth more than the inlining; a reviewer who disagrees should say so rather than assume it went unnoticed. The same grep also went red, exactly once, on the word **"cost"** in a docblock — slice 46's lesson arriving on schedule.

**THE PLANE NEEDED ITS OWN ACTION RUNNER, AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE STOPPED THE FIRST ONE REACHING FOR `runAction`.** `src/lib/server-actions.ts` maps an `AuthzError` to three DISTINCT messages, because on the member plane the reader is the agency. On the contact plane NOT_ENTITLED names the agency's plan, DISABLED_BY_TENANT names a switch somebody threw, and FORBIDDEN against NOT_FOUND maps which projects exist. `src/portal/action.ts` is `portalReadOrNull`'s bargain applied to writes: every `AuthzError` is ONE message with the reason in the server log, and a `DomainError` is **allow-listed** rather than passed through — today `REQUEST_RATE_LIMITED` and `INVALID_INPUT`, both facts about the READER. `action.test.ts` enumerates every code the product has copy for and asserts exactly two get through, which is the assertion that catches a service growing a refusal next year with no diff on that file.

**FOUR STRUCTURAL PINS, ALL MUTATION-CHECKED.** `src/portal/brokered-writes.test.ts`: every `withTenant` in a `portal-writes.ts` takes an INLINE `{type:'system'}`; `authorizePortal` is called before it opens (an ORDERING assertion on the function's own AST BODY — a whole-file `indexOf` is satisfied by the import at the top, which is slice 48's correction twice over); the audit row names the contact INSIDE that callback; and only the audit seam and the brokers may so much as mention `brokeredForContactId`. Plus: no `(portal)` route may import `runAction`/`runForm`, and every portal server action must call `requirePortalContext()` and may not read an identity out of its `FormData`. **Every assertion reads the AST rather than the text, and the first cut proved why in one run**: a `withTenant(tenantId, {type:'system'})` written inside a DOCBLOCK failed the pin for quoting the rule it enforces, and a paragraph saying "`runPortalForm` rather than `runForm`" was reported as reaching for `runForm`. Three mutations were driven and all three went red — a member principal on the write, a dropped `brokeredForContactId`, and the authorization moved inside the transaction — and a fourth on the disclosure list (adding `ARCHIVED`) reddened `action.test.ts`.

**THE CENSUS IS UNCHANGED, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE.** `work_item` stays closed to a contact principal in every command — no policy dropped, no migration touching RLS — and the behavioural half is in the dbtest: a contact principal handed a transaction and asked to INSERT the very row the intake creates is refused. If it were not, every forced column in `requests.ts` would be a suggestion.

**TWO LAYERS DISAGREE ON PURPOSE, AND A TEST SAYS SO.** `project`'s `portal_gate` is `client_id = app.client_id AND portal_enabled` with no archive term, so `authorizePortal`'s project ref ADMITS an archived project; it is `createRequest`'s own re-read under the system principal that refuses it with `ARCHIVED`. A reviewer reading only the policy would conclude the opposite. The contact never learns which of the two refused: `ARCHIVED` is not on the disclosure list.

**WHAT THE TWO FRESH REVIEWS TOOK OFF IT — one HIGH, and it was a TEST that could not fail.** The code review found that the dbtest three documents cite as "the whole justification for brokering" — a contact principal handed a transaction and asked to INSERT a `work_item` — **was answered by a TRIGGER, not by the policy**. `work_item_state_sync` is BEFORE INSERT and resolves `state_id` against `workflow_state`, a class-A table carrying `portal_deny`, so under a contact principal that lookup finds nothing *even for the project's real triage state*: the trigger raises before RLS's WITH CHECK is ever evaluated, and a bare `.rejects.toThrow()` was satisfied by it. **Replace `portal_gate`'s WITH CHECK with `WITH CHECK (true)` — opening the contact-writable census on the product's biggest table — and all twenty tests stayed green.** Verified against the migration before acting on it, and it is structural rather than incidental: on `work_item` that policy is unreachable by INSERT from a contact, whatever the test does. The claim now rests on two cases where the policy IS reachable — a `work_item_activity` INSERT, which carries the same WITH CHECK and whose only BEFORE trigger (`stamp_portal_enabled`) reads `project` and COALESCEs rather than raising, asserted on `/row-level security/` **with a system-principal positive control** so "the policy refused it" is distinguishable from "the row was malformed"; and a DELETE of the contact's OWN request, which is the row they come closest to reaching — `portal_no_delete` is a USING deny, so the refusal is a COUNT OF ZERO and not an exception, and a test that only asserted `rejects` would have passed whether the policy existed or not. The `work_item` case stays, asserting the trigger's own message, and its comment now records what it does *not* prove.

**THE SECURITY REVIEW RETURNED NO CRITICAL AND NO HIGH**, traced nine areas clean with evidence (the read path backstopped by RLS independently of the application code, the system-principal window and every ownership column derived from a row rather than an argument, the audit attribution in both directions, denial disclosure across every new path, the budget's exactness and fail-closed direction, input handling end to end, the migration, PII and logging, and that nothing existing was weakened to make the new code pass), and raised three MEDIUM and seven LOW. Both reviews independently found the two biggest ones.

**TAKEN (15).** *(a)* **A latent cross-client WRITE.** `projectId` was never checked for emptiness, Prisma silently drops an `undefined` `where`, and the project re-read runs under the SYSTEM principal where every portal policy is satisfied — so an `undefined` would have resolved an arbitrary project **of the whole tenant, possibly another client's**, and filed one client's words into it, born CLIENT_VISIBLE. Unreachable from today's only caller (a `FormData` action always passes a string) and guarded in all three places anyway, because the broker is on the public barrel and the repo already has a memory of this exact Prisma trap. *(b)* **The lock waits were unbounded** on the one path a client can drive. The intake takes two advisory locks, and this repo MEASURED that Prisma's transaction budget does not end a statement the database has parked (a blocked fan-out under a 3 s budget was still waiting past 30 s) — so a submission could park indefinitely while holding that contact's own budget lock, behind a member's bulk edit. It now takes `setPortalEnabled`'s shape exactly: `lockTimeoutMs`, `retryOnContention`, and a visible `REQUEST_BUSY` when the attempts are spent, which is deliberately NOT disclosable. *(c)* **The limiter capped rows, not requests** — an over-budget contact could still pay for two transactions and a lock per POST. A `portal.request_create` bucket now sits in front; it is a no-op until Upstash is provisioned, and that is acceptable *only* because fail-open in front of fail-closed is the opposite of the arrangement `requests.ts` rejects. *(d)* **Two `INVALID_INPUT` raises were facts about the AGENCY** ("project has no triage state", "no clock") on a code that is on the disclosure allow-list, whose rule is "something the reader themself did" — both are invariant violations and now throw plainly to the error boundary. *(e)* **`brokeredForContactId` was checked by principal TYPE only**, and the guard keyed on `undefined` while the row build keyed on truthiness — so `""` passed the guard, fell through to `actorType: SYSTEM` and wrote `actorId: ""`, a row that is neither. One condition and a UUID check. *(f)* **`requests.ts` was outside BOTH tiers of the portal tripwire** — the file doing the actual INSERT, which the split had moved there precisely to keep the forbidden-NAME list absolute. It joins the STRUCTURAL tier (AST, fires on real select keys) and stays out of the TEXT one, exactly as `view-as` already does and for the same reason; the widening is pinned, and mutation-checked — a select-less `findFirst` there now fails. *(g)* **Two of `brokered-writes.test.ts`'s own pins read the body's TEXT, comments included**, which its docblock claimed none of them did: deleting `brokeredForContactId` while leaving the comment that names it left the pin green. They read AST positions and the real property now, and the mutation goes red. *(h)* **`client-graph.test.ts`'s mutation check did not plant the shape it claimed** — it probed a file that imports `@/db` on its own second line, a one-hop trail with no barrel, so a resolver that had regressed to direct imports would have passed. It plants the multi-hop path through the barrel now. *(i)* **`PortalHome` ran two transactions in `Promise.all`**, where a non-`AuthzError` from both would leave the second an unhandled rejection; sequential. *(j)* A **docblock in `src/clients/view-as.ts` became false** with this diff ("`record` stamps `actorType` … never from its input"). *(k)* The **advisory-lock "namespace" claim was wrong** — one 64-bit space, `hashtext` is 32-bit, the prefixes change the input and not the namespace; the cycle conclusion survives for a better reason (nothing takes the two keys in the other order). *(l)* The **Swedish rate-limit copy said "wait a minute"** against a 15-minute window, so a client following it literally retries into the identical refusal — which on this plane is indistinguishable from a broken form. *(m)* A comment **misdescribed what notification `params` are for** (the inbox rebuilds its link from ids under the receiver's principal and never reads them; it is the EMAIL renderer that consumes them, outside this product). *(n)* The **e2e cleanup was scoped by KIND**, so the first triage-lane fixture would have been silently deleted by an unrelated spec's `afterAll`; scoped in time to the run. *(o)* **"Born CLIENT_VISIBLE so the submitter can read it back" was broader than what ships** — `listPortalTasks` never projects `descriptionText`, so they read the title, not their paragraph.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT TAKEN (2).** *(a)* **A timing differential.** An ARCHIVED project of the contact's own client passes `authorizePortal` (no archive term in the policy) and is refused a whole transaction later than an unreachable one — same bytes, different latency. Not closed: an archived project never appears in the picker, so there is nothing to compare against, and moving the check earlier means teaching the generic `authorizePortal` about archives. The comment that overclaimed indistinguishability is corrected instead. *(b)* **`brokeredForContactId` is not proved to name a contact of this tenant.** That is a read in the audit hot path; the shape check plus `brokered-writes.test.ts`'s restriction on who may name the field at all is the control, and it is written down as the limit rather than implied.

**AND ONE OBSERVATION THAT IS THE FOUNDER'S, NOT THE CODE'S: every contact of a client can read every other contact's request.** `portal_gate` on `work_item` is CLIENT-scoped, not submitter-scoped, so any ACTIVE contact of the same client sees a colleague's request (its title today; its body the moment a portal detail view ships). That is consistent with the product's model — the portal is the client's, not the person's — and this slice is the first place it can matter. If a request should be private to its submitter, that is a policy term and a decision, not a projection tweak.

**TWO TRAPS THIS SESSION PAID FOR, worth the ink because both cost real time.** `tsc --noEmit` runs with `incremental: true`, so `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` **caches the type of `messages/en.json`**: a `DomainErrorCode` added with its copy in the same edit reported a phantom "not assignable" failure until the cache was deleted. (The coupling itself is excellent — the type system will not let a code exist without copy in both locales — but the stale cache makes it look like the copy is missing when it is not.) And the Bash tool's heredoc trap bit three more times on long patch scripts, exactly as AGENTS.md records: every patch since is a file written with `Write` and then run.

**A STANDING DEPRECATION THE WHOLE DB SUITE ALREADY TRIPS, found by chasing it to the wrong door first.** `pg` prints *"Calling client.query() when the client is already executing a query is deprecated and will be removed in pg@9.0"* on many dbtest runs. I assumed it was this slice's `Promise.all` in `requestReceivers`, rewrote that read, and the warning stayed — so I ran an untouched file, **`work.dbtest.ts`, which emits it too**. It is PRE-EXISTING and comes from the codebase's deliberate `Promise.all` over one interactive transaction (`getItemDetail` fans nine reads that way, and its own comment explains why). Two things follow. **It is not a defect today** — a transaction is one connection, so `pg` queues the statements and the answers are correct — but **it is an ERROR in pg@9**, so every one of those sites becomes a runtime failure at that upgrade, and nothing in the repo records it. And the reason it was nearly mis-attributed is that the full `test:db` output was piped through `tail -60`, which cut the one line that would have shown it firing before this slice existed: **AGENTS.md's "check exit codes, not just output" has a twin — do not truncate the stream you are about to draw a conclusion from.** The receiver read is sequential now anyway, because on one connection the parallel form buys nothing.

**AND A PROCESS MISTAKE WORTH MORE THAN THE BUG IT HID: I EDITED `src/` WHILE A 29-MINUTE `test:db` RUN WAS IN FLIGHT.** The run came back 44 files green and ONE failure — this slice's own new TOCTOU case, which had reached disk before the code it tests did. Nothing was wrong with either; the result was simply not a result. **A `test:db` run is a measurement of a tree, and the tree has to hold still for half an hour.** The final gate below is a clean full run on the committed tree.

**GATES AND EVIDENCE.** Typecheck ✓, ESLint `src e2e scripts --max-warnings 0` → 0. Unit **77 files / 1228 passed / 1 skipped** (+22 over slice 48: the three new test files and the widened pins). `pnpm build` ✓ with `/portal/requests/new` dynamic (ƒ), and the browser chunks re-scanned after the leaf fix — `portalAuthSecret`, `DATABASE_URL`, `app_runtime`, `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, `reportedByContactId`, `brokeredForContactId`, `envSchema` and `util/types` all at **0 chunks**. `portal-writes.dbtest.ts` **22 passed**. Full `test:db` **45 files / 596 passed, 1 failed** — and the one failure is `ordering.dbtest.ts`'s twelve-way concurrency test at **5386 ms against the 5000 ms interactive budget**, which is the flake AGENTS.md already records at 5416 ms *with every change reverted*; re-run at `DB_TX_TIMEOUT_MS=20000` it is **17/17**, and the CI job runs a Postgres container on the runner where the link does not exist.

**THE LOCAL FULL E2E DIED OF THE MACHINE, AND THE EXIT CODE SAYS SO RATHER THAN A GUESS.** 123 passed, 1 skipped, **13 failed** — twelve of `work.spec.ts` and the Swedish width walk. Every one of the thirteen is `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, and the one test that failed on its own assertion first (a bulk archive, 48.7 s) is the one the server died *during*; everything after it failed in ~2.3 s against nothing. The server's last line is `[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 3221226505` — `0xC0000409`, Windows fail-fast, which on this machine is the memory signature PLAN already carries (a build plus five subagents exceeded the commit limit twice in one afternoon). **So the standing trap was worked in its own order**: `error-context.md` opened first, and what it showed was not the wrong app answering on the port — it was no app at all. `work.spec.ts` re-run alone on 3457: **15/15**. The slice's own spec passed inside the full run, as did `view-as` and the 204-shot visual sweep.

**AND THE RE-RUN FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN CLEANUP, which is the only reason the red run was worth the hour.** The code review had asked for the e2e cleanup to be scoped rather than deleting every `kind=REQUEST` row of the shared tenant; the first fix scoped it by `createdAt >= <when this run started>` — **the wrong instrument, and the same two-clocks mistake the rate budget had just been corrected for.** The rows are stamped by Postgres and the cutoff came from the test runner's clock, so a few seconds of skew against Neon would have made the cleanup delete NOTHING and leave a request sitting in the shared project's backlog for the visual sweep and the Swedish width ratchet — exactly the cross-spec contamination the scoping exists to prevent, arriving through the fix for it. It is keyed on the SUBMITTER now (this harness can sign in as exactly one contact, so "requests reported by that contact" is precisely the set this spec can create) with no clock in it at all. **Measured rather than reasoned:** `portal-requests` + `visibility` + `zz-swedish-widths` run together, in that order, **9 passed** — the width ratchet runs after the submit and stays green, which a leftover row would have broken.

**WHAT THE CI RUN HAS TO SETTLE**, stated so the next session reads it first: the full browser harness end to end. Local cannot give it today, and CI runs it in ~11 minutes on a container with none of this machine's memory problem. If it goes broadly red there, `work.spec.ts` is the file to look at and `error-context.md` is the first thing to open — but the two candidates AGENTS.md already names (the wrong app on the port; a spec leaving shared state behind) are both ruled out above by evidence rather than by argument.

**WHAT IS OWED, stated so the next slice does not have to rediscover it.** **(0) ~~A QUESTION THAT MUST BE ASKED~~ — CLOSED 2026-09-22, asked and answered by the founder. A portal request IS visible to the submitter's COLLEAGUES**, and `work_item`'s client-scoped `portal_gate` therefore stands unchanged (no `reported_by_contact_id` term). Reasons and the three places it is now recorded are at the top of this section. *Kept here rather than deleted because the shape of the question is the useful part: it was decided BEFORE any contact could hold a session, which made it free; a per-contact predicate after invites ship would have had to hide rows people had already read.* (1) ~~**The TRIAGE LANE**~~ — **DONE 2026-09-22, both commits** (at the top of this section). Its SERVER half shipped (slice 6b, first commit, at the top of this section): the four verbs, the client-readable decline reason, `work_item:triage` off the unenforced list, and the silent-vanish closed. and the SURFACE followed in the second commit: the lane at `/projects/[key]/triage`, the `triage` scope mounted for the first time, the server actions, the e2e round trip, and the drop-target fix (`canItemEnterState`). **What is still owed from this area is the `/home` triage count**, which UI.md rule 8 names and which has waited for a writer since 2W — there is one now. (2) **A request notifies nobody in a tenant with no `MemberProject` rows** (decision 5 above). **And a TRIAGE OUTCOME notifies nobody at all** (new, 2026-09-22): the submitting contact is not told their request was accepted or declined, because contacts have no notification channel in v1 — no `ContactNotificationPreference`, no SES production access — and building one inside a triage slice would mean designing the contact's whole email identity in passing. They learn it from the portal, which this slice makes truthful. The decline reason is written to be read cold, for that reason. (2b) **THREE RESIDUES SLICE 6b LEAVES ON PURPOSE, each checked and each left rather than missed.** *(i)* ~~**An ARCHIVED request takes its answer with it.**~~ **CLOSED 2026-09-22 — the founder chose to keep them.** `archivedAt` moved from the whole `where` into the LIVE-WORK branch only, so archiving hides a task in progress as it always has and no longer deletes the explanation a client was given. The PROJECT archive still hides everything. *This residue was recorded as "left because the answer was already delivered"; asking turned out to be worth more than the disposition.* *(ii)* **Triage works on an ARCHIVED PROJECT's request**, which follows the work module's own convention rather than diverging inside a triage slice: only `projects/*` services refuse on archive, while `changeState`, `createItem` and `updateItemFields` do not. The consequence is that the answer is written to a list the client cannot currently read (the projection filters the project's archive). *(iii)* **`duplicate_of_id` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and is now REACHABLE for the first time** — nothing wrote it before this slice. *(**Corrected by both fresh reviews, 2026-09-22.** This first read "no hard-delete path exists in the product, so this bites only the Phase-8 purge job" — true of `src/`, **false of the harness**: `removeTenant` in `e2e/fixtures/seed-cli.ts` hard-deletes `work_item` and handled only the `parent_id` self-FK, so one orphan holding a duplicate would have thrown `23503` and, because `sweepDbtests` loops with no try/catch, aborted the entire sweep. Fixed there; the Phase-8 purge job still owes the same clear.)* **The lesson is the residue, not the FK:** a disposition that says "no path exists in the product" has not checked `e2e/` or `scripts/`. (2c) **A HARD CONSTRAINT ON THE FIRST PORTAL ACTIVITY PROJECTION, recorded now because the rows are being written now** (security review F3). Every accept and every decline writes a **CLIENT_VISIBLE** `WorkItemActivity` row through `transitionState` — `field: "stateCategory"`, `oldValue: "TRIAGE"`, `newValue: "CANCELLED"`, and `oldRef`/`newRef` carrying two `workflow_state` ids. It is permitted (the field is on `writeActivity`'s portal-safe list and the CHECK's) and there is **no live leak**, because no portal projection reads activity. But the raw strings are the agency's internal vocabulary — the very word UI.md §11 forbids on a client's screen — and the ids are on `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS`/`PORTAL_NEVER_SELECTED`. **Whoever ships a portal history view must map the categories and must never publish `oldValue`/`newValue`/`oldRef`/`newRef` raw.** The shape predates this slice (BACKLOG→TODO has it too); what is new is that it is now guaranteed on the one row type a client most wants history for. (2d) ~~**`work_item:triage` is CME — an EMPLOYEE can publish prose to a client**~~ — **ANSWERED 2026-09-22: only managers may decline.** New code `work_item:triage_decline` (C M); details at the top of this section. (2e) **A RELEASE CARRYING TEMPLATE_VERSION 6 OWES A FULL `prisma/seed.ts` RUN** — the catalogue half is done (`scripts/seed-catalog.ts`), the B3 propagation half writes to every existing tenant and is the founder's. (3) **No visual-sweep stop for `/portal/requests/new`** — same reasoning as `/view-as` in slice 48: it needs a driven contact session and a stop-count update across five prose sites that already disagree with each other, and the e2e drives the whole flow. (4) **`Contact` has no per-contact capability toggles**, so "this client may read but not ask" is not expressible; both v1 profiles hold `portal.request.create`, which is why the refusal case in the dbtest uses a contact who is not ACTIVE rather than one without the verb. (5) **No `prisma/seed.ts` step is owed for this release** — no permission code was added and the catalogue is untouched; the one migration is an INDEX (`work_item(tenant_id, reported_by_contact_id, created_at)`), DDL only, so no `neon-smoke` run is owed either.

**MODEL AND EFFORT FOR WHAT COMES NEXT:** the triage lane's SERVER half is done; its **surface** wants Opus 5 at high for the same reason the whole slice did — a keyboard scope that has never been mounted, a Radix layer for the reason field, and an optimistic list whose rows leave it. The keyboard half in particular is where this repo's standing traps cluster (the `G`-sequence race, cmdk's swallowed keys, the focus-return rules), and none of them is visible from the source alone. Phase 3 otherwise remains what the memo's §4.5 asked for: `/security-review` on **every** slice regardless of what the diff appears to touch.


**PUSHED AND GREEN: slice 48 is `99e1d72`; CI run [35627296832](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/35627296832) — BOTH JOBS `success`.** On the service container: unit **74 files / 1207 passed / 1 skipped**, `test:db` **44 files / 575 passed, 0 failed** — identical to the local numbers, including `view-as.dbtest.ts` — and the browser harness **134 passed / 1 skipped in 11.6 min, no flaky** (+2 over slice 47's 132, which is exactly `e2e/view-as.spec.ts`). The `test:db` job builds from an EMPTY database, so it also proves the new `session.view_as_contact_id` migration applies cleanly from scratch and that the slice needed no catalogue bump: `project:manage_portal` was already seeded by slice 47, so **no `prisma/seed.ts` step is owed for this release** — unlike slice 47, which made the emergency switch unreachable until the seed ran.

**AND THE E2E DID NOT FLAKE ON CI, WHICH IS THE ONE THING WORTH WATCHING NEXT TIME.** `view-as.spec.ts` writes `User.locale` on the shared seeded member and restores it in `afterAll` rather than a `finally` — a code review's finding, taken precisely because a Playwright TEST TIMEOUT abandons the body and a `finally`'s awaits fail immediately, which would have handed every alphabetically-later spec (`visibility`, `visual`, `zz-swedish-widths`) a Swedish UI. CI ran it in the same worker as all 134 and the walk stayed green, so the arrangement holds under the real ordering; if a future run ever goes broadly red across unrelated surfaces, **this spec's locale restore is the first thing to check**, alongside the port question AGENTS.md already records.

**2026-09-21 — SLICE 48 (memo slice 5): VIEW-AS-CONTACT — and the byte comparison is the only reason any of it can be believed.** `/view-as` lets a member holding `project:manage_portal` walk a CLIENT'S portal as one named contact, under their own session, through a synthesised `PortalPrincipal`. SECURITY.md §5.1's vector table asked for four things and all four shipped: the same projection functions, a red banner, `project.viewed_as_contact` audited, and **output byte-compared to a real contact session in CI**. Gates, both fresh reviews and the decisions the founder should confirm are below.

**FIVE DECISIONS TAKEN WITHOUT THE FOUNDER, because the session was non-interactive and the alternative was delivering nothing. Each is one edit from being inverted.** *(1)* **It spans the CLIENT, not one project.** What a contact sees is their portal, and a project-narrowed view would be slice 4's panel a second time — it could never be byte-identical to anything, because no contact request produces one. *(2)* **The gate that makes that safe is `assertInScope({ clientId })` with `lifted` LEFT OFF** — a DIRECT client assignment or `client:view_all`, never the project→client lift, which is the exact predicate "this member already reaches everything this mode will show". *(3)* **The mode is a session pointer** (`Session.viewAsContactId`), not a cookie: a cookie is client-held, so a member could sit inside the mode with no audit row, and that is the one failure an audited control cannot have. *(4)* **The audit action stays `project.viewed_as_contact`.** I nearly renamed it to `portal.*` for the client-wide act and was wrong: the `portal.*` audit family means contact-CAUSED writes (`portal.request_created`, `portal.comment_created`, `portal.task_completed`), and `portal.area.verb` is the capability namespace. *(5)* **Exit goes to `/home` with no return path** — the only way to have one is a redirect parameter on a security-sensitive route.

**THE THREE FINDINGS THAT CAME FROM RUNNING THINGS, NOT FROM READING THEM.** *(a)* **`Session.viewAsContactId` was invisible.** The column was written and read back as `undefined`, `/view-as` concluded the member was not in the mode and redirected home — nothing failed, nothing logged. The adapter strips keys not declared in `SESSION_ADDITIONAL_FIELDS` (`betterauth-plane-traps`, the same failure that made `/ops` unreachable on 2026-09-09). Found by the e2e, not by any reading. *(b)* **The audit row could be incoherent.** An owner holds `client:view_all`, so `assertInScope` accepted Acme's PROJECT beside Beta's CONTACT, and the row would have read "from Acme's project, viewed as a contact of Beta" — a sentence describing nothing that happened. Found by a dbtest written to assert the opposite. The entry project must now belong to the contact's own client. *(c)* **My own prose broke my own tripwires three times** — `not.toContain("listPortalTasks")` went red on the docblock explaining the arrangement, and an `indexOf` for `<PortalHome>` found the paragraph before the JSX. All structural now (imports, attributes, function bodies), which is slice 46's "red for the wrong reason" lesson learned a fourth time.

**TWELVE MUTATION CHECKS WITH GREEN CONTROLS, AND ONE CAUGHT MY OWN TEST MEASURING NOTHING.** The locale-order pin compared `indexOf("isViewAsRequest")` against the WHOLE FILE, so the import at the top satisfied it and deleting the arm entirely left it green; it is sliced to `resolveLocale`'s own body now and fails at one attempt. Nine unit (proxy prefix anchoring, header deletion, the locale arm twice, the timezone arm, component sharing, the principal closed set, the banner boundary, the frame marker, a select-less read under `/view-as`) and three dbtest (the `lifted` arm, the project↔client pairing, admission). **The headline claim is measured rather than asserted:** with the locale pin removed the e2e byte comparison fails on every chrome string — "Shared with you" vs "Delat med dig", "Due Oct 1, 2026" vs "Klart senast 1 okt. 2026" — while the task titles, which are DATA, stay identical. **One mutation deliberately still passes and is recorded rather than hidden:** swapping `contact.tenantId` for the caller's argument in `synthesiseContactPrincipal` changes nothing, because the belt three lines above proves them equal. The safety is the belt; reading the row is legibility.

**THE ARCHITECTURE DECISION WORTH THE INK: the member plane now has ONE principal builder, not two.** View-as needed to synthesise a `PortalPrincipal` and the obvious move was a third entry in `portal-view-as.test.ts`'s closed set. Instead `src/portal/synthesise.ts` became the single member-plane builder and slice 4's preview moved onto it, so the set stays at TWO — `portal/context.ts` for the contact plane, `portal/synthesise.ts` for the member plane. It takes no tenant id to resolve gates from (it reads `contact.tenantId` off the row), which discharges by SIGNATURE the obligation `authorize.ts` had named for this slice. It also fixed a docblock that had been FALSE since slice 4 shipped ("only `requirePortalContext()` builds a `PortalPrincipal`") and a second `cache()` wrapper that would have doubled the gate round trips.

**THE LOCALE PIN, AND WHY IT IS KEYED ON THE ROUTE.** `src/proxy.ts` stamps an internal header on the `/view-as` prefix and DELETES any inbound copy everywhere else; `resolveLocale`/`resolveTimeZone` grow an arm above the member session. Keyed on the session POINTER instead, a member inside the mode in one tab would have found their own `/home` rendered in the client's language in another. **`src/i18n/request.ts` now honours an explicit locale**, which nothing in the product had ever passed — needed because the banner must render in the MEMBER'S language while the surface under it renders in the contact's. Two languages, one document.

**WHAT THE TWO FRESH REVIEWS TOOK OFF IT — one HIGH, measured in a build artefact rather than argued.** The code review read `.next/static/chunks` and found that a `"use client"` component importing `@/config` had shipped the env schema's field names, the `portalAuthSecret` derivation and a full `crypto-browserify` polyfill into a **444 KB browser chunk**, evaluated on every load of the Project → Portal page. No secret VALUE leaked (Next inlines only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`), and that is exactly why it would have stayed invisible — one REQUIRED field added to `envSchema` and the chunk throws `ZodError` at module evaluation with nothing failing server-side. Closed by `src/config/view-as.ts`, a leaf module that imports nothing, re-exported from `./index.ts`. **Measured after: 444,241 bytes → 12,377, all four markers gone.** Security returned **no CRITICAL and no HIGH**, cleared nine areas on traced evidence (the scope gate with no path around it, no writer of the pointer outside the audited action, the principal's tenant, the header's real reach, plane confinement, PII and audit metadata, denial disclosure, the comparison's boundary, the migration's grants) and raised eleven lower items.

**TAKEN FROM THE REVIEWS (16).** The banner and exit button now render in the MEMBER'S language — they were in the client's, which made the one warning that says "you are looking at somebody else's screen" a sentence chosen for the client; the e2e locale restore moved out of a `finally`, where a Playwright test TIMEOUT would have abandoned it and handed the 204-shot visual walk a Swedish UI; the e2e non-vacuity guard now asserts shared TASK titles, because `toContain(contactName)` was satisfied by the chrome's "Signed in as" line alone and two empty states would have compared equal forever; the three plane-boundary REWRITES now sanitise the header too (three docblocks claimed the strip was universal when it covered only the forwards); `pass()` no longer clones the header set on 100% of traffic; the timezone pin became an ORDERING assertion (it was a proximity regex that would have survived the arm moving below the member session, and the e2e cannot see that arm at all — Playwright pins the same zone on both sides); `MFA_REQUIRED` is re-thrown rather than swallowed into a silent bounce; the `projectKey` parameter is gone (caller data reaching a redirect builder, in the file whose own docblock boasts it carries no return path); the belt at the View-as call site compares two independently-sourced tenant ids instead of one value twice; `src/clients/view-as.ts` joined both tripwire tiers, verified clean of all 21 forbidden identifiers first; a negative PERMISSION test and a principal FIELD-SET pin joined the dbtest; the button got `self-start` (a flex child is stretched, so it spanned the whole column and no gate could see it); and four false sentences were corrected — a docblock claiming the page clears the pointer, a `revalidatePath` justified by a locale claim that is keyed on the route, a migration comment naming the wrong audit namespace, and two references to `src/i18n/view-as.ts`, a file that does not exist.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT TAKEN (3); the one that is the founder's belongs to the INVITE slice, not to this one.** *(a)* **The permission axis is not closed.** `listPortalTasks` runs under the contact principal and consults no member permission, so a custom role with `project:manage_portal` plus a direct client assignment but `work_item:view` tombstoned reads that client's CLIENT_VISIBLE titles and dates. Unreachable with seeded templates (C and M hold both), everything shown is data the agency published to that client, and AUTHZ.md now says the "exact predicate" claim holds on the SCOPE axis only — the same shape as slice 4's contact-PII disposition. *(b)* **`project.view_as_ended` does not exist, and on a second look it should probably stay that way.** The first version of this note said "add it now or never" and was wrong in both halves, so the corrected reasoning is here rather than the slogan. **NOT NOW:** no product code path activates a contact — the only non-test write of `portalStatus: "ACTIVE"` is a `where` filter in `portal-preview.ts` — and `authorizeViewAs` demands ACTIVE + invited + verified, so **the mode cannot be entered in production at all until the invite slice ships**. The interim holds no rows to lose. **NOT NEVER:** the catalogue is static TypeScript with no migration, so adding it is exactly as cheap on any later day. **AND PROBABLY NOT AT ALL**, which is the part that actually decides it: an "ended" row can only be written when the member clicks Exit, while a closed tab, an expired session, a sign-out or a plain navigation away all leave the pointer set and emit nothing — so the pair would be `started` always and `ended` sometimes, and a reader would take a missing `ended` to mean "still inside". That is worse than entry-only. `impersonation.started`/`ended` is not the precedent it looks like: platform impersonation is time-boxed and explicitly terminated, and View-as has no such property. Recording it would also force `requireTenantContext()` + `withTenant` onto `exitViewAsAction` — the one path deliberately built with no authorization and an `updateMany`, so that a member who has just LOST the permission can still get out. **If duration is ever wanted, stamp the entry with an expiry (or give the pointer a TTL) and derive the window; do not pair an event that cannot reliably fire.** Founder's call, and the moment for it is the invite slice, not today. *(c)* **The pointer has no TTL** — a member who enters, navigates away and returns an hour later is back inside on the original row, so the row counts MODE ACTIVATIONS rather than visits. Stated in the code rather than implied.

**AND TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT.** There is **no visual-sweep stop** for `/view-as`: it needs a driven session pointer AND a stop-count update across five prose sites (UI.md, RUNBOOK.md ×2, PLAN.md, AGENTS.md — which a review found already disagree with each other at 48/51/52 stops), and the e2e drives the whole flow already. And `scripts/preview-as-contact.ts` was **kept, not retired** — it probes more tables than the product projects (documents, versions, services, plus a cross-client control) — but its header no longer claims to be "View as client", because it reads rows directly and sits in neither tripwire tier: it answers "is my RLS doing what I think", never "what can a client see".

**GATES AND EVIDENCE.** Typecheck ✓, ESLint `src e2e scripts --max-warnings 0` → 0. Unit **74 files / 1207 passed / 1 skipped**. `test:db` **44 files / 575 passed, 0 failed** (+1 file, +16 tests over slice 47’s 43/559 — exactly the new dbtest; 1778 s, well over the documented ~16 min, on a loaded machine and the transatlantic link). `pnpm build` ✓ with `/view-as` dynamic (ƒ). `view-as.dbtest.ts` **16 passed**; `e2e/view-as.spec.ts` **2 passed** on `E2E_PORT=3457 E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3457`. **One unit failure was chased and disproved rather than explained away:** `import-boundary.test.ts` timed out at its 5 s budget inside the full suite while passing in isolation — it reproduced on a STASHED (clean) tree, so it is a pre-existing timing sensitivity under machine load, not this diff, and it passed on the next run. The load was ten leaked Playwright/vitest processes from this session's own runs; they were left alone rather than killed blind, because three of them were the harness's own MCP servers.

**PUSHED AND GREEN: slice 47 is `bc18363`; CI run [35605436012](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/35605436012) — BOTH JOBS `success`.** On the service container: unit **74 files / 1197 passed / 1 skipped**, `test:db` **43 files / 559 passed, 0 failed**, browser harness **132 passed in 11.2 min, no flaky** — identical to the local numbers, `ordering.dbtest.ts` included, which is the first run of that file since the 50-mover cut. The `test:db` job builds from an EMPTY database, so it also proves the migration-free permission code reaches a fresh install through `prisma/seed.ts` exactly as RUNBOOK.md now says a release must.

**2026-09-21 — SLICE 47 (memo slice 4): PROJECT → PORTAL, the master switch beside what the switch publishes — AND THE TAB'S FIRST GATE WAS THE WRONG HALF OF §5.** `/projects/[key]/portal` holds `Project.portalEnabled`, `hoursSharingMode`, a blocker list, an audience card, and "what the client sees": `listPortalTasks` run under a SYNTHESISED contact principal and drawn by the portal's own components. `project:manage_portal` is in the catalogue and enforced (TV5, catalog → 98). Gates and both fresh reviews below.

**THE FOUNDER'S THREE ANSWERS, asked before building the parts that depend on them.** *(1)* **Archiving a project KEEPS hiding its shared work** — slice 46's filter stands, and this tab is where it becomes visible from the member's side (a `PROJECT_ARCHIVED` blocker). *(2)* **A declined request will show as DECLINED with the agency's reason**, not vanish — the request-intake slice builds it; `PORTAL_TASK_CATEGORIES` and DATA_MODEL now carry the decision so that slice inherits it spelled. *(3)* **Four portal categories stay.** All three as recommended.

**THE FINDING OF THE SLICE, and a dbtest found it rather than a reading.** The first cut hid the tab behind `isAuthorized`, the shape every other conditional tab uses. `isAuthorized` runs gate 4 ONLY. `project:manage_portal` is module `portal`, so a tenant whose plan or preference had the portal off got a LIT tab, and the page behind it opens with `requireAccess`, which denies `DISABLED_BY_TENANT` — an error boundary on a route UI.md §3.1 says must be *hidden*. Closed by `hasAccess` (`src/entitlements/resolver.ts`), `requireAccess` as a boolean, short-circuited on the cap `loadProject` already resolved so the extra gate reads happen only for members who could hold the tab. **Its docblock names the one thing it must not be used for**: `MFA_REQUIRED` is an `AuthzError` too, so a ✦ surface asked about this way would vanish instead of prompting. The same measurement showed `MODULE_OFF` is reachable only through the **`work`** module — with `portal` off there is no tab to blocker-list — and that `src/entitlements/resolver.ts`'s own header had said "`core` and `portal` skip gates 2–3" since it was written, contradicted forty lines below by `ALWAYS_ON = {core}`. Corrected.

**THE PREVIEW IS NOT A PREVIEW, and that is the whole architecture.** SECURITY.md §5.1: *a separate preview renderer is how previews lie*. So `src/projects/portal-preview.ts` renders nothing and projects nothing — it authorises a member, picks a contact, synthesises that contact's principal and hands it to the SAME function `/portal` calls; the page draws the answer with the SAME components. **Two consequences worth stating.** The "off" state is produced by the database, not by an `if`: flip the switch and the trigger, the ten policies and `portal_gate` empty the panel. And the preview inherits every future narrowing of the projection for free, which is the property a second query cannot have.

**`listPortalTasks` GAINED `{ projectId }`, and it narrows TWO things.** The `where`, because a member's own scope can be a single project while a contact's is the whole client — filtering the answer afterwards would leave the client's other projects' names and titles in the render; and the `authorizePortal` REF, so a narrowed read of a portal-off project is REFUSED rather than filtered. The two layers disagree on purpose and a test says so: `project.portal_gate` has no archive term, so an ARCHIVED project is ADMITTED by the ref and then emptied by the projection's own filter. A reviewer reading only the policy would conclude the opposite.

**THE MEMBER PLANE OWNS THE REASON THE PORTAL PLANE MUST HIDE.** `portalReadOrNull` makes every refusal identical because a reason is a fact about the agency — and the member IS the agency, so this is the one surface where that rule would do harm. The tab lists every blocker that applies (`MODULE_OFF`, `PORTAL_OFF`, `PROJECT_ARCHIVED`, `NO_AUDIENCE`, `NOTHING_SHARED`), all of them, never the first, computed member-side from rows the member may read anyway. The two never share a code path, and both reviews traced that independently.

**THE HIGH, AND IT IS OPERATIONAL: A RELEASE WITHOUT THE SEED MAKES THE EMERGENCY SWITCH UNREACHABLE.** Found by the code review, and the security review reached the same place from the other end. A permission code is a `Permission` ROW the seed upserts plus a `RolePermission` grant `runTemplatePropagation` writes; there is no migration, and there never has been for a catalog bump. Moving the portal switch off `project:edit` (held by every template) onto a brand-new code therefore means that **between deploying this commit and running `prisma/seed.ts`, nobody in any tenant holds it** — tab hidden, switch FORBIDDEN. CI seeds fresh databases, so no gate can see it. **Nothing becomes newly VISIBLE to a client in that window** — a project already sharing goes on sharing — but it cannot be stopped from the UI. Dispositioned as documentation rather than a fallback code, because accepting `project:edit OR project:manage_portal` for one release would ship the C M E behaviour this slice exists to end, and a data migration for the catalogue would be the first of its kind for a step the RUNBOOK has always owned. **`docs/RUNBOOK.md` now says it in bold: run the seed WITH the release.** **FOUNDER: the dev database has the `permission` ROW (upserted from this session, catalogue only) but NOT the grants — run `pnpm exec tsx prisma/seed.ts` before expecting the tab.** Propagation was deliberately not run here: it walks every tenant and writes `RolePermission` + audit rows into `naxdor`, which AGENTS.md forbids an agent to touch.

**WHAT THE REVIEWS TOOK OFF IT — the security review's one MEDIUM, and 15 of the code review's 17.** *(a)* **The preview was outside BOTH tiers of `portal-projections.test.ts`** — named `portal-preview.ts`, outside `(portal)`, and never mentioning `withPortalRead` because it calls a function that does. The one file in the product that is a portal surface by CAPABILITY and by no convention at all, which is exactly the case slice 46's widening said the walk must follow; it is a named entry now, verified clean of every forbidden identifier so it cannot go red on prose the way the first widening did on the word "cost". *(b)* **`emailVerified` was missing from the audience filter.** `authorizePortal` admits ACTIVE + invited; `portalGateDecision` refuses an unverified address BEFORE any page runs. A client whose only contact had never verified was counted as "1 contact can sign in", with no `NO_AUDIENCE` blocker, while `/portal/login` turned them away. A blocker list is only worth reading if it is exhaustive. *(c)* **The empty panel spoke the CLIENT'S voice to the member** — "Nothing shared with you yet · ask your contact at the agency" — which is the FIRST state of this tab for most projects, since INTERNAL is the default. Rewriting that copy would fork the one component the tab's claim rests on; the fifth blocker `NOTHING_SHARED` carries the member-voiced explanation and the verb instead. *(d)* **The narrowing test measured nothing**: acme had exactly one live portal project in the fixture, so a `{ projectId }` that did nothing passed. A second project now exists inside that describe's own `beforeAll` — surgical, so the four tests above it that assert exact title sets and a single group still measure what they were written to. Mutation-checked: a no-op narrowing now fails it. *(e)* Both tripwires were **weaker than their prose** — `tx["workItem"]` evaded `delegatesOf` (the very evasion `portal-projections.test.ts` carries a control for), a spread evades `buildsPrincipal`, and the layout pin was a whitespace-exact string a Prettier reflow would have broken with a message naming no cause. Element access and a `PortalPrincipal` annotation are matched now, the pin is a regex, and the header says plainly that these are tripwires on the honest shape rather than mechanisms. *(f)* **Three code comments cited the wrong sections** — SECURITY.md §7 (the audit log) for a sentence in §5.1, AUTHZ.md §11 (open questions) for an obligation in §8. The repo's own recurring finding, in the slice that documents it. *(g)* The contact pick is **derived, not named**: prefer contacts whose profile holds `portal.work_item.view`, then the widest profile measured against the frozen capability table — `CONTACT_FINANCE` is already named as v2 and will hold neither, and the old `?? contacts[0]` fallback would have previewed such a client through a profile that sees nothing, with no blocker. *(h)* The switch **keeps its OFF direction while archived**: disabling it outright left the member shown `PROJECT_ARCHIVED` with no verb and, worse, unable to stop sharing on a project whose `portalEnabled` is still true — and archiving hides the task list only because the PROJECTION filters it. *(i)* A **pending affordance** on the switch: the fan-out plus a revalidation that re-runs the preview's three transactions is seconds, deliberately not optimistic, so without it the member presses and nothing happens. *(j)* `handleAuthzRedirect` before `notFound()`, the shape `loadProject` already uses. *(k)* `Contact.email` was selected, typed and returned and never rendered — PII crossing a boundary for nothing. *(l)* The tenant belt now covers the whole contacts list, not only the chosen row, because `audience` is counted from the list and a count is an answer too. *(m)* The module gates are memoised with React `cache`, the treatment `src/portal/context.ts` already gives them. *(n)* `task-list.tsx` has a MEMBER-plane consumer now, so its header forbids reaching for `requirePortalContext()` inside it — the timezone note one paragraph below invites exactly that, and it would throw at render on the member plane. *(o)* `list-disc` styling aligned with the app's only precedent.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT TAKEN (3).** *(a)* **The audit.** AUTHZ §3.2's row says `project:manage_portal` covers "View as client — audited", and this panel writes nothing. A page RENDER is not an act: Next re-runs it on prefetch, revalidation and refresh, so a row per render buries the act the name belongs to; every row shown is a CLIENT_VISIBLE row of a project the member already holds `project:view` and scope on; and `project.viewed_as_contact` names the explicit mode slice 5 builds, where a member ENTERS a client's view and navigates it — spending the name here would leave that slice without one. The catalogue row now says which half of it is audited and asks the founder to confirm. *(b)* **The layout's gate costs FOUR round trips, not three** — `hasAccess` re-resolves a permission set `loadProject` computed a few lines above. A `hasModuleAccess` running gates 1–3 only, AND-ed with the cap, would be cheaper and is what the reviewer proposed; rejected because a half-gate helper in an authz file is a thing someone will one day use alone, and the gate a reader must be able to trust is `requireAccess`'s own rather than a reassembly of it. The comment is corrected to say four. *(c)* **Contact PII on `project:manage_portal` alone.** The contact's NAME is read without `client:view`; unreachable with seeded templates (C and M both hold `client:view`) and only via a custom clone that tombstones it. `email` is gone, which was the part that mattered; the invite slice, which this tab's own checklist row says owns "contacts + last login + invite" here, is where the client-axis check belongs.

**AND ONE THING THE PINS ASK FOR THAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT.** §12's row names "what the client sees" CHECKBOXES — task list / kanban / hours mode / updates / files / milestones. Only `hoursSharingMode` exists as a column; the rest would each be a new `Project` column gating a portal surface that does not exist. **A switch that controls nothing is a switch someone trusts.** Each lands with the surface it gates; the row is marked `[~]` with that written in.

**SMALLER, BUT WORTH THE INK.** *(a)* The switch moved OFF Overview rather than being duplicated — one home per control, because a switch in two places is one someone flips in the version that is out of date. *(b)* The narrowed read's `PORTAL_TASK_LIMIT` applies per project, so a client whose whole list is truncated could see a task in the preview their own `/portal` cuts off; stated on the option rather than discovered later. *(c)* The preview renders in the MEMBER's language and timezone — the one thing it cannot claim to be byte-identical about, and the locale problem View-as-Contact must solve is already recorded below. *(d)* `ordering.dbtest.ts`'s 50-mover test is **20 movers now**, cut rather than re-diagnosed: each mover's Prisma budget starts at its own `BEGIN`, not at the head of the `FOR UPDATE` queue, so the last mover absorbs every predecessor's round trips inside one fixed budget — a property of the test against a link, not a defect. It had cost four slices an investigation. The property (no interleaving violates the rank unique, nothing is lost) is unchanged; what is reduced is the probability of a rare interleaving, an honest coverage trade. *(e)* `useRun` moved out of `overview-forms.tsx` into its own module now that two routes share it.

**GATES AND EVIDENCE.** Typecheck ✓, ESLint `src e2e --max-warnings 0` → 0. Unit **74 files / 1197 passed / 1 skipped**. `test:db` **43 files / 556 passed, 0 failed** — `ordering.dbtest.ts` included. `pnpm build` ✓ with `/projects/[key]/portal` dynamic (ƒ). Full e2e **132 passed / 1 skipped, 0 flaky** (56 min locally, 204 shots written) — **on the fourth attempt, and the three red ones were the environment rather than the tree.** Three consecutive full runs failed across board, backlog, visibility and the Swedish width walk — surfaces this diff does not touch — while every one of those specs passed in isolation; the failures were `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, then the app's error boundary, then 130 of 133 timing out. `playwright.config.ts` carries `reuseExistingServer: !CI`, and the page snapshot in `test-results/*/error-context.md` was the **Naxdor marketing site**: something else on the machine intermittently holds port 3000 and the suite had been running against it. Green on `E2E_PORT=3457 E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3457` (both are needed — the config derives from the first, `global-setup.ts` reads the second and otherwise falls back to a hardcoded 3000). **Two hypotheses were raised and DISPROVED before the snapshot was read** — machine memory (commit charge really was 45.4 GB of 50.4 GB, and really was not the cause; nine leaked Playwright browsers held 780 MB) and a `Promise.all` running two authz resolutions on one Prisma interactive transaction in the project layout. The second was a genuine defect and is fixed — one connection, interleaved statements, and `pg` warns about it by name — but rebuilding showed the warning predates this slice, so it was not the cause either. Both are now standing traps in AGENTS.md, together with the lesson: **on a broad cross-surface e2e failure, read `error-context.md` and check which APP answered before theorising.** **ELEVEN MUTATION CHECKS, because a passing test is not evidence until it has been made to fail:** a third `PortalPrincipal` builder fails 1; a work-table read inside the preview fails 1; `isAuthorized` in the layout fails 1; dropping the `projectId` from the `where` fails 4 + 2; dropping the `authorizePortal` ref fails 2; picking `contacts[0]` over the widest able profile fails 1; dropping the `PORTAL_OFF` blocker fails 2; `project:edit` back on the preview and the service fails 2; dropping `emailVerified` fails 1; dropping `NOTHING_SHARED` fails 1. The first `test:db` run went red on ONE test and it was the right one: `projects.dbtest.ts` asserted an employee *may* flip the switch, which is the behaviour this slice ends — inverted, with the reason written in, and FORBIDDEN rather than NOT_FOUND on both projects because the recipe checks the permission before the scope.

**THE TWO FRESH REVIEWS — code + security, read-only, given the diff and the gate results and nothing else.** Security returned **no CRITICAL and no HIGH**, cleared eight areas on traced evidence (principal synthesis, no RLS-bypassing read in the chain, column leakage, the C M E → C M narrowing's completeness, plane confinement through `src/proxy.ts`, denial disclosure, the narrowing, the fixtures) and raised one MEDIUM — the tripwire gap, taken. The code review returned 17 items including the seed HIGH; 15 taken, 3 dispositioned above (one item appears on both lists).


**PUSHED AND GREEN: slice 46 is `c7c0257`; CI run [35551538236](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/35551538236) — BOTH JOBS `success`.** On the service container: unit **73 files / 1192 passed / 1 skipped**, `test:db` **42 files / 544 passed, 0 failed**, browser harness **132 passed in 8.2 min, no flaky**. **`ordering.dbtest.ts` passed here too**, which is the fourth slice running to confirm the diagnosis PLAN already records: the 50-mover test serialises behind one `FOR UPDATE` on the anchor while each mover's 5 s Prisma budget runs from when ITS transaction opened, so the last movers must absorb every predecessor's round trips — a structural property of the test against a fixed budget on a slow link, not a defect CI green disproves. It has now cost four slices an investigation. **The durable fix is a widened `timeoutMs` for that one test, or fewer movers; `ordering.dbtest.ts` belongs to 2W and the next session that opens it should do it.** (CI reports 544 to the local run's 543 — the two `portal.dbtest.ts` cases added after the local run started.)

**2026-09-21 — SLICE 46 (memo slice 3): the first portal PROJECTION, the first portal ROUTE — and the tripwire meant to guard them was bound to two FILENAMES.** `src/modules/work/portal.ts` holds `listPortalTasks()`, the client-visible task list; `/portal` renders it under a real contact session; `/portal/login` now exists (the locked shell moved there, so the redirect every `/portal/...` request makes with no cookie stops landing on a route Next had nothing for). Gates below.

**THE FINDING OF THE SLICE, and it came from the security review rather than from building.** The forbidden-columns grep and the new AST allow-list check both walked `src/**` collecting files *named* `portal.ts` or `portal-writes.ts`. Nothing in the codebase makes a portal page read through one: ESLint confines `@/db/client`, `withPlatform` and `portalAuthClient`, but **`withPortalRead` is importable from anywhere**, and UI.md §11's "portal reads use only `modules/*/portal.ts` projections" is prose. So a `/portal/projects/[id]/page.tsx` written next slice as `withPortalRead(p, (tx) => tx.workItem.findMany({ where: { projectId } }))` would have handed the client every column of every CLIENT_VISIBLE row — the 512 KB ProseMirror body, the rank, the estimate, the member id — with **both tripwires green**, because no file named `portal.ts` was touched. **RLS filters ROWS, not COLUMNS**, and that sentence is the whole of why this matters: the database cannot save a projection that asks for everything. The walk now follows the CAPABILITY — the two conventional names, everything under the `(portal)` route group, and any file that so much as mentions `withPortalRead`. Mutation-checked with a probe page: a select-less `findMany` under `(portal)` fails the build, and the suite goes green again when the probe is removed.

**AND WIDENING IT IMMEDIATELY WENT RED ON A COMMENT, which is why the two tiers now have different scopes.** `src/portal/authorize.ts` says "at the cost of a WeakSet lookup rather than a round trip", and `cost` is on the never-list — so scanning every portal surface with the TEXT grep failed the build over a sentence. That is the failure this file already records for bare `label`: *a test that goes red for the wrong reason teaches people to ignore it*. So the grep keeps to code whose job IS projecting (the two names plus the portal routes, which are render code with no room for a paragraph about round trips) and the STRUCTURAL check — which fires on an actual select KEY and never on prose — runs over everything.

**THE STRUCTURAL CHECK ITSELF is the memo's §2.2 ask, over-honoured as it said to.** `src/authz/portal-projections.test.ts` parses each surface with the TypeScript AST and fails a read with no `select`, an `include`, an `omit`, raw SQL, a `select` that is not an inline literal — and **a relation picked whole**. `select: { project: true }` returns every column of the related row while looking exactly like a scalar pick and naming no forbidden column; keys are resolved against `prisma/schema.prisma` (parsed as TEXT — Prisma 7 has no runtime DMMF, and this must run in the unit suite with no `DATABASE_URL`), so a relation must carry a nested allow-list of its own. **A forbidden-column list cannot know about an internal column somebody adds next year; this can.** Eighteen negative controls, each hand-traced, plus five POSITIVE ones — see the `Object.create` note below.

**WHAT THE REVIEWS TOOK OFF IT, because "explicit" is not "safe".** The first cut proved a select was an allow-list and said nothing about whether the named columns were fit to leave: `select: { rank: true, triageStatus: true }` is explicit, is a real field, names nothing on the text grep's list, and publishes the agency's internal ordering of its own work. There is now a second tier — `PORTAL_NEVER_SELECTED`, checked against select KEYS — and it is a **separate list from `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS` on purpose: the text grep can never hold a common word** (`type`, `kind` and `rank` would fire on `type PortalTask = {`, on `readonly kind`, and on the paragraph in `portal.ts` explaining why the ordering is *not* by rank), while a select-key check can hold all three. `groupBy` and `aggregate` are banned outright rather than modelled — `groupBy` hands back the `by:` columns with no select to allow-list, no projection needs one today, and the day one does the exemption should be a visible change a reviewer meets.

**AND THE CHECK HAD TWO HOLES OF ITS OWN, both found independently by both reviews.** *(1)* An unresolvable delegate was a silent SKIP, not an offence: `tx["workItem"].findMany({select:{project:true}})` and `const wi = tx.workItem; wi.findMany(...)` both passed the one case the schema is parsed for, because with no model to look fields up in, every key read as a scalar. *(2)* Method names were matched receiver-blind, so `Object.create(null)` — **AGENTS.md's own ProseMirror trap** — `map.delete(tx)` and `hash.update(buf)` all became offences, in a walk that now covers `src/auth/portal.ts` (a Better Auth config, not a projection). Both are closed by one split: a **Prisma-only** method (`findMany`, `findFirst`, `upsert`, ...) is a row read whatever the receiver looks like, so an unresolvable delegate is an offence; an **ambiguous** one (`create`, `update`, `delete`) counts only when the delegate resolves to a real model. Five positive controls now assert that ordinary JavaScript still passes.

**THE OTHER REAL BUG: AN ARCHIVED PROJECT WENT ON PUBLISHING TO THE CLIENT FOR EVER.** `project`'s `portal_gate` is `client_id = app.client_id AND portal_enabled` — **no archive term** — and `archiveProject` sets `status`/`archivedAt` while leaving `portalEnabled` TRUE. An agency that finished a project, archived it and moved on would have kept serving its task list to that client indefinitely, with nothing on the member side showing the portal was still live. Filtered in the projection rather than in a policy because it is a projection decision and reversible. **Founder decision wanted:** if archiving a project should NOT hide shared work, one line in `listPortalTasks` deletes the behaviour. Measured from both ends (the row is reachable to the tenant, absent from the client's list, `portalEnabled` still true) and mutation-checked: removing the filter fails four tests.

**TWO PRODUCT DECISIONS THIS SLICE MADE AND THE FOUNDER SHOULD RULE ON.** *(1)* **`CANCELLED` has no portal category and is not shown.** Mapping it onto `DONE` would tell a client something was finished when it was dropped, and a fifth "Cancelled" heading is a word §11's vocabulary does not have. **The review sharpened this into the version that matters:** DATA_MODEL §6.14 pins triage `DECLINED` and `DUPLICATE` to a CANCELLED-category state, so **the one row on the list the client submitted THEMSELVES disappears silently the moment the agency says no.** Hidden is defensible for a task the client never asked for and indefensible for a request they did; the request-intake slice owns the fix (most likely a DECLINED portal category carrying the agency's reason). *(2)* **The portal has FOUR categories, not §11's three** — `REQUESTED`, `PLANNED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE` — because §11 gives two lists and both are right: its table says "Planned / In progress / Done" and its copy rule says a business reader is told "Requested", never "triage". Its own `STATUS_MAP` domain and its own messages, never a relabelled `stateCategory`, because a shared domain is how one vocabulary quietly becomes the other.

**DENIAL RENDERING — the inherited item (1), closed for authorization and DELIBERATELY NOT for admission, and the first draft of that claim was FALSE in three files.** `portalReadOrNull()` (`src/portal/render.ts`) turns every `AuthzError` into `null` and a page renders `null` exactly as it renders an empty answer, so NOT_ENTITLED, DISABLED_BY_TENANT, FEATURE_DISABLED, FORBIDDEN and NOT_FOUND are one surface, byte for byte; `render.test.ts` walks the whole `DenialReason` union so a reason added later cannot get its own branch, and it re-throws anything that is not an `AuthzError` — a page that says "nothing shared yet" when the database is down has told the client something false about their agency. **But the first draft used the SUSPENDED contact as its example, and both fresh reviews caught that independently.** A suspended, revoked or unverified contact never reaches a projection: `requirePortalContact()` redirects to `/portal/login` on any `portalGateDecision` verdict but `"ok"`, so `authorizePortal()`'s own `FORBIDDEN "contact is not ACTIVE"` is unreachable from a page and is exercised only by a hand-built principal in a dbtest. **That behaviour is right and stays** — a contact whose access was withdrawn must lose the session, not keep a usable one in front of a blank page — and the disclosure runs the other way: admission tells the reader a fact about **themselves**, which they need in order to ask for their access back; `portalReadOrNull` hides facts about the **agency**. Corrected in `render.ts`, `page.tsx` and AUTHZ.md §8, which now states the rule as *every authorization denial after admission renders identically; admission itself signs the contact out*.

**THE HARNESS HAS A THIRD PRINCIPAL NOW** (memo §2.4: "the portal walk needs an anonymous-ish fixture — a contact session — which the harness has no concept of today"). The seed activates its CONTACT_PRIMARY contact (`emailVerified`, `portalStatus=ACTIVE`, `invitedAt`, `invitedById`) and writes a `contact_account` credential the way invite acceptance will; global-setup signs it in through the **real** `/api/portal-auth/sign-in/email` in a context of its own and saves `.auth/contact.json`. Both passwords are generated per run in the test worker, passed in env vars, never written to the seed file and never printed. Two stops added — `portal-login` (anon) and `portal-home` (contact) — and the seed now switches the portal ON for the main project **through `setPortalEnabled`, not a column write**, so the ten-table fan-out is exercised rather than bypassed. The Swedish width walk skips `session` stops and **that is a gap, not a decision**: `setLanguage` writes `User.locale` and a contact's comes from `Contact.locale`, so covering the portal in Swedish needs a contact-side switch — the invite slice's profile menu is its natural home.

**SMALLER, BUT WORTH THE INK.** *(a)* **Ordering is NOT by `rank`, and the reason is that rank IS importance** (plan §3.1, UI.md rule 5) — ordering a client's list by it would publish the team's internal ranking of their work *without ever naming a forbidden column*, and without the grep noticing, because `rank` is not one. It orders by the two facts the client can already see. *(b)* `Contact.invitedById` joined the never-list, handed over by name from slice 2 — and `portal.dbtest.ts` **measures** the claim rather than restating it: a contact really can read every contact row of its own client, member id and all, because `portal_gate` on `contact` is structural. *(c)* `src/i18n/resolve.ts` gained a contact arm, positioned AFTER the member one so a member page pays nothing and a member who is also a contact keeps one language; no tenant fallback, because `tenant` carries `portal_deny` and Accept-Language is a better guess than the agency's own language. *(d)* `total` became `shown` — it is the size of the answer, never "how many tasks you have", and the old name invited the next caller to render it as the latter. *(e)* DATA_MODEL §6.14's pinned projection list was a pre-implementation draft and **disagreed with what shipped in four places**; reconciled in this commit rather than left as another documents-vs-schema gap. *(f)* `id` is a UUIDv7, so creation time ships with every row whether or not `createdAt` is selected — not an INTERNAL fact, but "we did not select it" is not "it is not there". *(g)* The empty state takes `variant="forbidden"` with a neutral glyph: §5.8 requires a nothing-yet state to offer the verb that changes it, and a contact has no such verb — they cannot share their own agency's work with themselves.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT TAKEN (3).** *(a)* **`PortalPrincipal.gates` is not bound to its tenant.** The same objection slice 2 dispositioned, with a sharper framing — the risk is a route REUSING another tenant's gates map rather than spoofing one — and the same answer: the member plane's `MemberActor.mfa` has the identical shape, AUTHZ §7.5 closes it with a rule rather than a mechanism, and branding does not survive a spread. The doc comment now names the hazard and names **View-as-Contact as the slice that must resolve gates from the VIEWED contact's tenant**. *(b)* **`NextIntlClientProvider` ships the whole message bundle to the portal.** Pre-existing, not tenant data, and narrowing next-intl per plane is its own slice — but the portal is the first surface whose reader is a stranger, so it is recorded rather than inherited silently. *(c)* **The DONE group sorts by `targetDate` (usually null) rather than `completedAt`,** so finished work reads oldest-first. Real, cosmetic, and changing it in the component would weaken the projection's "the order is part of the contract" claim; it belongs with the one-screen project page.

**OWED, NAMED HERE SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED.** **View-as-Contact's byte-identity test will fail on LOCALE.** `resolveLocale` prefers the member session and View-as renders under it (founder decision 1, 2026-09-20), so a member reading Swedish and a contact reading English produce different bytes for the same projection.
