**Slice 29 `e30e02b` — the stale-tab fence (CI `35347460402` GREEN). The hazard slice 26 created is CLOSED.** `Session.activeTenantId` became mutable mid-session when the picker learned to pick, and a session is one cookie jar: switch in one tab and every other tab shows workspace X while everything it posts resolves Y. An action carrying an entity id fails safe (RLS finds nothing, `assertInScope` refuses); a **create-shaped** one has no such id and lands where the member is not looking. **WHY THE FIX IS IN THE BROWSER, so no later session re-litigates it:** cookies are per ORIGIN, not per tab, so nothing the server reads distinguishes a stale tab, and a server action carries only what its caller passes — a fence at `requireTenantContext()` would be an argument on all 118 actions. But the hazard REQUIRES a shared session, a shared session means one browser profile, and one browser profile means a `BroadcastChannel` reaches every tab that can have the problem. The protocol is two messages in `src/lib/workspace-watch.ts`, unit-tested apart from the DOM: `who` and `here`, and a tab is stale when another names a different workspace **more recently than it learned its own** — both halves, or the tab that just rendered the truth marks itself wrong the moment a stale one says hello. Nothing is stored (ARC-25; `localStorage` also throws in a private window). The fence is a **modal**, not a banner and not `inert`: a banner leaves every control clickable and the write it must stop is one click, and the surfaces that most need stopping — the peek, any picker, a confirm — are Radix portals outside the shell subtree `inert` would cover. **The stamp is the SERVER render instant and the watcher is KEYED on it**, which is what makes the fence symmetric: "Go back to {name}" puts the pointer back into this tab's workspace, making the OTHER tab stale, and without the key nothing would have told it. A review caught that; the e2e had passed anyway on a remount that happened to fall out of the redirect. The security review found nothing and named one blind spot, now closed — a member who switches and then goes Back across a document boundary has a restored tab with no peer to answer its `who`, so `pageshow(persisted)` asks the server too. **One residual, recorded in the component rather than papered over:** `at` is a wall clock, so two app instances with skewed clocks could fence the wrong one of two tabs; no attacker control, no tenant boundary crossed, and the alternative is a database write per layout render (`Session.updatedAt` is the counter already there if it is ever wanted).

**Slice 30 `99b121f` — the global `C` (order item (4)).** UI.md rule 2 has said "`C` anywhere" since the plan was written; only the board had one. A dialog in the shell on every authed page; the project comes from the ROUTE on a project page and from a picker otherwise, and stays changeable either way. The list is read ON OPEN (`quickCreateProjectsAction` = `listProjects` verbatim, so `project:view` and the same scope filter decide what may be OFFERED while `createItem` decides what may be written — a review checked the two sets and the offer set is a subset). `createItemAction` is now a wrapper over `createItemAnywhereAction`, which returns the created row because ⌘Enter is create-and-open. **The browser found two bugs no reading did:** a `disabled` input has already lost focus, so re-focusing it after the create was a no-op and "Enter starts the next" silently did not work; and clearing the field on SEND instead lost a task outright, because the create had not landed when the member navigated and the browser cancelled the POST. It now does exactly what the backlog create row does — clear on the ANSWER, guard while one is out, never disable. Five review findings fixed, the sharpest being a **hydration race**: scope order only decides a key once BOTH bindings are registered, and the shell is interactive before a streamed page is, so a `C` pressed into that window opened the dialog over a board about to claim the key — and `keymap.spec.ts` presses `c` in a retry loop the dialog's exclusive scope would have starved for 30 s. The shell now declares its binding and DISABLES it on a board route (a disabled run-bearing binding swallows rather than falling through), so the key is **route-decided, not hydration-order-decided**.

**STANDING HAZARD CREATED 2026-09-18 (slice 26) — THE ACTIVE WORKSPACE IS NOW MUTABLE MID-SESSION, AND A STALE TAB CAN WRITE TO THE WRONG ONE.** Until slice 26 the pointer had no writer, so a member's workspace could only change at sign-in and the whole app was built on that. Now a second tab (or a restored/bfcached page) can be SHOWING workspace A while the session points at B — `revalidatePath` reaches only the tab that acted. Id-bearing mutations fail closed (`assertInScope` denies a foreign id and RLS backs it), but **create-shaped actions carry no id and take the tenant purely from `requireTenantContext()`**: verified on `createClientAction` (`clients/actions.ts`), which passes `membership.tenantId` straight into `createClient`. So: `/clients` open in A, switch to B in another tab, return to tab 1 without reloading, type a name, press Enter — the client is created in **B**, from a page that says **A**, where a different set of members can read it. Found by slice 26's security reviewer and verified from the code by the implementing session. **Latent in production today** — it needs more than one workspace and nobody has one. The fixes are a slice of their own: echo the rendered tenant id into mutating forms as a COMPARISON TOKEN only (never as the source of truth) and reject a mismatch with a typed `ActionResult`; and/or broadcast the switch to other tabs (`BroadcastChannel`) and force a reload. Whoever adds the next create-shaped action should know this exists.

**THE STANDING LESSON, recorded because it recurred FOUR times in one session and every instance was caught by a reviewer rather than by the session:** *(1)* three code comments stated causes that were false — `/projects` blamed on a name column when `table-fixed min-w-3xl` makes content irrelevant, `joinedAt` called a JS millisecond timestamp when it is a Postgres transaction timestamp, and "in ENGLISH nothing scrolls at all" written forty lines from a constant listing English overflows; *(2)* slice 25's two tests were INVERTED rather than extended when the fixture gained a second workspace, leaving the feature pinned by nothing; *(3)* slice 27 was verified with a command that cannot see what CI sees; *(4)* the suite's worst flake had its exposure doubled by adding a second test to a block whose `beforeEach` performs it. **Write the number first, then the cause it forces. Verify with what the gate will actually face, not with what is convenient. When a fixture changes, ADD a case — never invert the one that is there.**

**SLICE 26 (`52512f1`) — THE WORKSPACE PICKER CAN ACTUALLY SWITCH.** The standing hazard slice 25 recorded, closed. `src/auth/active-tenant.ts` is the writer that never existed, and **it holds the membership check itself** rather than trusting its caller: the posted id is matched against what `member_self_select` returns for the COOKIE's user, SUSPENDED is a denial and not a miss, and the session row is pinned by `id` AND `userId` so it cannot move someone else's pointer. Only P2025 becomes a denial (duck-typed on the code, no runtime import of the generated client) — anything else rethrows, because a pool timeout must not tell a member their workspace is gone. **No migration** (`active_tenant_id` has existed since init; `session` carries no RLS class) and **no audit event**: `audit.record()` structurally refuses to run outside a tenant transaction, so there is no in-catalog way to write this without inventing a tenant to attribute it to, and it is an auth-plane write to the caller's own session row exactly as `step-up.ts` writes `mfaVerifiedAt`. Each ACTIVE row **POSTs rather than links** — Next prefetches links, so a GET would switch workspace on hover — through a `useFormStatus` button (`workspace-row-button.tsx`) whose pending state is correctness, not polish: the action writes, sweeps the router cache and redirects, a window PLAN §0 measures at over two seconds, and two clicks on DIFFERENT rows would land wherever the last write went. Clicking the workspace you are already in early-returns. `aria-disabled`, never `disabled`. **A REAL ORDERING DEFECT found on the way:** `listMembershipsForUser` sorted by `joinedAt` alone, and `joined_at` is `TIMESTAMPTZ(6) DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` — Postgres' CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is the TRANSACTION's start time, so every member row seated in one transaction ties by construction, and a tied sort is arbitrary per query. A member's default workspace could differ between two requests. Tie-broken on `id` (stable; a `text` column by collation, so not creation order — do not read it as such). **The e2e fixture now seats the owner in a SECOND, EMPTY workspace** (closing slice 25's owed (a)): with one membership every assertion could only ever be an absence.

**SLICE 27 (`6ebfd16`) — THE CRAFT WALK NOW BOUNDS HOW FAR A TABLE SCROLLS.** Order item (3) turned out to be stale (above), so this slice built the thing whose absence let a false claim survive three slices: `tableOverflow` (`e2e/audit.ts`) measures each box's `scrollWidth − clientWidth` at the same widths `offscreenRowActions` is asked, against `KNOWN_OVERFLOW` (`e2e/visual.spec.ts`) — a **ratchet keyed `<stop>@<width>`**, every unlisted key held to 0, every listed one to the pixel. Keyed by WIDTH because a per-stop number measured on a phone would have licensed the same scroll on a desktop. **What it found the day it was written, both owed since slice 17 (owed (f)) and both worst on a PHONE, a width this walk has photographed all along without asserting on it:** `/projects` **412px** over a 356px box at 390px — `table-fixed min-w-3xl` is a hard 768px FLOOR, and every number is exactly 768 − box (390/768/880/882/1008/1010), so it is a constant, identical in every locale, and one class removes all of it; `/clients` **147px** and `/clients?archived=1` **161px** — the name cell's `max-w-[420px]` is a floor in Chromium (503px of content, 517 with the wider Archived badge), with `/clients/[id]/projects` at 0 as the control; and `files` / `client-files` / `error-banner` **3px**, named rather than buried under a wider tolerance. **Fixing those three table families is the next slice and was NOT done here** — each needs its own measured pass and a decision about which columns drop where, and rushing three table redesigns to make a new gate green is the wrong pressure.

**THE REVIEWS: THREE FRESH READ-ONLY AGENTS — 1 HIGH each on two of them, and the lesson is about COMMENTS.** Slice 26, security: **nothing HIGH**; it verified the form-supplied tenant id is not a breach (only ever MATCHED against what RLS returned; four attacks traced, no existence oracle), that no migration is owed, that Better Auth's cookie cache is OFF so the direct write is read back next request, and that the audit omission is right for a better reason than the session had given. **SESSION (2026-09-17, night) — THE `visibility.spec.ts:167` TOAST FLAKE: CAUSE ESTABLISHED, FIXED IN THE HARNESS; THEN SLICE 22, Σ SPENT ON THE CARD (record below this one).** Taken as §0's recorded NEXT. **THE CAUSE.** Reproduced locally at 2 of 20 repeats against a production build (`--repeat-each 20`, the retained traces of both failures compared with two passing runs captured with `--trace on`). The toast was "never", and the product was not at fault: every authed page registers the app's service worker (`PwaRegister`, production only — which is why `next dev` never showed it), and Playwright's `page.route` does not own a request a service worker's fetch handler has seen — Playwright's own note on `route` says so and recommends `serviceWorkers: "block"`. In a PASSING run the aborted POST failed at once with `net::ERR_FAILED` (the route's abort), the fetch rejected, and the toast followed within 100 ms. In a FAILING run the SAME POST was issued at the same instant, hung about four seconds, was cancelled with `net::ERR_ABORTED`, and the page's fetch promise NEVER settled: no toast, no revert — and the optimistic "Private to team" stuck on screen while the database held CLIENT_VISIBLE (the failure snapshot shows the badge on INTERNAL ten seconds later). Slice 19's `Toaster` change, the first suspect, was innocent; the earliest recorded occurrence (08-21) predates it and the worker does not touch a POST (`if (request.method !== "GET") return;`) — the interference is inside Chromium's interception, not in the worker's code. Next's action reducer rejects only when the fetch rejects (`server-action-reducer.js`; the offline replay path is compiled out — no `experimental.useOffline`), so a fetch that neither resolves nor rejects is a promise that hangs forever. **THE FIX (harness only, no product change):** `playwright.config.ts` sets `serviceWorkers: "block"`; `pwa.spec.ts` wraps its one registration test in a describe that re-allows the worker. Measured after: **60 of 60** (the whole visibility spec ×12, 11.8 min), the toast at 70–100 ms every time. Every spec that routes was exposed (`item-properties.spec.ts:543`, `time.spec.ts` ×4), and the long-recorded employee sign-in flake (`scoping.spec.ts:60`) MAY be the same class — not verified, watch whether it stops. **THE TEST** now asserts the after-state too — the badge back on CLIENT_VISIBLE (the optimistic value did not stick; the hang is exactly this failing) and the stored row unchanged — and on a missing toast reports what its recorder saw (`toast-diagnosis.json`: URL, sweep count, recorded toasts, the badge, the stored value, navigations, action POSTs, console errors) instead of a bare "received: false". **TWO THINGS RECORDED, NOT BUILT:** (1) CI uploads the Playwright report only on a FAILED job, so a flaky-but-green run keeps no trace of its first attempt — that is why five recurrences produced no evidence. `if: always()` would keep it, but the trace's HAR carries the throwaway tenant's session cookie and the repository is public; the founder decides whether a dead cookie in a 7-day artifact is acceptable. (2) A product observation: `VisibilitySelect`'s optimistic value has no timeout, so a POST that hangs (a proxy that never answers) shows the CHOSEN value indefinitely while the server holds the old one — for this control, "Private to team" while the client can still see the file. Inherent to `useOptimistic` over an unbounded request, and a design question (a deadline that reverts and toasts?), not a fix to slip into a flake commit. Gates on the harness change: typecheck 0, ESLint 0, unit 62 files / 1035.

**SESSION (2026-09-16, later) — SLICE 15: `J K`, THE BACKLOG'S ROVING ROW FOCUS, WHICH TURNS `X` INTO THE ONE-HAND FLOW `J X J X`. THE HEADLINE IS A TAB STOP THAT WAS DESIGNED, BUILT AND THEN REMOVED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: THE BOARD'S ROVING-TABINDEX PATTERN (ONE CARD AT `tabIndex=0`) WAS COPIED FIRST, AND THEN THE TAB ORDER WAS ACTUALLY WALKED — A ROW'S `<tr>` SITS IMMEDIATELY BEFORE ITS OWN CHECKBOX, SO THE STOP WOULD HAVE BEEN ONE MORE STOP ON A LIST ALREADY FOUR STOPS A ROW, WOULD HAVE SHIFTED THE SEQUENCE EVERY EXISTING TAB-DRIVEN E2E WALKS, AND WOULD HAVE BOUGHT NOTHING, BECAUSE A MEMBER ENTERS THE FLOW FROM ANY CONTROL IN A ROW. EVERY ITEM ROW IS `tabIndex=-1`: REACHABLE BY KEY, NEVER BY TAB.**

**SHIPPED (not pushed).** No migration, no service, no server action, no schema — focus is client state. `backlog-table.tsx`: `J`/`K` and `↑`/`↓` from anywhere inside an item row (its checkbox, key link, a resting control, the row itself) move DOM focus to the next/previous ITEM row's `<tr>` (`rovingStep` in `keymap.ts` is the one table of one-row moves); the arrows are left to a control that owns them (`ownsArrows`: a closed select/combobox trigger, a spin button, a slider, a radio) and to Shift, which a list keeps for range selection — round 2 replaced the first draft's "arrows only on the row itself", which made the arrows work or not by how the member had entered the row. Group headers are stepped over; the ends are the ends (nothing happens, and an arrow is left to the page). The row's inline delete question refuses them as it refuses `X`. **Auto-repeat is allowed** for a move (one row per event, so a held `J` walks the list — the board's rule) where `X` refuses it: the guard is `focusedKeyGuards(shape, goPending, { repeat: "allow" })` — a declared policy (round 2), the other five guards unchanged. Registered in the `backlog` scope with the board's `["J", "or", "K"]` hint, `enabled: !peekOpen`, no permission (a viewer walks the list too) — and since round 2 `J` carries a `run` that acts only when focus is nowhere in the list (the ENTRY into it, at the first row below the sticky header; `palette: false`), where `X` stays `run: null`; `projects.backlog.keys.navigate` "Move between tasks" / "Flytta mellan uppgifter". **Under the virtualised window:** the handler only NAMES the row (`setFocusedRowId`); the window's overscan already has the next row mounted (the focus pin is the belt if a scroll event were ever dropped — my first draft claimed the pin did the mounting, and the efficiency reviewer corrected it), and an effect with NO dependency list focuses the `<tr>` once it is in the DOM (round 2 — see below for why not keyed on the id), with an early-out when focus is already inside the named row, so a click or Tab INTO a row's control (which sets the same state through `onFocusCapture`) leaves focus on that control. No pending ref (the board keeps one because its effect must wait for `items`/`picker`). A step whose target lies outside the pin's reach (`inPinReach`, ONE definition shared with the pin) is refused rather than named: the member can wheel-scroll 49 rows away from a focused row with the pin holding it, and naming row 50 would unmount both rows and drop focus to `<body>`, which Chromium reports with no blur — found by three reviewers. `focus()`'s own scroll fires `measure`, which is how the window follows a held `J`. The rows carry `scroll-mt-16` / `scroll-mb-16` (overriding `TableRow`'s `scroll-mt-8`): the shell header is sticky at `h-12`, so the default would leave the top third of a `K`-focused row under it, and the bulk bar is sticky at the bottom. **The focus ring is `TableRow`'s standard OUTLINE at `-outline-offset-6`, keyed on `:focus`, defined once beside the selected bar (UI.md §9 records the geometry) — and it took both review rounds to land there.** My first draft used `-outline-offset-2`: an outline at that offset paints over the outer 2px band on all four sides, and on the left that band IS `visibilityRowCue`'s client-visible mark, so the one row the member is about to act on with `X` would have shown as INTERNAL — and below `sm` that edge is the only visibility mark (three of round 1's lenses, independently). Round 1's fix was an inset box-shadow ring, which round 2 refuted on four counts: UI.md §9 forbids box-shadow rings and the fix had not amended it; forced-colors mode drops box-shadows and engines differ on painting them on a collapsed-border `<tr>`; the ring occupied the SAME 2px band as the selected bar and Tailwind paints `--tw-inset-ring-shadow` above `--tw-shadow`, so a focused+selected row — every row in the `J X` flow — lost its `--primary` bar (the probe could not see it: `--ring` and `--primary` are both indigo); and my comment blamed the global outline for a negative offset it never had. -6 clears the 2px cue AND the 2px bar; `:focus` rather than `:focus-visible` because programmatic focus inherits the previous element's focus-visible state in Firefox and WebKit, where a mouse-focused link followed by `J` would have ringed nothing. `keyEventShape(e)` (`keymap.ts`) now builds the seven-field shape for the dispatcher and the backlog alike, so a guard added there reaches both. UI.md §6 has the new row and the `X` row is amended. **Not in this slice, recorded as owed:** Enter to open the focused row's peek; `Home`/`End`; the board's `onBoardKeyDown` guards only chords, so `G J` on the BOARD moves focus while the dispatcher swallows the `G`, where `G J` on the backlog is inert — the board should call `focusedKeyApplies` per key as the backlog does (its own slice, with its own e2e); `scroll-padding-top: 3rem` on `html` beside the existing `scroll-padding-bottom` would make every `focus()`/anchor clear the sticky header at once and retire ~30 per-site `scroll-mt-*` (`TableRow`'s `scroll-mt-8` has never matched the header) — a global change, not this slice's; the always-on `scroll-mb-16` is short by ~1.5rem for a bulk bar that wraps to two lines on a phone (a bar that declares its own reserve while open is the right shape); a shared `usePendingFocus` hook is not worth it until a third list wants it.

**THE REVIEW (round 2, the same eight lenses over the fixed tree): 3 real defects in round 1's FIXES, all fixed — the rule that a fix commit is a slice too earned its keep a third time.** (1) The inset ring (above). (2) **A step that does not land could never be retried:** the round-1 effect was keyed on `focusedRowId`, so if the target was not in the DOM at commit (a scroll between keydown and commit moved the window), a second `J` from the same row wrote the same id, which is no state change, and the keys were dead until the member clicked — the intent and the record were one cell of state. The effect now has NO dependency list and cheap early-outs, so any later render that mounts the row focuses it; and it tells a STEP (focus elsewhere in the table: `focus()` with its scroll) from a RESTORE (focus on `<body>`: the row was scrolled past the pin, unmounted with focus on it, and has come back — `focus({ preventScroll: true })`, so the flow resumes without yanking the scroll) from "the member moved on" (leave it). **SESSION (2026-09-15, later still) — PANEL SLICE 13: `⌘⇧O`, THE CHECKLIST ITEM THAT BECOMES A SUBTASK. THE HEADLINE IS A DESIGN CHOICE, NOT A BUG: THE CONVERSION IS **NOT** ONE TRANSACTION, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A SERVER ACTION THAT CREATED THE CHILD *AND* REMOVED THE LINE WOULD BE A SECOND WRITER OF THE DESCRIPTION, HOLDING A BASE TOKEN WHILE THE EDITOR'S OWN AUTOSAVE — TWO SECONDS BEHIND EVERY KEYSTROKE, AND ⌘⇧O IS PRESSED RIGHT AFTER TYPING THE LINE — HELD THE SAME ONE; ONE OF THE TWO WOULD BE REFUSED AS STALE AND THE MEMBER TOLD “SOMEONE ELSE SAVED THIS DESCRIPTION” ABOUT THEIR OWN TYPING. SO THE CHILD IS CREATED FIRST AND THE LINE LEAVES ONLY ONCE IT EXISTS, AS AN ORDINARY EDIT IN THE ONE WRITER THE FIELD HAS ALWAYS HAD. THE SECOND HEADLINE IS THE TEST'S OWN TRAP: A PLAYWRIGHT CLICK SETS THE DOM SELECTION AT ONCE, BUT PROSEMIRROR LEARNS OF IT FROM `selectionchange`, WHICH CHROMIUM FIRES ON A LATER TASK — SO A CHORD PRESSED IN THE SAME TICK READ THE CARET'S *PREVIOUS* POSITION AND CONVERTED THE WRONG LINE. A MEMBER IS SLOWER THAN A TASK; A HARNESS IS NOT.**

**SHIPPED.** UI.md §6's last unshipped item-scope key, on both surfaces. With the caret in a checklist item, `⌘⇧O` creates a child of this task from that line and removes the line. No migration, no new service, no new server action, no schema change: the create is the SAME `createSubtaskAction` the Subtasks section's add row uses, so a child made from a line lands exactly as a typed one does — numbered, at the bottom of the project's order, in the default state, **its visibility inherited from the parent row the server share-locks** (`items.ts`, never from anything the client sent) — and the removal is an ordinary editor edit, flushed at once instead of waiting out the idle timer. The failure shapes follow from that order and are the reason for it: a refused create changes NOTHING and says so; a failed save leaves the words on screen and the field dirty, the editor's standing contract; the one state the order cannot produce is a line that vanished into a subtask that does not exist. **The key is PROSEMIRROR's, never the shell registry's** — the registry is inert while an editable element has focus and answers no chord but ⌘K — so it is a Tiptap extension that adds no node and no mark, leaving the schema the server validates against exactly the schema the browser edits with; the registry carries a `run: null` row (`key:"o"`, `hint:["mod","Shift","O"]`) purely so the `?` overlay advertises it, which `decide()` skips before the `enabled` check and the palette filters out, so it can neither dispatch nor swallow a bare `O`. **Both spellings are registered** (`Mod-Shift-o` and `Mod-Shift-O`): `event.key` is uppercase while Shift is held, so prosemirror-keymap looks up `Shift-Ctrl-O` and reaches a lowercase binding only through its `event.keyCode` fallback. **The rule is narrow on purpose** (`src/lib/rich-text/checklist.ts`, pure, 13 table tests): an item that is not a single line — a nested checklist under it, a second paragraph, a line break — is refused rather than flattened, because every way of converting it loses something the member wrote, and the refusal is actionable (convert what is nested first and the parent becomes convertible); a TICKED item is refused for the same reason, since a new task starts in the default state and converting a finished line would delete the one record that it was finished; a selection that runs out of the line it starts in names no single line, while a selection INSIDE one line still converts the whole line, because a task title is the line. The removal survives the round trip by NODE IDENTITY (`nodePosition`), which answers both questions the await opened — where the line moved to, and whether it is still the line that was converted — where a remembered position would answer neither; a line edited meanwhile is left where it is and the member is told.

**SHIPPED.** The item rail's eighth property and its first MULTI one (UI.md §5.2 `L`), on both surfaces — and, because nothing anywhere created a label, the service under it: `src/modules/work/labels.ts`. `createLabel` coins a TENANT-WIDE word under `label:manage` (CMA — an employee is refused), audited `label.created`, and may put it on one task in the same transaction (`applyTo`: the task's `work_item:edit` and scope are refused BEFORE any label row exists, so a member who may coin a word but may not edit this task creates nothing; the return type keys on the argument, so a caller that applied is never handed `null`). `setItemLabel` puts ONE label on a task or takes it off under `work_item:edit` — routine by the founder's 2026-09-12 carve-out (labels are named in it): a `WorkItemActivity` row and no audit, INTERNAL by construction because `labels` is not portal-safe and a label is a word the client never sees; the row is the schema's own shape, an add in `newRef` and a removal in `oldRef`, as the assignee's rows say it, and never the name (the read resolves the ref, so a rename shows the current name and a deleted label reads as gone). The task is share-locked (rows.ts `"SHARE"`, the comment writer's lock for the comment writer's reason), and `changed` is decided by the join write's OWN row count — `createMany skipDuplicates` against the composite PK, `deleteMany` — never by a read before it, so two adds of one label count exactly once. The answer is always the WHOLE list as it then stands, so two members labelling one task never overwrite each other's adds. A label of another project is `NOT_FOUND`, as absent as one that does not exist; nothing creates a project-scoped label yet, so that check has no trigger belt — it lands with whatever does. **The database decides the name's uniqueness:** migration `20260915180000_label_tenant_wide_name_key` adds a partial unique expression index on `(tenant_id, lower(name)) WHERE project_id IS NULL`, because the schema's `(tenant_id, project_id, name)` index cannot refuse two tenant-wide names — NULLs are distinct to a unique index — which is what DATA_MODEL's "app also checks" had meant; the dev database has zero duplicates, the index went in through the pg-driver+ledger path (checksum method re-verified byte-for-byte against two recorded migrations first), and `db-errors.ts` maps its name to `LABEL_TAKEN` exactly as `work_type_name_live` is mapped. `readItemLabels` (off the barrel, `labelId` being on `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS`) gives `getItemDetail` the task's labels and its vocabulary (tenant-wide plus the project's own; `offered` empty for a member who cannot edit) and `caps.manageLabels`. ONE name key and ONE order for every surface (`labelNameKey`, `compareLabelNames` in `@/lib/work-view`, beside `MAX_LABEL_NAME_LENGTH` = 40): the key is trim + lower-case, what the index computes — deliberately not `matchesQuery`'s diacritic fold, since "Café" and "Cafe" are two words and a client that hid the Create row for one the server accepts could never coin it; the order is by that key then the raw name, never `localeCompare` or a collation, because CI's C.UTF-8 and Node's ICU disagree on `["Zed", "race"]`. **The picker gained its third seam, `selected`**: a MULTI property passes `value={null}` — nothing seeded, a bare Enter INERT (the picker stays open; there is no current row to re-pick), the member steers or types first — and `selected` draws the check and the "(applied)" words on every applied row. And the set is part of the highlight BASIS (`picker-rows.ts`, three new table tests): a steered row whose membership flips underneath the member is re-seeded and un-steered; another row's flip leaves it alone. "Create “<text>”" is the typed row (`derive`), offered only under `label:manage` and only while no row has that name under the key, null past the bound; the rows are the vocabulary PLUS any applied label it does not carry yet, so a label coined a moment ago is a row before the refresh delivers it (disabled while its create is in flight — its id is provisional). The island (`labels-field.tsx`) is `M`'s shape with one difference worth stating: the verb the newest answer carried travels WITH the shown value (`last`), and the actions echo the label acted on and the verb, so a superseded answer announced late names ITS label and verb. The chips are neutral `Badge`s that may WRAP. Two sentences joined the history (`labelAdded` / `labelRemoved`), `LABEL_TAKEN` joined the domain codes, and the shared `matchesQuery` lost a pre-existing bug on the way: it walked the haystack by code point but indexed the needle by UTF-16 unit, so an emoji never matched itself — the first member-coined vocabulary a picker filters was the first to notice (`text-match.test.ts`, new).

**SESSION (2026-09-15) — PANEL SLICE 11: THE MILESTONE (`M`) PICKER. THE HEADLINE IS A RULE THE SLICE HAD TO DISCOVER: A HISTORY ROW MAY NOT CARRY A PHASE'S NAME. `milestoneId` IS ONE OF THE FIVE PORTAL-SAFE FIELDS, SO ON A SHARED TASK ITS ROW IS CLIENT_VISIBLE — AND A NAME WRITTEN THERE IS A COPY THAT OUTLIVES EVERY LATER DECISION ABOUT THE PHASE'S OWN VISIBILITY, WHICH NOTHING CHASES. THE ROW CARRIES IDS; THE READ RESOLVES THEM PER READER, SO THE ANSWER IS RLS'S AND NOT OURS — AND NO MIGRATION WAS NEEDED TO GET IT.**

**SHIPPED.** The item rail's seventh property (UI.md §5.2 `M`, §5.11's sibling contract), on both surfaces: `setItemMilestone` (`src/modules/work/items.ts`) files a task under one of its OWN project's phases or takes it out of the one it is under — `requireAccess("work_item:edit")` → `loadItemInScope` (locked, then read, then scoped, the order `assignItem` takes) → one milestone read BOUND to `item.projectId` (so a phase of another project is `NOT_FOUND`, exactly as absent as one that does not exist) → an UPDATE with an inline `select` → a `WorkItemActivity` row. A **ROUTINE** edit by the founder's 2026-09-12 decision: activity, never audit, though the field is portal-safe. `getItemDetail` gained `milestones` (the project's phases by RANK — the timeline's own order, so the picker and the timeline can never disagree about what comes after what), read only for a member who can edit, beside `activeMembers` under the same rule; `ItemDetail.milestone` traded the `visibility` nothing rendered for the `status` the trigger's glyph draws. `setItemMilestoneAction` is the seventh sibling in `backlog/actions.ts`, unchanged in shape. `milestonePickerTargets` (`@/lib/work-view`, four unit tests) is the one rule for which phases may be CHOSEN: a CANCELLED phase is not a target, the item's own is always a row — non-selectable when it is one of those, the `S` rule verbatim — and the test-id ordinals are numbered over the FULL list before the filter, so a row's id never depends on which phases are live. The island (`milestone-field.tsx`) is `A`'s shape: rows in one order with the current checked in place, the "No milestone"/"Remove from milestone" pair under the empty-property rule (two values, both committing null), each row's glyph its `STATUS_MAP.milestoneStatus` icon and each dated row its date in `meta` — the datum that tells "Sprint 3" from "Sprint 4". **Three sentences** joined the history (`milestoneSet` / `milestoneChanged` / `milestoneCleared`, the estimate trio's shape so nothing reads like the state row's "moved this from…"), and `readItemActivity` resolves `milestoneId` refs exactly as it resolves `assignee` ones, bound to the tenant AND the item's own client. **No migration:** `work_item_milestone_guard` has been in place since 20260912120000, and its token stays UNMAPPED on purpose — the service reads the target bound to the item's project, nothing moves a milestone or an item between projects, and no service deletes a milestone, so no member can reach it (`db-errors.ts` says so now, and DATA_MODEL records the decision).

**THE REVIEWS: `/code-review high`, `/security-review` (no finding at threshold), then TWO read-only lenses, one over each fix delta — and the second lens found a MEDIUM the first fix had left half-closed, which is the whole case for the rule.** 11 findings, 0 HIGH. **Round 1 (2):** the new dbtest's `afterAll` guarded `f?.tenantId` but not `foreignProjectId`, so a `beforeAll` that threw would have turned three scoped `deleteMany` calls into tenant-wide ones and wiped the fixture's own project mid-teardown (the standing Prisma undefined-where trap, one file away from the comment that documents it); and the island's degradation gate read `milestones.length === 0` when what decides whether anything is pickable is `targets` — a project whose phases are ALL cancelled rendered a live picker whose only row was the checked "No milestone", a dead control whose key was disabled. **Security trace, no finding:** the `milestoneId` row's CLIENT_VISIBLE-ness is pre-authorised by the DB CHECK; the row carries only refs; `Milestone` is class B so an internal phase does not resolve for a contact; and `oldRef`/`newRef` are on `PORTAL_FORBIDDEN_COLUMNS` besides. It also caught the service's own comment over-claiming what Phase 3 would render. **Round 2 (4):** the `hasChoice` fix read the OPTIMISTIC value, so in that all-cancelled project clearing the last phase unmounted the popover out from under Radix's close AND took `usePanelCommit`'s live region with it on the committing render (`AssigneeField` is safe from this only by luck — its gate is a prop a pick cannot move); the corrected comment ranked a Vitest grep ABOVE a Postgres policy, when the grep reads only files named exactly `portal.ts` and matches camelCase identifiers; the rail comment still said "six pickers … S A P E D V"; UI.md's row-existence sentence was looser than the code. **Round 3 (4 more, on the fixes):** the early return dropped `<PropertyPicker>` while leaving `open` true in island state, so a gate that closed and reopened — a colleague cancelling the last live phase, then un-cancelling it — would have mounted the popover ALREADY OPEN and pulled focus out of whatever the member was typing (closed by an `open && !gate → setOpen(false)` adjusted during render, `PickerBody`'s own pattern); It had never failed in the six previous CI runs and the slice does not touch it (the diff under `backlog/` is the `MAX_TITLE_LENGTH` constant, value unchanged). **What the trace proves:** at the moment the reload resolved the SSR page already had its 60 initial rows and its bottom spacer — full height, so the scroll had somewhere to land; the rename's action POST answered 200; hydration finished ~0.5 s after the scroll (the sidebar prefetches are at +0.6 s); the final window is 21 rows with a bottom spacer and no top spacer, i.e. measured at scrollY 0; **no console message and no page error in either attempt's trace** (so a hydration recovery, which would log, is not evidenced). **What it does not prove:** what moved the scroll back to 0. Locally the test passed 3/3 on the committed build, and a throwaway probe that reloads the big backlog and scrolls at once under 1×/4×/8× CPU throttling saw the scroll land at the bottom every time and the window follow as soon as hydration measured (5 s later at 8×). **A product-side "fix" was written and WITHDRAWN on review:** a `measure()` when the table's scroll listener attaches, to catch a scroll landing between the measuring layout effect and the listener — the fix-delta lens read React 19.2's scheduler and showed the gap does not exist on the reload path (the layout effect's `setMeasured` from `null` forces a sync re-render, and `performSyncWorkOnRoot` flushes the passive effect before paint), so the line was a no-op with a false comment; and it showed the evidence contradicts a missed-event theory anyway (a missed event leaves the page at the BOTTOM over blank spacer; the screenshot is the top). Two candidates remain, both outside the app's code: Chromium's reload scroll restoration landing after a programmatic scroll (it overrides a script scroll, never a user's) with a saved offset of 0, or a transient document-height collapse that clamps scrollY. **What shipped:** `work.spec.ts` scrolls to the end UNTIL the target row is visible (`scrollToEndUntil`, every one-shot `scrollTo` in the file) and RECORDS any retry as a `scroll-retried` test annotation with the final scrollY, so the reset class this would otherwise mask stays visible in the report; a window that never follows a scroll still fails (a repeat `scrollTo` to the same offset dispatches nothing). **Open, recorded:** if the annotation ever appears in a CI report, the trace of that run is the next evidence; a member cannot hit this by hand (a wheel is many events, and the browser restores their position on reload), so it is not a product bug until shown to be. The flake is `scoping.spec.ts:60` (the employee sign-in timeout on record), green on retry. **The failure: `item-properties.spec.ts:679`, the ⌘K-from-the-due-date-picker test, BOTH attempts** — the `?` overlay, opened from the palette's "Keyboard shortcuts" row, still open 30 s after Escape with the palette confirmed gone. **Third recorded occurrence** (run 34757971735 on 2026-09-13; once locally tonight on a build WITHOUT the shared-wrapper Escape change; it passed in run 34907609420 on a build WITH it — the slice's Escape work is not the cause). **Reproduced locally: 1 failure in 6 runs of the test alone**, and the failing trace shows the Escape one poll after the palette's dialog left the DOM. **The mechanism, as the fix-delta lens established it from React 19.2's scheduler and Radix's source** (my first reading was wrong and its "fix" was withdrawn before commit): Radix attaches a layer's document-level Escape listener in a passive effect keyed on "am I the highest layer", which becomes true only in the re-render the layer's own registration forces — a DefaultLane Scheduler task, two tasks after the click — while the closing palette's listener is removed in a passive cleanup. The palette's 120 ms exit animation can batch its removal into that very render, and then the overlay's listener attaches only in that commit's deferred flush: an Escape pressed after the palette's node is gone but before that flush meets the palette's listener, still the highest layer, which takes the key for a dialog already closed, and the overlay stays open. **What is NOT a signal:** focus inside the overlay — its `FocusScope` focuses synchronously at the click, long before the listener exists (that was my first fix; eight local passes proved nothing against a one-in-six baseline, and the lens showed the wait could not close the window in any interleaving). Nothing observable in the DOM lands in the same flush as the listener. **What shipped:** the file's own idiom in reverse — the test presses Escape again only while the overlay is still `data-state="open"` (a stray second press during its exit is a no-op and cannot reach the picker, whose listener is not back yet) and records that it was needed as an `escape-retried` annotation, so the race stays visible in the report. **Not a member's bug:** a person cannot press a key inside that window. **THE MACHINE.** The build session (17:52–19:37) died twice. VS Code's main.log: `renderer process gone (reason: oom)` at 18:22:25 and 19:37:24; Windows Event 2004 "low virtual memory" seconds before each; the extension host exits when its window dies and the Claude Code CLI is its child. Windows does not OOM-kill selectively; allocations fail and V8 processes abort. **Recovery:** this session read the dead transcript (its last 30 minutes were four failed Turbopack builds and a fifth, `next build --webpack` with `cpus: 2`, that PASSED after the session was already dead), closed Comet (free commit 4.5 → 16.8 GB), re-ran the review with READ-ONLY agents and no build in flight, and finished. **Two rules, now in AGENTS.md and in memory:** review agents never compile or test — the implementing session runs each gate once — and no build runs while agents are in flight. **THE REVIEWS: `/code-review high` (8 finders), 5 custom lenses (service read · client runtime · security and visibility · UI/i18n/a11y · tests and docs), `/security-review` (no finding above threshold; one hardening note), then 2 lenses on the fix delta.** 53 raw items, 39 distinct; **0 HIGH, 1 MED, the rest LOW** — and the one worth the headline was found by THREE finders independently: **`activityCursor` accepted ANY well-formed UUID as an `id <` bound**, so a stale link, another task's row id or the task's own id was a FILTER: `?before=<older stranger>` rendered "No older activity — everything before this point has already been shown" for a task with a full history, and a newer one rendered the newest page under a "Latest activity" button linking to itself — while the doc said "a cursor that is not a row id is the newest page". **SESSION (2026-09-13, after slice 7) — THE REPOSITORY IS PUBLIC. THE FOUNDER'S DECISION, REVERSING 9 SEPTEMBER'S NO, TAKEN WITH THE MEASUREMENT IN HAND; AND THE ONE THING THE CODE SCAN COULD NOT SEE WAS IN THE ACTIONS LOGS.**

**THE DECISION.** At 1,746 of 2,000 included Actions minutes with 18 days of the cycle left, the founder asked to publish `azcheema/fortleva`. Re-measured per repository since 1 September (jobs API, per-job ceil): manecab 1,370 — all but 21 of it on 1–5 September, idle since — fortleva 421, four small sites 154; Dependabot's 113 are free. So **9 September's second reason no longer held: fortleva is now the forward burn, 18 billable minutes per push** (isolation 4 + browser 14), and 254 minutes was ~14 pushes. I recommended keeping it private with a capped overage budget (GitHub bills $0.006/min for Linux 2-core; ~$2–6 for the rest of September at this month's pace); the founder chose to publish. **Visibility: PUBLIC since 2026-09-13.** It is the second time: the 2026-09-01 entry below records making it "PRIVATE AGAIN" once that month's quota reset, so the August docs and logs were public before. GitHub reports 0 forks and 0 stars, so nothing was forked in that window.

**PRE-FLIGHT, ALL READ-ONLY.** GitHub held only `main` (no other branch, no PR refs), all present locally. **Full-history scan, 1,831 blobs: no credentials** — the only key/value hits are test-user passwords in `auth.dbtest.ts`/`auth-audit.dbtest.ts` and CSS token names on `/settings/design`; no `npg_` Neon password, no key files ever committed, no personnummer-shaped strings, and the phone-shaped strings are fixtures (`+46 70 123…`) and one float coefficient. **Personal data that is now public is the founder's own:** name and Gmail address in `scripts/seed-naxdor.ts` since the first commit, and the author email on all 194 commits. `docs/` (pricing in 10 files, SEK figures in 11, roadmap, competitor analysis, MRR/churn) — accepted by the founder. There is no LICENSE file, so the code is visible but not licensed for reuse.

**THE ACTIONS LOGS, WHICH BECOME PUBLIC TOO.** A scan of all 79 runs (20 had no retrievable logs) found no credential, no JWT, no real email — but **Prisma's `migrate deploy` prints `Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "neondb", schema "public" at "ep-….c-6.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech"`**, the full endpoint host of the database that holds the real Naxdor tenant, in **31 logs**: 29 pre-container CI runs (8–31 August) and both `neon-smoke` dispatches. GitHub masks a secret only as its WHOLE string, never the host inside it. **Those 31 logs were deleted before publishing** (`DELETE /repos/…/actions/runs/{id}/logs`; the run records and results remain; the API then answers 404 for the run's and its jobs' logs). *Verification trap:* `gh run view --log` kept showing the host after the deletion — it serves a LOCAL cache of logs it has downloaded; verify with `gh api --method HEAD -i …/runs/{id}/logs`, never with it. **`neon-smoke.yml` now masks the hosts** in a step after the ref guard (`::add-mask::` of each URL's host and its `ep-…` id), so future dispatches should print `***` — ~~unverified until the first dispatch, whose log must be checked for `neon.tech`~~ **VERIFIED 2026-09-14: dispatch run [34897726442](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/34897726442) (success, 21 min — the six pooler-sensitive files against real Neon from a US runner) prints `Datasource "db": PostgreSQL database "neondb", schema "public" at "***"`, and its 555 log lines hold zero occurrences of the host domain or the endpoint id (31 masked values). Checked by counting matches, never by printing lines.** **It is committed with this entry and MUST reach GitHub before the next neon-smoke dispatch.** *(It did.)*

**AFTER THE FLIP.** Secret scanning and push protection are ON (non-provider patterns, validity checks and Dependabot security updates left off — the founder's call). Fork pull requests from first-time contributors need approval (GitHub's default, confirmed). `ci.yml` holds no secrets and both workflows declare `permissions: contents: read`, so a fork PR can run CI but read nothing private. **Never attach a self-hosted runner to this repository** (any PR could run code on it) — the self-hosted option in the 2026-08-21 and 2026-09-09 notes was for a private repo. Standard runners for public repositories are larger than the private 2 vCPU / 7 GB that the 2026-09-09 concurrency revert assumed, and they bill nothing: re-measure CI on the next push rather than trusting the old per-job figures. AGENTS.md gained the public-repository rule.

**SESSION (2026-09-13, later) — PANEL SLICE 7: `A` AND `V`, AND THE LAST UNLOCKED DIFFS. THE HEADLINE IS A GUARD THAT WAS RIGHT BY COINCIDENCE: THE PANEL'S NO-OP CHECK COMPARED A PICK AGAINST WHAT WAS SHOWN, WHICH WAS THE PENDING PICK ONLY BECAUSE EVERY ISLAND HAD BEEN OPTIMISTIC — THE FIRST NON-OPTIMISTIC ONE DROPPED A MEMBER'S REVERSAL AND LEFT THE TASK SHARED.**

**SHIPPED.** The item rail's Assignee and Visibility are `<PropertyPicker>` islands with the keys `A` and `V` (`item-panel/assignee-field.tsx`, `visibility-field.tsx`), on the peek and the full page, in the rail order `S A P E D V` (which is also the `?` overlay's and the palette's). `A` lists every ACTIVE member of the tenant in the order the backlog's cell and the board's lanes use (one `activeMembers` read, `joinedAt` then `id`), the current one checked in place, a checked "Unassigned" row leading only while nothing is set and "Unassign" trailing only while something is; contacts are Phase 3's. `V`'s trigger rest state IS the `<VisibilityBadge>` — the chip left the panel header for the rail, so one chip, never two that could disagree — and it is the one island that is **never optimistic** (`usePanelCommit`'s `optimistic: false`): the chip holds the canonical value until the server answers, so a refused downgrade never flashes "Private to team" over a task the client can still see, and the refusal that reaches the member is the database's own `HAS_VISIBLE_CHILDREN` sentence. Both are `ActionResult` actions with the validated `surface` (`setItemAssigneeAction`, `setItemVisibilityAction` — the last two `FormResult` property actions are gone, and the `visibility` enum is closed at the boundary rather than coerced to INTERNAL). `getItemDetail` carries `canChangeVisibility` and the members (read only for a member who can edit). **The carry-over from slice 6 is closed:** `assignItem`, `changeItemVisibility` and `setItemArchived` diff under the row lock and return canonical rows with `changed`; `moveItem` locks its own row FOR UPDATE after the queue lock and before its neighbours; the bulk verbs lock the selection under the queue lock; and the mechanism is now a module (`src/modules/work/rows.ts`): `loadItemInScope` LOCKS by default, then reads, then asserts scope, so an unlocked read is an explicit `lock: false` that only a queued writer's probe and `deleteItem`'s compare-and-set make (rank-lock.ts "THE ONE ORDER"). The picker draws the current row's check itself, beside its sr-only "(current)" words, from the one comparison; `usePanelCommit` hands each island its live region as `status`; the badge exports `VisibilityIcon`, `visibilityLabelKey` and `VISIBILITY_VALUES`, used by the chip, the picker rows and `VisibilityInlineEdit`; the backlog table's `run` toasts "Saved" only for a write that happened (`wroteSomething`, `src/lib/action-result.ts`). Docs: UI.md §5.2 (both rows and the contract paragraph), §6, §7.2, §10.4.

**THE DEFECT THE FIRST REVIEW FOUND, CONFIRMED BY A REFUTER WITH A FULL REACT-19 TRACE.** `usePanelCommit`'s no-op guard was `same(next, shown)`. On every optimistic island `shown` IS the pending pick, so the guard was right; on `V`, with `optimistic: false`, `shown` stays the canonical prop for the whole round trip — so a member who picked "Client can see" and then, before the answer landed, "Private to team" to take it back, had the reversal dropped as a no-op against the unchanged chip; the share landed, was announced, and the task ended shared against their last word. Four lenses found it independently. Fixed: the guard's basis is the newest pick IN FLIGHT (a ref set beside the sequence token, cleared only when the newest answer lands), and the failure branch now SHOWS a superseded answer rather than only announcing it — and, when nothing else answered, sets the shown value back to the prop at once (an optimistic island's revert otherwise waits for the refresh, and a retry of the failed pick in that window compared equal and was dropped; the fix-delta review's client lens found that one). The refuter also settled what NOT to do: disabling the trigger while pending, which `isPending` would drive, outlives the action through the refresh round trip, swallows `V` and flickers the overlay. **Pinned in the browser:** `e2e/item-properties.spec.ts` holds the visibility POSTs with a delayed route, picks the reversal while the first pick is in flight, and asserts a second POST and a task that ends private.

**THE REVIEWS: 10 lenses on the slice (40 raw items, 29 distinct), a security lens with no findings, 5 lenses on the first fix delta (security and lock/read: none; client 1; tests 6; docs 9), 3 on the second (fixture 2, docs 3, client 1) and a refuter on the last hook change.** The behavioural claims were adversarially verified: the reversal (CONFIRMED) and the visibility flip's lost post-wait scope re-check (CONFIRMED only at the line level — every queued writer in the module checks scope before its wait and `requireAccess` precedes every wait, so it was a consistency edit, not a lost safety property; made anyway, and it is what `rows.ts` now does for every writer). Fixed besides: the select-less archive and rank UPDATEs (512 KB descriptions read back per click), the archive action's toast-and-revalidate for a no-op (`setItemArchived` returns `changed`), the "Saved" toast for a colleague's earlier change, the bulk read pulling fifty descriptions under the queue lock, `assignItem`'s two member reads, a `joinedAt` tie in the member order, the fixture guard I had loosened to the dbtest prefixes (now a strict `assertE2ETenant` on every writing command, `big-project` and `drop-project` included — both had NO guard before), the thirteen copies of the race harness (`raceBehind`, which also races the probe against the writer's own error), and nine sentences that were false — among them my claim that locking the moved row first removes the copyWeek deadlock cycle (it only turns it around). **Recorded, not fixed:** a contact assignee (`assigneeContactId`, which nothing writes yet) would show as "Unassigned" and could not be cleared, and `assignItem`'s guard diffs only the member column — Phase 3's contact slice must design the hand-over before it writes the column; the backlog's `VisibilityInlineEdit` keeps a refused pick in its trigger's accessible name while its badge shows the server (InlineEdit's reducer, pre-existing on every select cell) and the documents table's `VisibilitySelect` is fully optimistic — one non-optimistic visibility control for all three surfaces is its own slice; four `isAuthorized` calls per panel read; `moveItem`'s lock and read as two statements; the flat `ItemDetailResult` caps beside `ItemList`'s nested ones (restructure when `L`/`M` add theirs); the raw client-visible comment literal in six test files; and the `A` picker, the backlog cell and the board lanes all list every ACTIVE member of the tenant where §5.2 says "members in scope" — narrowing all three together is a small follow-up.

**TWO e2e FAILURES, BOTH THE TESTS' OWN** *(corrected 2026-09-14 — the first is NOT settled; see the end of this paragraph)*. The ⌘K-from-picker test once found the `?` overlay still open after Escape on a loaded machine: a Radix layer registers itself and its Escape listener in passive effects, after the overlay has painted, so an Escape pressed the instant it is visible can be taken by the closing palette's layer — the test now waits for the palette to be GONE first. And the new reversal test ended mid-assertion with "Route is already handled": `page.unroute` auto-continues a request a delayed handler still holds, and the handler's own `continue` then throws — the hold is a flag now, never an unroute. **CORRECTION (2026-09-14):** `item-properties.spec.ts:679` flaked AGAIN in run [34757971735](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/34757971735) on `94c62cf`, which already carried the wait-for-the-palette-to-be-gone fix — the `?` overlay stayed open after Escape with the palette confirmed gone — so "the test's own" was wrong about this one. It may be a real race: Escape failing to close the shortcuts overlay opened from the palette over an open picker. Second recorded occurrence; open. Reproduce it before touching a timeout (the toast flake's lesson).
