**SESSION (2026-09-13) — PANEL SLICE 6: P, E AND D, AN IN-HOUSE CALENDAR, AND ONE ACTION PER PROPERTY. THE HEADLINE IS A MEASUREMENT: THE ANNOUNCEMENT THIS SLICE WAS DESIGNED AROUND DOES NOT HAPPEN, AND ONLY A BROWSER COULD SAY SO.**

**SHIPPED.** The item rail's Priority, Estimate and Due date are `<PropertyPicker>` islands with the keys `P E D`, on the peek and on the full page (`item-panel/priority-field.tsx`, `estimate-field.tsx`, `due-date-field.tsx`), and all four rail pickers share ONE commit path, `usePanelCommit`. `PropertyPicker` grew two optional seams: `derive` (one row parsed from the typed query — E's `90m`, D's `2031-03-14`) and `footer` (non-list content AFTER the cmdk root, inside the popover — D's calendar, because cmdk's root owns Enter, ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Home and End for every descendant). Its row model moved to the pure, table-tested `src/lib/picker-rows.ts`. `CalendarGrid` is built in-house on `week.ts` + `Intl` (`src/lib/calendar.ts`, `src/lib/due-date.ts`): an ARIA grid starting on the tenant's `ui.weekStart`, ISO week numbers when `ui.showIsoWeek`, and today/tomorrow/next week resolved in the zone the SERVER resolved, never the browser's. **The ActionResult migration:** the backlog's four property setters (`setItemStateAction`, `setItemPriorityAction`, `setItemEstimateAction`, `setItemDueDateAction`) take an object with a validated `surface` enum (`backlog · board-peek · backlog-peek · page` → `itemReturnTo`, the MFA step-up return address, built only from validated values) and return the canonical row with `changed`; the table and the panel share them, and `setPanelStateAction` is gone. `updateItemFields` returns what the column STORED through an inline `select` and writes nothing on a no-op; it and `changeState` now diff under the item's row lock (`lockItemRow`, `rank-lock.ts`). Trigger-less dialogs — the palette, MovePicker, the `?` overlay, the shell's More sheet — return focus where they were opened (`useFocusReturn`), and the shared `TooltipTrigger` refuses the returning focus event so a return never opens a tooltip. Also: the `Command` wrapper defaults `vimBindings` to false (Ctrl+K inside "Move to…" now reaches the palette); `KeyboardHint` speaks "or"/"then"; state option test ids are per-category ordinals over the FULL list (`statePickerTargets`), closing slice 5's disposition; and the C0 bug — `durationInputText` seeded 1,000 h as "1,000h", which parsed back as 60 minutes (the round-trip test failed 3 of 4 cases before the fix). Docs: UI.md §5.2/§6/§7.2/§8/§9/§10.15, ARC-24 (`date-fns` and `Intl.DurationFormat` struck), and the AGENTS.md trap list.

**THE MEASUREMENT.** The design seeded the highlight `""` and listed the current state first so that cmdk would light the row itself — "the only path that sets `aria-activedescendant`, so the row is announced". Two review verifiers traced cmdk's source and agreed. **A headless browser disproved it**: the fix pass's e2e author bundled the real picker with the real cmdk 1.1.1 and measured, and a throwaway probe spec then re-measured it in the REAL app, against the production build (not committed): E opened unset — the "No estimate" row `aria-selected`, `aria-activedescendant` absent; E after typing `90m` — the derived row selected, attribute absent; P opened — absent; P after ArrowDown — the attribute names LOW, correctly. A row cmdk lights BY ITSELF is `aria-selected`, but cmdk assigns the attribute inside its layout flush, from a DOM that has not re-rendered, so it stays unset — or, after a typed derived row, names the row lit before. Only ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End or a click set it. **Recorded as an OPEN DEFECT, not fixed:** no seed is announced until the member steers. It cannot change a write — Enter acts on `aria-selected` — and the trigger's label speaks the value before the picker opens. The fix is active-descendant wiring of our own, which wants its own slice. *The lesson is the familiar one in a new place: an instrument that reads code cannot see the event loop, and a trace through minified library source is still reading code.* **Correction to slice 5's record** (its paragraph "Three more real defects, each invisible to the tests I had written", left as written): its claim that the picker's controlled seed on a disabled row "became the input's `aria-activedescendant`" is false against cmdk 1.1.1 — the controlled-value effect sets only the store's value and never `selectedItemId`, so no controlled seed has ever set that attribute.

**THE FIRST INDEPENDENT REVIEW: 7 lenses, 46 agents, 19 findings, each verified by a refuter and a reproducer — 16 upheld, 2 split, 1 refuted.** The one that mattered: **F04** — E and D used ONE cmdk value, `none`, for both the checked "No estimate" row and the "Remove estimate" row, and nothing re-seeded the highlight while the picker was open, so the board's 12 s poll could turn a highlighted no-op into a clear beneath the member's Enter and erase a colleague's value. Fixed three ways: distinct `none`/`clear` values, re-settling the highlight when the value changes under an open picker, and an Enter guard that refuses a highlight the member did not steer to (cmdk re-picks its first row by itself when the lit row unmounts, and in controlled mode no prop can take that back). **F16, a split verdict, REVERSES slice 5's choice:** seeding the first enabled row for a disabled current state let an employee's bare Enter reopen a gated Done task they could not re-close; now nothing is lit and Enter is inert until the first ArrowDown. **F05/F06:** palette rows could stack a second picker on an open one, and a dialog nothing opens from a trigger dropped focus on `<body>` on close, where every single key acted behind the layer still open; now `paletteOffersPageRows` and one `useFocusReturn` hook, which cannot coexist with a child's `autoFocus` (a scan in `keymap.test.ts` pins that). **F03:** D's ~450px popover ran off a 667px phone with nothing that could scroll — capped at the Radix available height. **F07** (split, fixed; refined by G04 below): the selected day's border was the focus ring's own indigo. **F19:** `updateItemFields` diffed against an unlocked read, so two concurrent edits wrote client-visible due-date history from a row version the UPDATE did not replace — now `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` first. Also F12 (sr-only "(current)"), F13 (a superseded commit no longer adopts or announces), F14 (December 2100's empty week row), F15, F18, and four false doc claims (F01, F08–F10). **F17 dismissed**, refuted by both verifiers.

**ONE DEFECT NO TEST AND NO REVIEWER RAISED — THE SWEEP'S SCREENSHOTS DID.** 32px picker triggers beside 20px text values put every picker's label 6px above its value on four of seven rail rows, in both themes, while the craft audit passed. Fixed with one row geometry (`min-h-8`; UI.md §10.15 pattern 7). *Look at the shots; a green sweep only proves nothing threw.*

**THE BROWSER FOUND A BUG IN THE FIX ITSELF.** `useFocusReturn` worked for one dialog and failed for a CHAIN: the palette's "Keyboard shortcuts" row runs `onOpenChange(false); fn()` — the palette closes and the `?` overlay opens in ONE batch — so the overlay's FocusScope mounted while the palette, still playing its exit animation, held focus, and recorded the palette's search input as its origin. The palette's own deferred restore (Radix dispatches the unmount event from a `setTimeout` after the exit) rightly skipped, because the overlay held focus; the overlay's restore then aimed at a node that no longer existed, and focus fell to `<body>` over the still-open picker — the exact leak F06 was about. The e2e assertion added for the overlay failed on its first run (19 passed / 1 failed). The fix is a registry keyed by the FocusScope container (`event.target` of both Radix events): a dialog opened from inside a CLOSING focus-returning dialog inherits that dialog's origin, while one opened over a dialog that stays open returns focus into it. *Code reading approved the single-dialog version; only a real sequence of two dialogs showed the second one's origin was already stale.*

**THE FIX-DELTA REVIEW (founder rule: fixes are slices): 5 lenses, 36 agents, 15 findings over exactly the fix delta (git trees `d224e43` → `27def25`, snapshotted through a temporary index so untracked files were in the diff) — 12 upheld, 1 split, 2 refuted.** It independently found the same chained-dialog focus bug the browser did (G03). The rest, all fixed unless noted: **G02** the shell's "More" sheet is also a trigger-less dialog and did not return focus; **G04** dropping the selected day's line (F07) left selection at ~1.02:1 in dark, fainter than hover — the line is back and steps aside only under `focus-visible`; **G05** a re-seed leaves `aria-activedescendant` on the last steered row (part of the recorded defect; comments corrected); **G06** `changeState` had F19's unlocked-read race too — `lockItemRow` moved to `rank-lock.ts` and guards both single-row writers; **G08** when the newest pick fails after an earlier one answered, that answer's value is now announced; **G09** no test exercised F04's protection — now driven in e2e with TWO pages of one session: the watcher holds E open in the BOARD's peek, which is the only surface that refreshes an open peek by itself (`board.tsx`'s 12 s `/api/version` poll; the backlog and the item page have no poll), while the colleague page sets the estimate; after the poll the new value's row is lit and a bare Enter posts nothing, and a typed `3h` survives the refresh and commits; **G10/G11** one rule (`highlightAfterChange`) now decides whether a steered highlight survives a value or options change — only while its row is still rendered, enabled, in the same group and not the old value's row, or is the typed derived row; **G12** returning focus to a tooltip-wrapped button reopened its tooltip, which ate the next Escape; **G13** ⌘K during the palette's exit animation reopened it without page rows — now judged by where the closing dialog returns focus; **G15** the race dbtests' lock-wait probe matched any waiter on the server — now scoped to the colleague's xid. **G14 split, recorded not fixed:** `bulkSetPriority` diffs rows it read under the rank lock but did not row-lock (pre-existing, outside this delta). **G01 refuted** (the "PLAN §0" pointers are forward references to this entry) and **G07 refuted**. Two refinements the fixers made to the lead's brief, both kept: the staged focus-return registry inherited from ANY enclosing dialog — so ⌘K over the still-open `?` overlay would have sent focus behind it — and now only a CLOSING dialog hands its origin on; and a ⌘K landing in a closing dialog is judged by where that dialog RETURNS focus, not treated as "no layer", which would have re-offered page rows over a picker still open.

**THE SECOND FIX DELTA'S REVIEW (`27def25` → `7b43cad`): 5 lenses, 24 agents, 9 findings — 6 upheld, 2 split, 1 refuted.** **H01** (medium) is the one worth remembering: the tooltip guard G12 added was OPT-IN per call site — three shell triggers — so a return still opened the Download button's tooltip inside the item peek, and its layer ate the Escape that should have closed the peek, while UI.md and AGENTS.md already claimed "a return never opens a tooltip". Fixed by construction: the shared `TooltipTrigger` wrapper refuses the returning focus event for every trigger, and the per-site guards are gone. *A rule that has to be remembered at each call site is a rule that is already broken at one of them.* Also fixed: **H06** (`lastSaved` records a superseded answer whatever `changed` says), **H08** (a tautological unit test deleted), **H04/H05** (two e2e assertions that passed with their bug present, hardened). **Recorded, not fixed:** **H02** (board drops and `bulkChangeState` still diff unlocked reads), **H07** and **H09** (below). **H03** refuted.

**THE THIRD FIX DELTA'S REVIEW (`7b43cad` → `8a13fc1`): 3 lenses, 10 agents, 3 findings — 2 upheld, 1 split, all low, none a behaviour defect in the slice.** **J01:** the tooltip assertion added after the second Escape could not catch the late tooltip its comment named — a tooltip that opens late takes that Escape and closes, so every check after it passes — and the comment now claims only what the assertion proves. **J02:** `usePanelCommit`'s premise that an earlier pick's answer always lands before a later one's is false when a NAVIGATION is dispatched while an action is pending: Next marks that action discarded and starts the next queued one while the first fetch is still in flight (`app-router-instance.js` `dispatchAction`), so answers can land out of order and `lastSaved` may name an older answer — pre-existing (the same sequence fails on `7b43cad`), recorded, premise comment corrected. **J03** (split): a code comment's "recorded residue (PLAN §0)" pointer — this entry is that record. *The J01/J02 fixes are comments only and cannot change behaviour, so they take no fourth review round (the scope carve-out in the independent-review rule).*

**TWO LOCAL e2e FAILURES, BOTH EXPLAINED, NEITHER THE SLICE.** (1) `work.spec.ts:410` once hit Next's global error page: the server log's digest named `PrismaClientKnownRequestError P2028` — the backlog render's interactive transaction took 5,911 ms against the 5,000 ms timeout, on the Neon dev database; the spec re-ran 13/13. (2) `theme.spec.ts:86` failed in 0 ms with "worker process exited unexpectedly (code=3221226505)" — a Windows 0xC0000409 crash of the Playwright worker, not the app; it re-ran 4/4. *Read the server log's digest before calling either a flake or a regression.*

**VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT (final tree):** typecheck · eslint 0 · unit **964 / 1 skipped** (was 857) · `pnpm build` · e2e **93 passed / 1 armed-skip, 0 failed** on the final tree's production build, in four batches (was 84 passed / 1 armed-skip) · the sweep at an unchanged 48 stops / 192 shots (on the reviewed build; no later delta changes a photographed stop). **NOT run locally: `pnpm test:db`** — the canonical-row, no-op and five row-lock race dbtests (two for `updateItemFields`, three for `changeState`) are CI's to prove from empty, so the first push is their first run. **CI run [34748014849](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/34748014849) on `360319c`: FULLY GREEN.** Isolation 3m41s incl. **test:db 32 files / 392 tests** from empty (385 → 392: exactly the seven new dbtests, the five row-lock race tests among them); browser harness 13m21s, **95 passed / 2 flaky / 1 skipped** (the 94 specs plus the sweep's 4 walks). Neither flaky test is this slice's: `scoping.spec.ts:60` timed out in its `beforeEach` at the employee SIGN-IN (`waitForURL('**/home')`, 30 s), before any page rendered; `visibility.spec.ts:170` is the known toast flake (founder item 3 — root cause still not established), failing exactly as before, with the expected failure string never reaching a toast. Both passed on retry.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT DONE.** (1) The announcement defect above. (2) **Slice-7 carry-over — writers that still diff an unlocked read:** `assignItem`, `setItemArchived`, `changeItemVisibility` (single-row: add `lockItemRow`), and `bulkSetPriority`, `bulkChangeState`, `moveItem` (multi-row, under the rank lock: row-lock the selection or derive history from RETURNING); `assignItem` and `changeItemVisibility` are also still `FormResult` actions with a hardcoded backlog return address. (3) `updateItemFields` and `changeState` take the row lock BEFORE the scope check: an out-of-scope member with a guessed item id holds it for the milliseconds until `assertInScope` refuses; RLS still isolates tenants. (4) **H09:** `PickerBody` keys groups by heading, so a workflow whose categories interleave by rank gets duplicate group keys, and a steered row can then be remounted under a re-rank and re-picked by cmdk while still steered — needs a stable group identity across filtering and re-rank. (5) **H07:** a dialog opened inside a closing popover's exit window (a picker's Escape, then ⌘K, within one `--dur-instant`) returns focus nowhere. (6) **J02:** out-of-order action answers after a mid-flight navigation. (7) The item peek's Sheet does not return focus (its close is a navigation), and the tooltip guard covers returns made by `useFocusReturn` only — Radix's own trigger returns are not flagged (no tooltip wraps such a trigger today). (8) `tree-guards.dbtest.ts` keeps its own cluster-wide lock-wait probe (G15's defect, older). (9) The ⌘K double-tap during the palette's exit (G13) has no e2e — inherently racy; keymap unit cases guard it. (10) `ui.showIsoWeek` governs only the calendar; `/time`, `/time/team` and `/home` print week numbers regardless (pre-existing). (11) MovePicker: Ctrl+J/K/N/P no longer move its highlight (the `vimBindings` default).

**FOUR DECISIONS, RATIFIED BY THE FOUNDER 2026-09-13 — each the default the slice shipped; settled, do not re-litigate:** (1) the calendar follows `ui.weekStart` — the settings hint already promises "calendars … start on this day"; (2) "Next week" = the first day of the next grid week, each token row showing its resolved date; (3) the backlog table's S/P/E/D cells stay `InlineEdit` until a table-density trigger exists; (4) `date-fns` 4 + `@date-fns/tz` struck from ARC-24 — never installed, and a second week-number path.

**NEXT:** slice 7 (`V` / `A`, carrying item 2 above), then Activity, subtasks, comments. Still owed outside the panel: nothing creates an EPIC.


**SESSION (2026-09-12, later still again) — PANEL SLICE 5: ONE KEYBOARD DISPATCHER, A `?` OVERLAY THAT CANNOT LIE, AND THE FIRST PropertyPicker. THE HEADLINE IS AGAIN A METHOD LESSON: MY OWN E2E FOUND A BUG THAT KILLED EVERY KEY IN THE APP, AND TWO OF MY PASSING TESTS PASSED *BECAUSE* IT WAS BROKEN.**

**SHIPPED.** The scope registry is **hand-rolled, not `react-hotkeys-hook`** (UI.md §6 and ARC-24 both amended; ARC-24 records the four specific reasons it lost — it adds listeners rather than removing them, its scopes cannot shadow, its scope activation is unrefcounted global state, and **its sequence branch never calls `preventDefault`**, which is the exact `G T` bug this codebase wrote `isGoSequencePending()` to kill). `src/lib/keymap.ts` holds the pure `decide()`; `use-hotkeys.ts` holds the scope store and **ONE** window listener at bubble phase. **Three window listeners became one**, and three workarounds deleted themselves with it: the board's `{capture:true}` phase (it existed only to see an armed `G` before the shell cleared it), the timer pill's double `defaultPrevented`+`isGoSequencePending` guard, and the pill's key-owner election. `isApplePlatform` is gone (no importer; `keyboard-hint.tsx` has the better twin). `isGoSequencePending` survives with exactly ONE caller — `board.tsx`'s React-tree handler, which runs at document-bubble, before the dispatcher, and has no other way to see an armed `G`.

**`peekOpen` was DELIBERATELY KEPT** as the board scope's `enabled` value rather than replaced by a containment / transparency / layer-depth rule. All three proposed replacements were worse: one was self-flagged by its own author as the likeliest bug, one is a heuristic about where focus is, and one is provably wrong on a deep link to `/board?item=KEY-1`, where the board and the SheetContent mount in the SAME commit.

**THE BUG THE BROWSER FOUND, AND WHY NOTHING ELSE COULD.** The `?` overlay registered its modal scope with `exclusive: true` **unconditionally** — open or closed — with an empty binding list while closed. `modal` is the top of `SCOPE_ORDER`, so the dispatcher met it first, matched nothing, and took the exclusive break. **Every single key in the application was dead.** The 32 new unit tests all passed, because they test `decide()` and `decide()` was right; the overlay's *registration* is the thing they cannot see. Worse, **two of my ten e2e tests passed while the whole keyboard was broken** — both assert an ABSENCE ("no picker opens inside the editor", "`?` does not fire behind an open menu"), which is exactly what a dead keyboard produces. *A negative assertion is not evidence that the mechanism works; it is evidence only that it did not misfire.* The fix is one word (`exclusive: open`) and it is now pinned by a unit test named "the footgun", because the semantic itself is right — a modal with no keys really should own the keyboard.

**A DEFECT I REPORTED AND THEN DISPROVED — the correction is the useful part.** I claimed, in this section and in `990daad`'s commit message, that **`Escape` does not close the item peek on the board**, and said I had verified it as pre-existing by stashing the slice and reproducing on `f216963`. **That was wrong, and the method was the reason.** Every diagnostic I ran used a fixed `waitForTimeout(1500)` and then counted the peek. Closing the peek is a SERVER NAVIGATION — `PeekShell` pushes the list URL and the surface re-renders — and it takes **~3.4 s** on this machine. Re-measured with a polling assertion it closes every time: board via `?item=` URL 3386 ms, board via the row menu 3367 ms, backlog via URL 2898 ms. The tell was there and I walked past it: the same fixed-wait diagnostic also "failed" on the BACKLOG, whose behaviour `work.spec.ts:266-276` has pinned green for weeks, and it "failed" for the sheet's own CLOSE BUTTON, which has nothing to do with Escape. Two independent contradictions of my own hypothesis, both visible in the output I had already read. *A fixed sleep is not a measurement; a disagreement between a new diagnostic and a green shipped test is the diagnostic's problem until proven otherwise.* The `e2e/keymap.spec.ts` ladder now asserts BOTH rungs on the board (and again on the backlog, a different mount) with a polling budget, so the real contract is pinned rather than a rumour. **Nothing is owed here, and no slice is needed.** The honest residual observation is only that closing the peek costs a round trip — which the repo's own 20 s test budgets already assume.

**THE PICKER HAS NO TOOLTIP ON ITS TRIGGER, on evidence rather than taste.** Radix opens a tooltip on FOCUS, and Radix returns focus to the trigger when the popover closes — so the tooltip is open the instant the picker shuts, its dismissable layer is then the highest, and the member's next Escape is spent closing a tooltip they never asked for (measured: `tooltip-content` count 1 immediately after the picker closed, and the following Escape dismissed it and nothing else). The key is advertised three other ways — the `?` overlay row, the ⌘K "On this page" row, and `aria-keyshortcuts`. *Removing the tooltip did NOT fix the board-peek Escape defect above; the two are unrelated, and the experiment is what proved it.*

**TWO BEHAVIOUR FIXES IN PASSING.** (1) `?` **toggles** now — it was `setOverlayOpen(true)`, so it could open the overlay and never close it. (2) **A key no longer leaks through an open menu**: Radix traps focus, not events, so `t` behind an open `RowActions` menu used to stop the running timer (a menu item is not an editable target). Suppression is target-based over the components' own `data-slot`s, and a unit test parses `src/components/ui/*.tsx` to prove every selector names a slot that is actually emitted — `dialog-content`/`sheet-content` are deliberately ABSENT, because the peek is a dialog and must keep its keys.

**A FREE EFFICIENCY FIX, found while making the write satisfy §7.2.** `transitionState`'s `tx.workItem.update` had **no `select`**, so it returned the whole row — the 512 KB ProseMirror `description` included — on every board drop, every bulk change, every import and every create-into-a-column, and threw it away. It now selects five columns and RETURNS them, which is how §7.2's "a mutation returns the canonical row" is satisfied at zero query cost. `changed: false` is a real value: a no-op move writes no row, no activity and no audit, and the dbtest counts rows before and after to prove it.

**RULE 7 IS CLOSED, AND TWO SURFACES ARE UNBLOCKED.** The `?` overlay and the palette's new "On this page" group are both projections of the same live snapshot the dispatcher acts on, so a surface ships a key by adding ONE `useScopeKeys` call and gets both for free. The overlay used to omit three keys that already shipped (board `C`, board `S`, global `T`); it cannot any more. **`bulk-bar.tsx` and `inbox-list.tsx` both shipped zero keys citing this exact blocker — their stated reason is now false.** What remains for them is the product question of what each verb should do, not a mechanism.

**THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW (founder rule): 6 lenses, 66 agents, 37 findings, each verified by TWO adversaries — a refuter told to default to REFUTED and a reproducer told to walk the execution path or refute. 20 upheld, 11 distinct, all fixed but two.** The reviewers had the diff and the rules, never the implementation reasoning.

**The one that mattered most is the standing trap in a shape I had not seen it take.** `changed: false` came back from the server and the client `return`ed early — no refresh. But `changed: false` does not mean "nothing to do"; it means **the server disagreed with the props this panel rendered from**, because someone else had already moved the item there. The optimistic value then unwound to the STALE prop: the member's pick appeared to revert, with no toast, and the panel stayed wrong until a full reload. On the item PAGE — which has no 12 s poll — it stayed wrong indefinitely. *"An action failure must never look like a revert" has a silent-success form, and this was it.* Both branches now adopt the canonical row and refresh.

**Three more real defects, each invisible to the tests I had written.** (1) The picker seeded its highlight from the current VALUE without checking whether that option was `disabled` — so for an item in TRIAGE, or in a gated Done under a non-approver, the current state was marked `aria-selected`, became the input's `aria-activedescendant`, and **Enter did nothing at all**, because cmdk attaches its select listener only to enabled items. (2) Worse, my re-seed lived in `onOpenChange`, which **Radix never calls for a controlled popover opened programmatically** — so the reset never ran for the `S` key, the way this control is actually meant to be used. Both are now structural rather than remembered: the list's state lives in a child that only exists while the popover is open, so Radix's own unmount IS the reset. (3) The sr-only `role="status"` was always mounted AND always non-empty, leaving "State changed to To do" standing in the accessibility tree of a task nobody had touched, on every peek open. It is mounted and silent now, and speaks only after a commit.

**Two the review caught in my own test code, which is the half I would have defended.** (a) The `?` overlay rendered **two sections both headed "Global"** — the literal one and the registry's projection — because `shell.shortcuts.global` and `scopes.global` resolve to the same word; found independently by four lenses. The literal rows are not the `global` scope (⌘K is answered ahead of every scope; Esc belongs to Radix), so they got their own heading and the orphaned key was deleted. (b) The whole `DECLARED` describe block was **unfalsifiable** — three assertions about a hand-written constant nothing tied to a call site, so none could fail when the bug it named appeared. `DECLARED` is deleted; the `?` overlay is the live map it was pretending to be. Its one rule worth keeping is now **structural instead of detected**: `decide()` skips any binding whose key is Escape, so registering one is not an error anyone must notice — it simply cannot match. *(A source-scanning version was written first and thrown away after it was checked: it missed the board's bindings entirely and picked up unrelated `key:` properties. A tripwire that fails open is worse than none.)*

**And one that would have poisoned the sweep silently.** The State-picker e2e drove the **seeded fixture's first board card** into a different column and never restored it — and `visual.spec` photographs that very project, so a moved card would have been baked into 192 new shots without failing anything. It creates and deletes its own task now, pass or fail, like `work.spec` does.

**Also fixed:** the ⌘K "On this page" group invoked the `run` closure captured in the **version-cached** snapshot, while the keydown path deliberately re-reads `entries[…].ref.current` because `signatureOf` cannot see a closure — so a key and its palette row could have done two different things; both go through `runScopeBinding` now. The palette's blanket exclusion of the `global` scope was wrong on its own stated grounds ("those keys already have palette rows") — the timer's `T` had neither a row nor an opt-out, so its verb was reachable by the bare key alone; the per-binding `palette: false` decides now, where it is declared. `disablePointerSelection` left the picker's rows completely inert under the cursor, so a hover surface is back (deliberately WITHOUT the `data-selected` left bar, so a mouse user can see that the hovered row and the Enter target differ). The State value was indented 10px past every other value in the rail by the trigger's own `px-2.5`. And the canonical-row dbtest's title over-claimed — on the happy path the service's `stateCategory` and the trigger's agree, so that assertion cannot by itself distinguish `RETURNING` from an echo; it is renamed to what it proves, with the honest comment.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT FIXED (2).** (1) *The picker's option test ids are keyed by CATEGORY, so the seed's two IN_PROGRESS states share one* — the identical property `MovePicker` already carries (`work.spec.ts:716` lives with `.first()`). Fixing it properly means keeping `seedKey` on `ResolvedWorkflowState`, which widens a type the board and backlog share, for a test affordance; deferred to slice 6, where `P E D` will exercise the picker API anyway, and the e2e now says in a comment why it uses `.last()`. (2) *`hint: ["J","K"]` renders with the same grammar as the ⌘+K chord*, so "either key" reads as "press both" — the fix is an `"or"` token in the shared `KeyboardHint`, which the sweep photographs; the row's own label ("Move between cards") disambiguates meanwhile.


**CI RUN [34713766519](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/34713766519) ON `990daad`: the isolation job PASSED, so the four new dbtests are proven from EMPTY — and the browser job reported `1 failed · 1 flaky · 82 passed`.** The failure is `visibility.spec.ts:170`, the **known** toast flake whose root cause is still not established (founder item 3 — do not close it as understood). The FLAKY one was mine and is fixed: `keymap.spec.ts` pressed `c` the instant the board rendered, and `useScopeKeys` registers in an EFFECT — on a CI runner the keystroke can beat hydration. A local run cannot see this; the machine is too fast. The three presses that race a scope's registration now go through a `pressUntil` helper that retries the key and is GUARDED against pressing twice (`?` toggles, and `c` types into the field it just opened, so a blind retry would undo the first press). It still fails if a binding is genuinely dead — it just stops calling a race a regression.

**VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT:** typecheck · eslint 0 · unit **857 passed / 1 skipped** (+31: the ordering matrix, the shadowing/swallow/doc-only rules, `signatureOf`'s closure-blindness, `overlaySections`, the suppression-selector scan, `enterableStates`) · `pnpm build` · **`e2e/keymap.spec.ts` 11/11** in a real browser, plus `palette` and `work` re-run green after the review fixes, and the FULL suite 84 passed / 1 armed-skip with the 192-shot sweep unchanged at 48 stops. Four dbtests added (the canonical row equals a fresh read; the no-op writes ZERO rows and leaves `updatedAt` untouched; states by rank with the RAW nullable pair; an employee's `canApprove` false) — **not run locally**: `pnpm test:db` writes to the shared Neon dev database, which a cleanup hook wiped once before, so CI's container-from-empty run is the safer equivalent.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT DONE.** (1) `MovePicker` deliberately NOT folded into `PropertyPicker` — different verb (state × position, §7.1) and the refactor would churn the category-keyed `data-testid`s `work.spec.ts:716` pins with `.first()` for the seed's two IN_PROGRESS states; it does carry a follow-up, `MovePicker` still ships cmdk's `vimBindings` defaulted TRUE. (2) `command.tsx`'s 44px `CommandInput` wrapper left un-`cn()`-able — no consumer needs a denser row yet. (3) The `inline-edit.tsx:176-187` bubble-phase Escape defect inside the peek (live today via `VisibilitySelect` in `documents-table`) RECORDED, not fixed: a bubble handler cannot beat Radix's `ownerDocument` capture handler, and the fix touches a safety-critical visibility control. (4) No new visual stop — the 48/192 count is unchanged in all its mirrors; an open popover is not a route. (5) `setItemStateAction` (FormResult) and `setPanelStateAction` (ActionResult) coexist until slice 6's migration folds them. (6) §7.2's stale-conflict revert is not implemented for the panel — it has no freshness poll and no compare-and-set token.

**FOUR TRAPS JOIN THE STANDING LIST (AGENTS.md).** (a) A hand-written Escape handler can never beat a Radix layer. (b) Two window keydown listeners will race over a key SEQUENCE — one dispatcher removes the workarounds rather than adding another. (c) cmdk's `vimBindings` defaults TRUE, so Ctrl+k inside any Command means "previous item" and shadows the global ⌘K. (d) A Prisma `update` with no `select` returns the WHOLE row — a 512 KB document included — even when the caller discards it.

**NEXT:** slice 6 (`P E D` + the calendar + the ActionResult migration), then `V`/`A`, Activity, subtasks, comments. Still owed outside the panel: nothing in the code creates an EPIC (a 2W DoD gap).


**SESSION (2026-09-12, later still) — PANEL SLICE 4: THE TIPTAP DESCRIPTION. THE SEARCH INDEX FINALLY HAS A BODY, AND THE TWO TESTS FOUND WHAT 78 REVIEW AGENTS DID NOT.** The editor, its server-side normaliser, the write path and the panel wiring; no migration. `WorkItem.descriptionText` now has a writer — the LAST of the three recon hazards (the paragraph further down is struck through), so the search index's C-weight body tier fills on the first save.

**THE HEADLINE IS A METHOD LESSON, NOT A BUG REPORT. Three defects, three different instruments, and no instrument found another's.**

1. **The dbtest found the token bug on its FIRST run.** The write handed the editor a token hashed from the document it had just SENT. jsonb does not store the bytes it is given — it re-orders every object's keys canonically, so `{"type":"text","text":"hi"}` comes back `{"text":"hi","type":"text"}`: jsonb-EQUAL, a different string, a different hash. The first save of an editing session succeeded and **every save after it was refused as stale**. Six of eleven dbtests failed on it. The fix is `RETURNING description` — hash what Postgres holds, never what this process sent. (The SQL compare-and-set was always right: jsonb-to-jsonb equality cannot care about key order.) Four of the six review lenses found this one independently too.
2. **The e2e found a bug NO review lens found — checked: zero of the 78 agents mention `Object.create`, "null-prototype", `$T` or "temporary reference".** ProseMirror builds every node's attributes with `Object.create(null)` and `toJSON()` hands that same null-prototype object out. React's server-action serialiser cannot encode it, so `attrs` crossed the wire as an opaque reference (`"attrs":"$T"` in the captured POST body) and the normaliser correctly refused the document as INVALID_INPUT. **Plain paragraphs carry no attrs, which is exactly why it hid:** the first two saves in the test passed and the checklist save did not. Every heading, link, ordered list, code block and checklist was unsaveable. The client now round-trips `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(editor.getJSON()))`. **A bug that lives only in the wire format between two libraries is invisible to code reading; it took a browser typing into the real editor.**
3. **The review found the client-state bugs neither test could.** `commit()` cleared the dirty flag when the request LEFT, and there was no `catch` at all around `await save(...)` — so a failed save left the field CLEAN, the badge stuck on "Saving…", and the next 12 s poll then REVERTED the member's words: the standing trap in its worst form. Also: unmounting inside the 2 s debounce discarded the pending save (Escape-closing the peek lost the sentence, with no blur to rescue it); the panel was not keyed by item id, so a reused panel could carry one task's text into another; and the sync effect adopted ANY differing token, including an older payload rendered before our own write.

**THE REVIEW: 6 lenses, 78 agents, 36 findings, each adversarially verified by two agents (a refuter and a reproducer).** All 36 fixed except one, dispositioned below. Fixed beyond the three above: the second parse validated NOTHING (`Node.fromJSON` does not check a node against its content expression, so a LEAF could be handed children that render nowhere and still reach `descriptionText` — **text that poisons the search index and appears on no page**; `node.check()` now recurses over content, attrs and marks); a non-`doc` root was accepted and stored; `U+0000` and lone surrogates reached Postgres as a driver 500 instead of a typed refusal; `JSON.stringify` on the untrusted body sat outside every try/catch (a BigInt is `$n` to React's decoder and a TypeError here); the size cap measured only what ARRIVED while normalisation ADDS the attributes the sender omitted; `safeHref` kept embedded credentials (`https://www.the-bank.example@evil.test/` reads as the bank — and a description can be CLIENT_VISIBLE, so the target is the tenant's own customer); `bg-surface` **is not a utility this design system defines**, so the editor box had no background at all; the focus ring was a `box-shadow`, which UI.md forbids precisely because the peek is an `overflow-y-auto` container that clips it; `role="toolbar"` had seven tab stops and no roving tabindex; `editable` was read only at construction; and Tiptap named every checklist checkbox in ENGLISH (`a11y.checkboxLabel` is now translated — it adds no node and no mark, so the server's schema is still the browser's schema).

**TWO PERFORMANCE FINDINGS WERE REAL AND MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** (1) **A board with no `?item=` in the URL was downloading 386 KB of ProseMirror** — measured in the browser, not inferred from a manifest: `item-panel.tsx` imported the editor statically, so it sat in the board's and the backlog's client graph. `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false` removes it (the editor already sets `immediatelyRender: false`, so it renders nothing server-side by design); re-measured after, that file is gone from the board's initial load. (2) `items.ts` imported `descriptionToken` from the write-path module, which reaches `normalize.ts`, which built a ProseMirror schema **at module scope** — dragging the whole editor graph into the server bundle of every route that touches `@/modules/work`. `descriptionToken` is a sha256 of some JSON and now lives in its own tiptap-free module (`description-token.ts`); the schema is built lazily.

**A FIX I MADE AND THEN UNMADE, WHICH IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF.** Three select-less `work_item.findFirst` reads (a board drag, the state machine, create) now pull a document that can be 512 KB. The tidy fix looked like a GLOBAL Prisma `omit` beside the rate ciphertext — and it would have **silently emptied every task description out of the tenant data export**, because `src/export/service.ts` dumps every model with `findMany({})` and **no test covers work items there**. Reverted to three inline `omit` literals at the reads themselves. *A global omit is a change to every reader, including the one whose whole job is to return everything.* (Prisma also loses the result type through a shared `as const` omit — it must be an inline literal.)

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT FIXED (1 of 36).** *Every autosave bumps `work_item.updated_at`, so `projectWorkVersion` changes and every OTHER open board refreshes on its next 12 s poll — every 2 s while a colleague types.* Accepted for this slice: the description IS a change to the row, the card's checklist badge really can change with it, and the alternatives are a lying `updatedAt` or a freshness token that hashes only board-visible fields — a change to ARC-18's token, which deserves its own slice rather than a hurried carve-out here. Revisit if Naxdor reports board churn.

**SHIPPED in slice 1 (migration `20260911200000_work_tree_guards`, DDL only — no neon-smoke needed):** `work_item_parent_guard` reads the parent `FOR SHARE` when a write could break child ≤ parent (an insert, a changed parent, or a row CLIENT_VISIBLE after the write) — closing the write-skew where a client-visible subtask and its parent's make-private both committed, blind to each other (the parent FK's FOR KEY SHARE never conflicted with a no-key UPDATE); a NEW parent must be live. `work_item/comment/document_restore_guard` fire ONLY on `deleted_at → NULL`: a row that died under a shared item cannot come back into view after the item went private (no restore path exists yet; the undo UI.md promises will need these). Every tree RAISE carries a token; `src/modules/work/db-errors.ts` maps the reachable ones (`HAS_VISIBLE_CHILDREN`, `PARENT_NOT_VISIBLE`, `CANNOT_NEST`) — the backlog's `V` refusal is no longer a generic failure. `deleteItem` counts children AFTER it holds the row (and refuses as `HAS_CHILDREN`, not "no permission"). The token mapper moved to `src/lib/db-error-map.ts`, shared by time and work, and refuses a token table where one token is a substring of another.

**THE REVIEW CYCLE, AND THE LESSON IN IT.** Round 1 (7 lenses, 27 agents): 14 survived — a test rank key (`zz-<uuid>`) that is an INVALID fractional key 1 time in 16 (≈11% of CI runs red), and a parent lock taken on EVERY child write, which opened new deadlock cycles (and sat on make-private, where it protects nothing). The fix narrowed the lock and took the parent's lock "first" in the services. **Round 2 (4 lenses) proved that fix wrong: the other multi-row writers lock by RANK (moveItem, in either direction) or SCAN order (bulk edits, the portal fan-out) — never by tree — so no lock order can be imposed; parent-first only moved the cycles.** A self-review of that fix had also found it deadlocked two quick subtask creates under the project's last row. **What holds instead: SERIALISE.** Every work service that locks more than one work_item row of a project now takes the project's rank advisory lock before its first row lock (`rank-lock.ts` — create, move/rebalance, bulk edits via `loadSelection`, a subtask's raise) and re-reads what it read before the wait; a writer of ONE work_item row cannot close a cycle among work_item rows with them. Make-private takes neither the rank lock nor its parent's lock — it never waits on the queue or on its parent, only on whoever holds its own row (an in-flight subtask create or raise under it included: that wait IS the write-skew fix). Pinned by dbtests that hold a stand-in move / bulk row lock and assert the other writer (a raise, a bulk edit, a subtask create) waits on the ADVISORY lock holding no row. **Round 3 (3 lenses, 16 agents, 10 upheld, 0 refuted):** the bulk verbs and the raise read BEFORE the new wait and wrote from that stale read (a row deleted during the wait was still archived and audited) — both now re-read after the lock, pinned by dbtests; `createItem`'s lock order got its own test; and the record overclaimed. **Three OLDER lockers sit outside the queue** (listed in `rank-lock.ts`, none introduced here): the portal fan-out and `copyWeek` (whose time-entry foreign keys take KEY SHARE on several work items in date order) can deadlock WITH a queued writer; `deleteItem` versus an attachment's visibility flip deadlocks with that flip alone and never with the queue — it writes only `deleted_at`, so it never takes a second work_item row.

**SUPERSEDED BY THE NEXT RUN — READ THIS FIRST. The CI slice saves FOUR minutes per run, not zero and not the one predicted.** Run `34623441685` on `cb87e14`, the second with `.next/cache` and therefore the first with a WARM one: isolation 197 s → 4, **e2e 414 s → 7**, **total 11 billable against the 15 the three-job layout billed.** The full arc for e2e is 586 s (pre-change) → 650 s (cold cache, paying to save with nothing to restore) → **414 s (warm)**. So the cache needed exactly one run to populate, as `ci.yml`'s comment hedged, and the `turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: false` fallback is NOT needed. At ~65 runs/month that is ~260 minutes saved. **The lesson is the method, not the number: one run is not a trend, and the paragraph below — written after run one — drew the opposite conclusion from real data that was simply too early.** Left standing rather than deleted, because the reasoning in it is right and only its conclusion expired.

**RUN ONE SAID NET ZERO (2026-09-11, superseded above).** Run `34619114519` on `40ef1c6`, the first with the merged job layout, billed **15 minutes — exactly what the three-job layout billed before it.** Per job, against pre-change run `34155378723`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | 94 s → 2 | *(merged away)* |
| `isolation` | 138 s → 3 | **202 s → 4** |
| `e2e` | 586 s → 10 | **650 s → 11** |
| total | **15** | **15** |

**The merge worked exactly as designed** — 232 s billing as 5 became 202 s billing as 4 — **and e2e gave the minute straight back**, 586 → 650 s, crossing a rounding boundary. Part of that is expected on a FIRST run: `.next/cache` had nothing to restore and still paid to save. But the typecheck skip should have returned ~28 s, so 64 s of regression is not fully explained by the cache write, and something else moved too. **RE-MEASURE BEFORE CONCLUDING** — one run is not a trend, and the saving claimed in commit `74e4beb` has not appeared. If a warm-cache run does not put e2e back under 600 s, take the branch `ci.yml` already names: `turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: false` under CI, which reclaims the write cost for free. The job merge is banked either way.

**`paths-ignore` DOES NOT SKIP A COMMENT-ONLY EDIT TO A `.ts` FILE.** It skips only when EVERY changed path matches `docs/**` or `**/*.md`. Commit `cb87e14` said "docs and comments only, so paths-ignore skips the pipeline" and was wrong — it touched `src/auth/audit-hooks.ts` and cost a full run. Split comment edits into their own commit only if you are willing to pay for them, or batch them with real work.

**THE CHALLENGE-BURN GAP IS CLOSED AS WONTFIX, with a refutation worth keeping.** Five rows per grind means "the challenge was ground to death" is derivable; a sixth adds nothing the first five do not prove. And the obvious fix — park the user id in a `hooks.before` — **cannot work**: Better Auth hands a before-hook a SPREAD COPY of the context (`hook.handler({...context, returnHeaders: true})`, `api/dispatch.mjs`), so a WeakMap keyed on `ctx` keys an object that dies with that call; and if any before-hook returns a context modification, `defuReplaceArrays` replaces the whole context before the after-hooks run. There is no identity to key on — and a throwing before-hook is a 500 BEFORE the handler, on the plane with no second way in. Recorded in the code comment so it is not re-proposed. **The correct boundary number is FIVE recorded failures, not four** (an earlier estimate here said four).

**STILL UNVERIFIED, narrowed further.** The factor guard's refusals, the enrolment ramp (unreachable now that a factor exists) and the backup-code reissue on the console side have not been exercised. One known dev wrinkle: the middleware matcher exempts only `_next/static` and `_next/image`, so dev HMR endpoints get swept under `/ops` on the ops host — cosmetic, page renders, hot reload may not.

**SESSION (2026-09-11, later — THE OPS CONSOLE LEAVES A TRAIL, AND THE AUTH HOOKS STOPPED BEING ABLE TO BREAK SIGN-IN).** Two commits. The second closes the "platform instance writes NO audit rows" item that has stood since 2026-09-10; the first is the prerequisite it would otherwise have inherited and amplified.

**FIRST, A LIVE DEFECT ON THE MEMBER PLANE.** `guarded()` wrapped only the EMITTER call, never the handler body — so the after-hooks ran `internalAdapter.findUserByEmail()` and `ctx.getSignedCookie()` outside it. Better Auth's `runAfterHooks` turns whatever an after-hook throws into the RESPONSE: an APIError replaces an already-successful one, anything else becomes a 500, and the session row and cookie are already written. **The user is signed in and told they are not.** That cookie read runs on EVERY successful two-factor sign-in and verifies a signature against a shared secret, so a malformed cookie, a rotated secret or a name collision was enough; on the console, where a factor is mandatory, it is the only way in. Whole bodies are wrapped now, pinned by `src/auth/audit-hook-guard.test.ts` — a static scan, because `audit-hooks.ts` reaches `@/db` and the unit job runs before `migrate deploy`. **The scan was verified by reintroducing the defect twice**, in its awaited and its synchronous shapes, and watching it fail both times; the first version of that test would have missed the synchronous one.

**A REJECTED SECOND FACTOR WAS RECORDED NOWHERE, ON EITHER PLANE.** It is the highest-signal auth failure there is — at the code prompt the caller has already passed the password — and Better Auth throttles those endpoints, so an attacker who knows an address could grind codes until the account's factor locked, denying it its own sign-in, silently. `auth.mfa_verification_failed` covers it on any 4xx. The two stages are recorded where the facts are: sign-in failures from the after-hook via the pending challenge's verification row (which a failed code does not consume), step-up failures from `step-up.ts`, because `verifyTwoFactor` resolves the session into a LOCAL and never puts it on the request context — reading `ctx.context.session` there would have attributed nothing at all, silently. **One transition is still uncaptured and the comment now says so instead of claiming otherwise:** the 400 challenge-burn after five tries, because `beginAttempt()` consumes the verification row BEFORE throwing, so nothing is left to attribute it to. The five INVALID_CODE rows preceding it are recorded, so the grind is visible; only the row marking the challenge's death is missing. The 429 lockout IS captured.

**SECOND: SEVEN `platform.*` ACTIONS, AND WHY THEY ARE NOT `auth.*` REUSED.** A platform-plane event is not a tenant event with a null tenant: `tenant_id` is NULL because there IS no tenant, the actor id lives in the global `user` namespace rather than a tenant's `member` namespace, and the audience is the operator. Reusing `auth.*` would also route them through `recordForUserMemberships`, which loops over ACTIVE memberships — and **a platform admin who belongs to no tenant makes that loop run zero times, write nothing, throw nothing and return 0.** Nothing in `src/` grants a membership alongside `platformRole`, so the reused path would have produced a console trail that stayed silently empty for exactly the accounts that most need one. Written by `recordPlatformEvent()` (`src/db/platform-audit.ts`) under `app_platform`, because `audit_tenant_insert` carries `WITH CHECK (tenant_id = app.tenant_id)` and `app_runtime` cannot insert a NULL tenant at all. The pure row builder is split into `src/audit/platform-record.ts` so its refusals — unknown action, TENANT action, MIRRORED action — are unit-testable with no connection. Both planes now share ONE set of hooks parameterised by a sink; only `session.create` stays a per-instance literal, because it writes the plane stamp `getPlatformSession()` reads and putting the console's admission rule behind a parameter is how the operator gets locked out. `recordPlatformEvent` is seam-grade: both belts (ESLint + `import-boundary.test.ts`) now pin `auth/platform-audit-hooks.ts` as its only importer.

**`metadata.superadmin` IS THE ROW TO READ.** Both instances share one `user`/`account` table and the console gates sign-in on the PASSWORD alone — `requirePlatformAdmin()` refuses the session afterwards, but the sign-in itself succeeded. So an ordinary member whose password is accepted at the ops form is otherwise indistinguishable from the operator. `superadmin: false` on a `platform.login_succeeded` row is that signal, and nothing else in the product reports it.

**STILL OWED, in rough priority.** (a) **Nothing READS any of these rows** — there is no ops audit view on either plane, so the whole trail is forensic-via-psql until one lands. That reader has a wrinkle already visible: running under `withPlatform` writes a `platform.tenant_access` row per invocation, so browsing the audit log inflates it. (b) **The plane invariant is convention, not a constraint.** `(tenant_id IS NULL) = (visibility = 'PLATFORM')` holds by agreement only, and `src/members/provisioning.ts:76-86` already breaks it (a `tenant.provisioned` row with PLATFORM visibility AND a tenant id, written by a hand-rolled `tx.auditEvent.create` that skips `record()` entirely). A `CHECK … NOT VALID` migration would bind it for every role including `app_platform`, but it must land WITH the provisioning fix — deliberately deferred as its own slice rather than bolted on here. (c) A SUPERADMIN changing their password on the APP plane writes tenant rows and no platform row, though that password is what opens the console. (d) `mirroredToTenant` is still declared, test-asserted, promised by DATA_MODEL §3.1 and read by no runtime code; `platformAuditRow()` refuses mirrored actions outright rather than pretending. (e) `job.run` is catalogued and emitted nowhere.

**NONE OF THE PLATFORM HALF IS VERIFIED BY RUNNING IT.** The console is unreachable without a distinct `OPS_URL`, no e2e spec touches `/ops`, and `pnpm test:db` was NOT run locally — it writes to the shared Neon dev database and a cleanup hook wiped that once before, so CI's container-from-empty run is the safer equivalent. The member half is exercised by two new `auth-audit.dbtest.ts` cases; everything platform-side rests on unit tests (platform-record 7, catalog pins, the hook scan) and the pinned Better Auth sources.

**SESSION (2026-09-11 — BACKUP-CODE REISSUE, AND THE FIRST THING IN THIS RANGE ANYONE HAS ACTUALLY RUN).** Commit `87c9c42`. The founder had lost their backup codes, which surfaced that **nothing in this product could produce them again**: they are shown once at enrolment, and two screens threw them away outright — `account/totp-enrollment.tsx` replaced them with a success message on activation (almost certainly how they were lost), and the previous day's ops ramp dropped them the moment Activate succeeded. `/account` now reissues on a live TOTP **and** the password, which is strictly more than Better Auth's endpoint asks (a password alone — which would hand a password thief a permanent set of second factors).

**Two gate conditions, and the marker is the load-bearing one.** Keyed on a fresh `mfaVerifiedAt` alone — the first version — a stolen member cookie plus the password could reissue inside the window of ANY unrelated member-plane step-up, because every step-up writes that stamp: the weak plane minting the strong plane's second factors, the exact pattern the rest of the guard exists to stop. `src/auth/reissue-intent.ts` is a process-local AsyncLocalStorage marker only the reissue action opens; a request cannot set one, so the raw endpoint stays frozen for a platform principal whatever a caller sends. **Six digits only, never a backup code** — `verifyStepUpWithHeaders` routes anything else to `verifyBackupCode`, which CONSUMES the code, and it runs before the password is checked, so accepting backup codes would have meant every mistyped password permanently spending one of the codes the caller came to replace. A 429 from the per-IP limiter also no longer reports as a wrong code (it told the caller to "try the next code", so they retried and burned the per-user budget too).

**VERIFIED IN USE, and that is the point of this note.** The founder reissued and saved codes through `/account` on 2026-09-11. **This retires the "nothing here has been run" caveat for the MEMBER-plane reissue flow ONLY.** Everything else in `afebbd8` remains unexercised: the ops console is still unreachable without a distinct `OPS_URL`, no e2e spec touches `/ops`, and the platform gate, factor freeze, enrolment ramp and host-scoping rest on unit tests and the pinned Better Auth sources alone.

**Still the largest hole, unchanged: the platform instance writes NO audit rows.** `auditPlugin()` is absent and its `databaseHooks` declare only `session.create`. Note the reissue's own audit (`auth.backup_codes_reissued`) inherits the same limit — `recordForUserMemberships` fans out per ACTIVE membership, so a platform principal with no active tenant membership writes nothing. Take that next.

**SESSION (2026-09-10 — THE PLATFORM PLANE NOW ENFORCES WHAT TWO DOCUMENTS HAVE CLAIMED FOR MONTHS, AND THE CONSOLE IS REACHABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME).** Five findings from the 2026-09-09 exposure audit were about the ops plane; this slice closes four of them and records the fifth. **The headline is not the MFA gate — it is that `/ops` has been UNREACHABLE, by two independent mechanisms, and nobody noticed because each hid the other.** (1) The platform Better Auth instance declared no `user.additionalFields`, and Better Auth builds each model's output by copying only the keys in that instance's own table schema (`@better-auth/core/.../adapter/factory.mjs`, `for (const key in tableSchema)`; schema composed in `.../db/get-tables.mjs`). `platformRole` was never copied off the row, came back `undefined`, and `getPlatformSession()` denied EVERY session at its SUPERADMIN check — sign-in succeeded, `/ops` bounced to `/ops/login`, forever. (2) `OPS_URL` is unset, so `planeForHost` never answers "platform" and `proxy.ts` rewrote `/ops` to `/404` anyway. Meanwhile `/api/platform-auth/*` matched no pass-through and fell to the generic branch, whose only gate is the PRESENCE of a member cookie — a value any scripted client invents — so **the console's entire credential surface was operable from the tenant origin while the console itself was absent**. On a real ops host the same middleware redirected those paths under `/ops`, 404ing the console's own sign-in. Each configuration broke the opposite half.

**SHIPPED (no migration).** `platformGateDecision()` (`src/auth/platform-gate.ts`, pure, no imports — so the matrix is pinned by a unit test with no database, cookie or Better Auth in reach) requires plane=PLATFORM · platformRole=SUPERADMIN · `twoFactorEnabled` · a non-null `mfaVerifiedAt`, failing closed at every step and ordered so a denial never leaks a fact the caller had not already established. **The gate is a DAL function, never a layout** — Next's own shipped docs say a layout "does not control whether the rest of the route renders" and that the pattern "will not prevent nested route segments and Server Actions from being accessed"; a Server Action is a POST addressed by action id and never runs the layout of the page that rendered it. Both auth APIs are now host-scoped (`src/proxy.test.ts`, 9 cases), `admin()` is gone from BOTH instances, `disableSignUp` is on for the platform instance, both instances share ONE rate limiter with a per-plane bucket subject, and the platform instance finally revokes sessions and audits on password reset.

**THE REVIEW CYCLE WAS THE WORK: one `/security-review` (3 of 4 findings confirmed ≥8/10 by independent refuters) and FIVE `/code-review` rounds, 22 findings, every one on code written earlier in the same session.** Four rounds each broke a claim the previous round's comments asserted, which is the pattern worth keeping:
- **The MFA gate defeated itself.** The anti-lockout ramp let a password holder sign in unenrolled, call `/two-factor/enable` with that same password, and verify a TOTP they had just generated — and first-enrolment verify DOES `createSession` on `/two-factor/verify-totp`, so `isFreshFactorPath` stamped it. My own comment and SECURITY.md both said "only a NEW session gets the stamp"; **that was false.** Worse, `enable` on an account that already has a verified factor deletes the secret and backup codes and recreates the row as verified — silent factor replacement with no proof of possession. `src/auth/factor-guard.ts` now refuses `enable` (when verified), `disable`, `get-totp-uri` and `generate-backup-codes` for a SUPERADMIN. **First enrolment is still password-bootstrapped and SECURITY.md §3.5 now says so** rather than claiming a closed door.
- **Guarding one plane guarded neither.** The first draft put that guard on the platform instance only — but `TwoFactor.userId` is `@unique`, so a SUPERADMIN has ONE factor row and the member plane's `/two-factor/disable` deletes the very row the console gate depends on. **The same shared-row reasoning that removed `admin()`, not applied to itself.** It now runs on both, keyed on the USER being SUPERADMIN so ordinary members keep self-service 2FA.
- **`cookiePrefix` did not do what it claimed.** better-call signs the cookie VALUE only (`signCookieValue(value, secret)`) — the NAME is not in the HMAC payload — and both instances share one secret and one `verification` table, so a `better-auth.two_factor` value replays verbatim as `flv-ops.two_factor`. What closes it is `proxy.ts` refusing `/api/auth/*` on the ops host; the prefix is hygiene, not the control.
- **The prescribed recovery would have BRICKED the console.** "Delete the `two_factor` row" is wrong on its own: Better Auth decides whether to demand a factor from `user.twoFactorEnabled`, not the row's existence, so sign-in would keep demanding a code no endpoint could accept, with no session through which to enrol. **It is two statements**, and `UPDATE "user" SET two_factor_enabled = false` is not optional.
- **The anti-lockout ramp was unreachable, twice.** Seeding `useState` from a search param never re-runs when the gate's redirect is a client-side navigation back into the same segment; and tagging the override with its reason still stranded a repeat `?reason=enrol`. Both fixed, plus an escape hatch out of the enrol stage and the backup codes carried onto the success stage — they can never be reissued now, so dropping them was a lockout in waiting.
- Also fixed: `role: "admin"` was revoked only inside the not-yet-SUPERADMIN branch, so it never fired on the founder row it was written for; `decodeURIComponent` on a raw cookie could throw a 500 out of middleware instead of failing closed; one shared limiter let app-host traffic from a shared egress IP eat the console's budget.

**DISPOSITIONED, NOT FIXED — owed work, each with its reason.** (a) **The platform instance writes NO audit rows at all**: `auditPlugin()` is absent and its `databaseHooks` declare only `session.create`, so console sign-ins and MFA enable are unaudited. Pre-existing, not a regression from this slice, and adding the plugin needs the auth fan-out rethought first — `recordForUserMemberships` is membership-based, and a SUPERADMIN with no ACTIVE tenant membership produces zero rows. **Take this next; it is the largest remaining hole on the plane.** (b) **The MFA freshness check never expires**: `expiresIn: 8h` is an IDLE timeout, `updateAge` re-extends it on use, and the refresh preserves `mfaVerifiedAt` — so a used console session passes forever. Bounding it needs an absolute cap or a stamp-age check, and a stamp-age check needs a step-up route on the ops host first. (c) **Single-host is now MEMBER-PLANE-ONLY**: with `OPS_URL` unset the console, its gate, the factor guard and the ramp are all 404. Deliberate and fail-closed, recorded in `RUNBOOK.md` §6 — **set a distinct `OPS_URL` to work on the console at all.** (d) The **impersonation** half of the original finding is closed only by DELETION: `/admin/impersonate-user` is gone, so the dead read-only mask in `authorize.ts` and the never-supplied `impersonatorId` in `audit/record.ts` are now unreachable rather than wired. When impersonation is actually built it needs the mask on a real actor flag, dual-identity audit on both `impersonation.started` and `impersonation.ended`, and to live behind `requirePlatformAdmin()` — not a plugin re-registered on the member instance.

**NOT VERIFIED END TO END, and it cannot be from here.** No e2e spec touches `/ops`, and the console is unreachable in this repo's own configuration, so **every claim above rests on code, unit tests (`platform-gate` 14, `proxy` 9) and the pinned Better Auth sources — not on a console anyone has signed into.** The first real sign-in is also the first enrolment: expect `/ops/login?reason=enrol`, and transcribe the backup codes before pressing Activate.

**SESSION (2026-09-09 — "LET'S MAKE THIS REPO PUBLIC" WAS ASKED, MEASURED, AND ANSWERED NO; THE CI SLICE IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN IS SHIPPED).** The proposal was to publish `fortleva` for free Actions minutes. Rejected on evidence, and the evidence is the point: publication is one-way (clones, forks and caches survive un-publishing) and **it does not fix the burn**. Per-repo minutes reconstructed for the current cycle: **manecab 1,371 · fortleva 255 · webask 56 · naxdor 46 · naxdor-se 40 · f1rmav 9 = 1,777 of 2,000 in nine days.** manecab is 77% of it; publishing fortleva removes 14% and the allowance still goes. **CORRECT FORTLEVA'S OWN FIGURE: ~940 min/month, not 255** — 252 was a SEVEN-DAY window (~5 runs per active day, ~13 active days, ~15 min/run), so this repo becomes a problem on its own even after manecab. **And e2e has regressed from the 11.5 min headline to 15**: `pnpm test:e2e` went 8 m 18 s → 9 m 46 s as the suite grew 45 → 71 tests. Re-measure at every phase close instead of trusting the note — that drift is what made "255" look safe.

**METERING TRAP, because the documented method silently returns nothing.** `actions/runs/<id>/timing` returns `total_ms: 0` for every run on this account — HTTP 200, well-formed body, `jobs` count correct, all durations zeroed. Taking it literally yields "0 billable minutes". Meter from `actions/runs/<id>/jobs?filter=all` (`filter=all` catches re-run attempts) and sum `ceil((completed_at - started_at)/60)` PER JOB; exclude `runner_name: null` jobs (never landed on a runner, never billed). Cross-checks to within 2.4% of `run_duration_ms`. Also: run ids are ACCOUNT-GLOBAL, so `repos/<other-repo>/actions/runs/<id>` 404s — that 404 means wrong repo, not a fabricated run.

**THE PUBLICATION EXPOSURE AUDIT IS WORTH KEEPING EVEN THOUGH THE ANSWER WAS NO.** Five lenses, 30 findings, each handed to an independent agent told to refute it: 26 refuted, 4 upheld. **No leaked credential anywhere** — no `.env` was ever committed on any ref, the `.env*` ignore rules are in the FIRST commit (so there is no pre-ignore window), 1,614 blobs clean of keys/PATs/PEMs/JWTs/storage-state/DSNs, 723 dependencies all permissive, no `pull_request_target`, no self-hosted runner, ci.yml references no secrets. Nothing would need rotating or a history rewrite. What publication would actually cost is **business IP, not security**: `docs/` is 1.9 MB holding the pricing tiers, the cost model beside them, the 11–13 month roadmap, the launch sequencing and a feature-level teardown of ~40 named competitors.

**SHIPPED (no migration): the CI slice, three of the four proposals, one deliberately reverted.** (1) The `check` job is **merged into `isolation`** — two jobs paid checkout + install + `prisma generate` twice and GitHub rounds every job up to the whole minute separately, so 94 s + 138 s billed as 5 minutes for 232 s of work; now ~198 s = 4. Same commands, same order, positioned BEFORE `migrate deploy` so a commit that cannot typecheck still never reaches the database — that is what the deleted `needs: [check]` edge bought, preserved by ordering. Each moved step carries its own `timeout-minutes` (5/5/3), which is TIGHTER than the old per-job 10. (2) `next build` stops re-running `tsc` under CI — **28 s measured** on run 34155378723. (3) The e2e job **restores `.next/cache`**: next 16.3 enables `turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild` by default, so CI has been WRITING a Turbopack cache every run and never reading it. Estimated, not measured, and labelled as such in the file — if it does not pay for itself, take the doc's other branch and turn the cache off under CI instead. **REVERTED ON REVIEW:** running typecheck/eslint/unit concurrently in one `run:` block. **This repo is private, so `ubuntu-latest` is 2 vCPU / 7 GB, not the 4 cores public repos get** — three Node processes plus a postgres:18 container on 7 GB is a plausible OOM, which surfaces as a red run with a truncated log and no error in it; capturing per-command logs to files also loses them entirely when `timeout-minutes` CANCELS the job; and it destroys fail-fast. Serial keeps all three properties and the merge is where the saving was anyway.

**THREE FRESH-AGENT REVIEW ROUNDS, 11 FINDINGS, ALL DISPOSITIONED — and the second and third rounds were the valuable ones, again.** Round 1 (5): the concurrency revert above answered three of them at once; the `next build` bypass was keyed on the generic `CI`, which **every hosted build platform exports** (Vercel, Netlify, Coolify, Kamal), so it would have escaped into deploy builds; an orphaned comment block was re-joined to its command. Round 2 (3): `GITHUB_ACTIONS` was still too broad — true in EVERY workflow, so a `deploy.yml` added later would silently ship unchecked types; the deleted job's `timeout-minutes: 10` had gone with it. Round 3 (3): **`NEXT_SKIP_TYPECHECK` alone is FORGEABLE** — `next build` calls `loadEnvConfig` BEFORE loading `next.config.ts`, so an untracked `.env.local` (or a deploy platform's env panel) could set it and disable the type pass on exactly the builds with no compensating check, and playwright.config.ts's dotenv load would carry it into the local webServer child. **The bypass now requires BOTH `NEXT_SKIP_TYPECHECK === "1"` AND `GITHUB_ACTIONS === "true"`**, declared on exactly one job, both compared to strings so `=0` cannot read as true. **Verified empirically, four modes:** forged opt-in alone → typechecks; Actions without the opt-in → typechecks; both → skips; plain local → typechecks. **REFUTED with evidence, so it is not re-found:** that `actions/cache` saves a partial cache after a failed run — `actions/cache@v4`'s `action.yml` carries `post-if: "success()"`, read directly from the repo. Also refuted: that deleting the `check` job could orphan a required status check — branch protection is unavailable on Free for a private repo (403) and GraphQL reports zero rules; all 67 runs have been `push` or `workflow_dispatch`, never `pull_request`. **The one real regression this merge could hide:** a unit test that opens a connection would now silently get the container instead of failing closed. Checked rather than assumed — the suite was run locally with all three database URLs pointed at an unreachable host, and passed identically (44 files, 757 tests).

**STILL OPEN, and none of it is this repo's CI.** (a) **manecab is the actual burn** and has not been touched this session — 1,371 minutes in nine days, E2E being 838 min from 15 runs (avg 56 min/run), roughly half of which ended failed or cancelled. It is the next cost slice, not this one. (b) **Push batching** is the single biggest remaining lever here (−470 to −585 min/month, zero coverage loss, no YAML) and is behavioural, not a change anyone can commit. (c) A **self-hosted runner** bills zero on Free/private and is the real substitute for publishing — but `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust` at `ci.yml`'s two service blocks MUST become a password first; the workflow says so in its own comment ("safe because of `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` and nothing else"). Wants Opus and a fresh-agent `/security-review`.

**FIVE PRODUCT FINDINGS FELL OUT OF THE EXPOSURE AUDIT AND ARE NOT ABOUT PUBLISHING.** Each was refuted as a *publication* risk while the verifier explicitly confirmed the *code* fact, so they survive the decision and want their own slice. (1) **Platform-console MFA is not enforced anywhere in code**, though `SECURITY.md` §3.5 and `AUTHZ.md` both call it mandatory — `getPlatformSession()` checks cookie, plane and `platformRole`, never `twoFactorEnabled`; that plane holds `app_platform`, a BYPASSRLS cross-tenant role. (2) **Better Auth's `admin()` impersonation endpoint is mounted on the tenant app host** while the documented read-only mask in `authorize.ts` is unreachable and `impersonatorId` is supplied by no caller — impersonation would be silent and unaudited. (3) `src/auth/platform.ts` has **no rate-limit hooks** while the member instance does, making the ops console the least-protected of the three login surfaces. (4) Rate limiting **degrades to a no-op in production** if `UPSTASH_*` is unset — one `console.warn`, no boot assertion. (5) **C20: a legacy `send.` SES identity on the Naxdor domain that nobody monitors**, with no DMARC `rua` — real regardless of publication, and the only finding whose verifier crashed, so treat it as plausible-unverified.

**SESSION (2026-09-07 — TWO OF THE THREE STANDING HAZARDS, CLOSED AS TWO SLICES).** **SHIPPED, no migration:** (1) **the locale restamp** — `src/search/rebuild.ts`, called from `updatePreferences` in the SAME transaction as the tenant row, gives `search.index_rebuilt` the producer it has been catalogued without since 2W. `search_index.lang` is per row and `search` is STORED-generated from it, so a workspace that switched language kept searching yesterday's rows with today's stemmer. The restamp is ONE statement with the config resolved once in TypeScript (`search_lang()` is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, so naming it would run it twice per row); it audits only when a row actually changed. **Measured: 201 rows restamp in 424 ms**, printed by the dbtest so a future slow save is read as a finding. (2) **the comment cascade** — `src/comments/cascade.ts` (core, because `src/documents` may not import `src/modules/*`), called from `deleteItem` and from the new shared `softDeleteDocumentsInTx`. `Comment.subjectId` has NO foreign key and `search_feed_comment` indexes every comment with `title = left(body_text, 140)` plus the whole body, so a deleted task's thread stayed alive and findable; the search hydrate papered over it. Now the subject's delete takes its comments — and a document's versions' comments — under the SUBJECT's delete permission, one `comment.deleted` per comment, ids only.

**THE REVIEW FOUND 21, THEN 9 MORE, AND THE ONES WORTH KEEPING ARE ABOUT WRITING A TRUE AUDIT TRAIL.** Both cascades originally found their rows and then stamped them in a second statement — two statements that can disagree under READ COMMITTED, so the trail could name this actor for a comment another transaction had already deleted. Both now use **`updateManyAndReturn`: the rows it gives back ARE the rows it stamped**. The same reasoning reached the item itself — `deleteItem` guards its own update on `deletedAt: null` and denies NOT_FOUND when it loses the race, and `softDeleteDocument` now answers the same way instead of reporting success having written nothing. Audit rows for a cascade go out in ONE statement (`recordMany` in `src/audit/record.ts`), so a long thread costs a delete two statements rather than two hundred.

**THE BELT THE NEW OPERATION FELL OUT OF, and it is the finding to remember.** `updateManyAndReturn` is a DIFFERENT Prisma operation name from `updateMany`, and both of this repo's belts are keyed by name: the tenant-injection belt and `undefinedWhereGuard` — the guard written after the 2026-08-31 dev-database wipe, and the ONLY protection on the BYPASSRLS platform client. The first version of this slice added the new name to one belt and not the other. The guard is now one `$allOperations` hook testing a single exported list, so a hook nobody wrote can no longer look like a guard that passed, and **it was PROVEN to fire** against a client pointed at an unreachable database (all three bulk writes refused, reads untouched). The cascade also refuses a falsy subject id outright: `{subjectType, subjectId: undefined}` would have become "every comment of that type in the tenant" — the same fail-open, one level down, where no belt can see it.

Rules (1) deep-path imports, (2) module direction and (4) portal.ts model types do not exist in `eslint.config.mjs` or any test; only the `withPlatform` allowlist does.
