**SESSION (2026-09-06 — `/search` AND ⌘K ENTITY ROWS: THE PHASE ITSELF).** **SHIPPED:** `src/search/query.ts` (the first reader of `search_index`) + `src/search/shape.ts` (its DB-free half), `/search` with a debounced server-param query, and entity rows in the palette. **NO MIGRATION** — the table, its RLS and its six feed triggers all shipped with 2W core; the only DDL this phase needed was the trigger repair above.

**THE REVIEW OF THE READER FOUND A PRIVILEGE ESCALATION, and it is the finding to remember: SCOPE IS NOT A PERMISSION.** Assignments and roles are independent axes (AUTHZ.md §4), so a member seated on a custom role holding nothing but `invoice:view`, with one `MemberClient`, can open no board, no client and no document — and the unguarded query still handed them every task title, every document name, every client and contact name, and **the first 140 characters of every internal COMMENT, because a COMMENT index row's `title` IS `left(body_text, 140)`**. Every sibling read in the product calls `requireAccess`; search was the outlier. Each entity type is now gated by the permission that governs reading it, through `requireAccess` — which is also the flag, entitlement and tenant-preference check, so a tenant that switched a module OFF cannot be searched through the back door its list pages close. **The gate is an `entity_type = ANY(...)` TERM, never a post-filter**: a forbidden row must not occupy a per-type cap slot a permitted one would have taken. Two dbtests pin it in both directions.

**THE SECOND BELT §6.19 MANDATES WAS ALSO MISSING, and skipping it is what turns a dormant DDL gap into a live bug.** Hits are now hydrated by id under the caller's principal and dropped if the source is gone. It closes a gap that exists TODAY: nothing cascades a work item's soft delete to its comments, so a comment's index row outlives the task it was written on.

**THEN THE REVIEW OF THE SURFACES FOUND FOUR MORE, ALL MINE, ALL REAL.** (1) **Every COMMENT hit was silently dropped** — the hydrate built its work-item lookup from the work-item HITS only, so a comment whose parent task did not also match the same query resolved to no address and was thrown away. Comments were unsearchable while the page, the palette and both catalogues promised them; there was no COMMENT case in the dbtests at all. (2) **Enter could switch the member's language.** cmdk moves its highlight to the first item on every SEARCH change, but entity rows arrive 200 ms later — and with `shouldFilter={false}` the Actions group was filtered by nothing, so a query matching no nav row left the highlight on "Switch language" and Enter changed the locale and revalidated the layout. Every group now does its own matching. (3) From the same cause: **`CommandEmpty` was unreachable dead code** (with the filter off cmdk sets its filtered count to the number of MOUNTED items, so it never reaches zero) and an **empty "Navigate" heading rendered over nothing**. (4) **A stale palette result could still land**: nothing bumped the ticket on close, and the `openRef` effect runs AFTER the reset commits, so a result resolving in that window repopulated a palette that had just been cleared.

**Also fixed from that pass:** an archived task's address opened a backlog that HIDES archived rows (archived rows stay in the index by design; the address now asks with `archived=1`); the search box did not follow a same-route navigation it had not caused (the rail's own Search link left the old query in the box over an idle page); palette titles overflowed instead of ellipsing (a nowrap flex child needs `min-w-0 flex-1`, which the `/search` row already had); and **the idle state rendered `SearchXIcon` — a magnifier with an X through it, i.e. "nothing found" — BEFORE anything had been searched**, because `EmptyState`'s `filtered` default is that glyph.

**AND A THIRD REVIEW, ON THE FIXES, FOUND THAT ONE OF THEM ONLY NARROWED ITS BUG.** Filtering the Actions group changed WHICH row the highlight was stuck on, not that one was: **cmdk moves its highlight on a SEARCH change only** — item registration re-selects nothing while something is already selected — so entity rows mounting 200 ms later never take it. On a Swedish tenant, typing `logg` matches no nav row and exactly one action, `Logga ut`; Enter signed the member out. Reachable pairs also include sv `spr` → `Byt språk` (the very bug the previous fix claimed to close), `kort` → `Kortkommandon`, en `ska`/`lang` → `Switch language`. **The fix is a CONTROLLED selection**: `value`/`onValueChange` on the root, with the highlight moved to `hits[0]` the moment results exist — the one thing cmdk will not do. Rows are also now stored WITH the query they answer and rendered only while fresh, so Enter during the debounce can no longer fire a result for the previous query. An e2e pins it. **Two more from the same pass:** the close path bumped the request ticket but never CLEARED THE ARMED TIMER, whose callback mints a fresh ticket and checks only `openRef` — true again after a reopen — so a close-then-reopen inside 200 ms still landed the old query's rows under an empty box; and `search-input` had the same shape, where an armed debounce silently undid a clear the member had just performed through the rail's own Search link.

**ONE REVIEW SUGGESTION WAS ITSELF WRONG, AND A DBTEST CAUGHT IT.** It proposed replacing the lexeme probe's `SELECT DISTINCT lang` scan with a direct `GREATEST(sv, en)`, on the grounds that the config set is closed so the answers are identical. **They are not**: "och" is a Swedish stop word and an ordinary English word, so the max across both reports it meaningful, and a Swedish tenant searching "och" would be told "nothing matched" instead of "that needs a word to go on" — which is the entire distinction the probe exists to draw. The scan is the price of the answer being right, and the reasoning is now written above it so it is not "optimised" again.

**TWO PROCESS FAILURES OF MINE, both worth keeping.** My scope e2e asserted only that the employee finds NOTHING for a term — which reads identically whether the scope filter works or the term simply matches nobody; there is now an owner-side positive control. And **I ran `pnpm build` while the full e2e suite was live**, the exact standing trap this file records: the run was killed, `.next` removed, the orphaned server on 3000 killed, and the suite restarted clean rather than trusted.

**THE PALETTE'S CONTRACT, now that it has server-ranked rows:** `shouldFilter={false}`, because cmdk both filters AND re-sorts by fuzzy score and a `ts_rank_cd` order it re-sorts is not a ranking; every group therefore matches for itself, nav via an accent-insensitive SUBSEQUENCE test so "prj" still reaches Projects; every entity row's `value` is `type:id`, because cmdk tracks selection as one string and marks EVERY item equal to it, so a shared value lights two rows and Enter fires whichever is first in the DOM.

**SESSION (2026-09-06 — SEARCH RECON, AND TWO SHIPPED DEFECTS IT FOUND INSTEAD).** Reconnaissance for `/search` + ⌘K entity rows, run as a 58-agent workflow (5 mapping lenses, 6 hazard lenses, every hazard adversarially refuted): **47 hazards proposed, 25 survived, 22 refuted.** **THE PHASE IS NOT WHAT PLAN §0 SAID IT WAS.** `search_index` is ALREADY BUILT — table, the `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (…setweight…) STORED` tsvector, both constraints, the three btrees, `tenant_isolation` + a RESTRICTIVE three-term `portal_gate`, `fortleva_sv`/`fortleva_en` with unaccent-in-config (the "1b spike will decide" question §6.19 still poses was answered in code and never written back), six feed triggers and a backfill — all in the 2W core migration, lines 1100–1369. Nothing reads it: no Prisma model (schema.prisma carries the counter-decision), no `src/search/`, no route. So the slice is application-layer, and the only migration it needs is a TRIGGER REPAIR.

**DEFECT 1 — THE ⌘K PALETTE HAS BEEN CRASHING ON OPEN, IN SHIPPED CODE. Fixed.** `CommandDialog` leaves cmdk's `<Command>` root to its caller — deliberately, because the root owns `shouldFilter`, which both filters AND re-sorts by fuzzy score, so the surface has to choose. Of its two callers `MovePicker` rendered one and `command-palette.tsx` did not, so `CommandInput`/`List`/`Item` mounted with no store and the palette threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'subscribe')` from `useSyncExternalStore` the instant it opened; the dialog never appeared. **Reproduced, then fixed, then re-proved.** It shipped because `MovePicker` is the only `CommandDialog` any test had ever opened. **This is load-bearing beyond itself: UI.md rule 7 says every single key owes a ⌘K entry, and BOTH the selection bar and the inbox deferred their hotkeys to a palette that did not work.** Also fixed alongside it: the `sr-only` `DialogHeader` sat OUTSIDE `DialogContent`, so an `<h2>Command palette</h2>` and its `<p>` were in the DOM of every authed page whether the palette was open or not — which is also why the string looked covered. `e2e/palette.spec.ts` now presses the real hotkey (not the button — the binding ignores Alt, fires inside inputs and TOGGLES), asserts an option renders, and asserts `pageerror` is empty so a future failure says "crashed" rather than "never opened". A `palette` visual stop drives it open, so all four walks now assert `trace.pageErrors` on it — the stop that would have caught this. **45 → 46 stops, 180 → 184 shots.**

**DEFECT 2 — A LATENT VISIBILITY LEAK IN THE SEARCH FEED. FIXED by migration `20260906150000_search_feed_soft_delete`.** `search_feed_document` branches on `TG_OP = 'DELETE'` **only**, while `search_feed_work_item` and `search_feed_comment` both branch on `TG_OP = 'DELETE' OR NEW.deleted_at IS NOT NULL` (migration.sql:1216, :1242 vs :1263). Documents are ONLY EVER soft-deleted — `softDeleteDocument` is the sole path — so a delete arrives as an UPDATE, the trigger takes the upsert path, and the index row SURVIVES with a refreshed `updated_at`: a deleted CLIENT_VISIBLE document stays inside `portal_gate` and becomes the NEWEST hit. Unreachable today because nothing queries the table, wrong in the database now, and live the moment `/search` ships. **Proven before it was fixed** — a dbtest soft-deletes a CLIENT_VISIBLE attachment and counts the index row: 1, not 0, against the real database. **THE SECURITY REVIEW OF THE FIX FOUND SOMETHING WORSE THAN THE BUG: the sweep would have deleted NOTHING, silently.** `search_index` is FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, which subjects the OWNER to its policies, and both policies are `TO app_runtime` — so a migration role that is not app_runtime matches no permissive policy, every row is filtered, and the DELETE reports success having removed nothing. **TENANCY.md §11 records `app_migrate` as exactly that: "owner; subject to FORCE RLS on DML"**, and ci.yml:149 says the container's superuser "bypasses RLS here and does not there". CI could never have caught it — the container owner IS a superuser and the database is empty. The migration now carries `SET LOCAL row_security = off`, which is a no-op for a BYPASSRLS role and raises `query would be affected by row-level security policy` for any other: a silent no-op becomes a failed migration. **The same line closes the second sweep's real cliff** — it deletes on the ABSENCE of a `document` row, so under a filtered read of `document` its `NOT EXISTS` would be true for EVERY row and it would wipe every DOCUMENT row in every tenant. **The review also caught the dbtest running the wrong statement:** `indexOf("DELETE FROM search_index")` finds the TRIGGER BODY's delete first — a `NEW`/`OLD` reference that raises outside a trigger — and splitting on `;` then dropped both real sweeps, because after trimming they begin with their comment blocks. It now anchors on the `si` alias, which appears only in the DML, and asserts neither statement carries a trigger-only reference. **And the ghost row it inserts had no cleanup path** — no source row means no feed trigger can remove it, and `search_index` has no FK to tenant either, so the tenant teardown would have left it unattributable: the same class as the orphaned dbtest tenants swept in `a73cd12`. `afterAll` now deletes by tenant first, as `seed-cli.ts` already does. **Local: 29 of 30 pass; the one failure is the trigger test, which needs the migration applied to the dev database — CI migrates from empty and proves both.** **The dev database still needs a `neon-smoke.yml` dispatch, which is a founder call.**

**A SIBLING OF THE SAME DEFECT, ONE LEVEL UP, NOT FIXED — for whoever writes the reader.** The cascade is asymmetric: `deleteItem` soft-deletes the item's anchored documents, and `softDeleteDocument` soft-deletes only the document. **Neither touches `comment`, and no trigger does either.** So after a work item or a document is deleted, every CLIENT_VISIBLE comment on it keeps its `search_index` row — with `title = left(body_text, 140)` and the FULL body in `body_text` — satisfying `portal_gate` completely. Same shape as the bug above, same "unreachable until `/search` ships" caveat. The fix belongs in the reader (a parent-liveness check in the hydrate) or in a cascade at delete time, not in this migration. **Verified by the review that every OTHER feed is clean:** `project` has no `deleted_at` (only `archived_at`, which nothing writes) and its row is gated by `portal_enabled` anyway; `client.archived_at` is written but `search_feed_client` hardcodes `'INTERNAL', false` so the row can never pass the gate; `contact` has no soft-delete column at all.

**A CORRECTION I OWE THE RECORD: my first explanation of the visibility-toast flake was wrong.** I claimed a `MutationObserver` had reported zero toasts because sonner "reveals a pooled node rather than inserting one". Sonner 2.0.8 does no such thing — a fresh `<li data-sonner-toast>` per toast, no pool, no portal — so the observer should have caught it, and in 2 of 3 runs it did. The failing run genuinely recorded NO toast. The dismissal-race theory is weak too: Playwright's retry backoff settles at 500 ms, so a 30 s budget samples ~60 times and every one would have to miss a window that opened once. **ROOT CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED and this loose end must not be closed as understood.** What shipped instead is a test that can settle it: a 25 ms in-page sweep into an append-only array (monotonic — dismissal cannot lose it), asserting the ACTUAL failure string (`Could not change visibility`) rather than mere non-emptiness, asserting `data-type="error"`, and LOGGING the latency so a green run that reports 9 s is read as a finding rather than a pass. The safety assertions (cell and stored row still CLIENT_VISIBLE) now run BEFORE the toast poll, so a toast timeout can no longer hide the answer to the leak-shaped question. Local: 30/30 with the old assertion's successor, and the action→toast latency reads **74 ms**. **Three reviews of that one test were each right about the one before:** the first prescribed asserting the stored row, the second caught an eagerly-evaluated `expect.poll` message (it reported the sweep count from BEFORE the wait, which would have sent the next engineer chasing a starved recorder) plus the false sonner claim, and the third caught that my `started` timestamp was taken before two Playwright round trips and so over-reported the latency it was there to measure.

**THE REVIEW ALSO CAUGHT MY FIX BEING WRONG.** My first palette fix put the cmdk root inside `CommandDialog` — which double-nests it for `MovePicker`, whose own root then becomes a dead store with a dangling `<label for>` and a duplicated surface box, silently, with every test still green. The root stays the caller's.

**HAZARDS RECORDED FOR THE SEARCH SLICE ITSELF (the survivors worth carrying):** `$queryRaw` CANNOT deserialize this table — `tsvector` (OID 3614) and `regconfig` (3734) have no case in `fieldToColumnType` and throw `UnsupportedNativeDataType`, so `SELECT *` is a runtime error and every read must name its columns and cast. `scopeWhere` is unusable against `search_index` (it returns a Prisma `where` keyed on camelCase model fields; the table is deliberately not a model), so member scope must be applied by hand on the search path — and **AUTHZ.md:277 and :474 promise a lint rule enforcing exactly that WHICH DOES NOT EXIST**. `search_index` is invisible to the registry-driven posture and portal-gate sweeps (it is not a Prisma model, so it is in no `RLS_CLASSES` list), and cannot simply be added — the "no stale registry entries" test requires a matching `model` block. The lexeme probe, the only in-repo query precedent, hardcodes `fortleva_sv` and would break every `en` tenant if copied. ~~A tenant locale change leaves every row's `lang` stale with no rebuild path (`search.index_rebuilt` is catalogued with no producer).~~ **CLOSED 2026-09-07** — the change now restamps every row in the same transaction and audits it (`src/search/rebuild.ts`); a row fed concurrently can still straggle, which is why the reader still matches per row. `WorkItem.descriptionText` and the C-weight body tier are EMPTY — nothing in the app ever writes it. And a project key rename never re-feeds its tasks, so every WORK_ITEM subtitle keeps the dead key.

**SESSION (2026-09-06 — `/inbox`, NOTIFICATION PREFERENCES AND THE WEEKLY SELF-REMINDER).** The surface PLAN §0 has pointed at since 2026-09-02, and the 2T D6 reminder that has been blocked on it since 2026-08-21, both landed together. **SHIPPED, as two slices.** (1) **`/inbox`** — `src/notify/inbox.ts` (list · countUnread · read/unread · archive/restore · snooze/unsnooze · markAllRead), the page with four bucket tabs on `?filter=`, the row menu, the rail's unread badge, `G I`, `src/lib/snooze.ts` (9 unit tests), 20 dbtests, 7 e2e tests and an `inbox` visual stop. (2) **`/settings/notifications` + the reminder** — `src/notify/preferences.ts`, the email-level LADDER now honoured per kind by `emit`, `src/notify/weekly-reminder.ts` (pure: opt-in selection + `dueAt`, 15 unit tests), `src/jobs/weekly-reminders.ts`, 14 dbtests, 2 e2e tests and a second visual stop. **NO MIGRATION** — every table this needed already existed and was already registered; the opt-in lives in `NotificationPreference.perKind`, which the model calls its own extension point. **FOUR THINGS THE BUILD SETTLED, all written into DATA_MODEL §6.18:** a template key is NOT a notification kind (the outbox worker marked anything that was not a fan-out kind DEAD, which would have killed the reminder on its first send); `emailLevel` is a ladder with `atLevel` per kind and `NONE` deliberately not expressible as an `atLevel`; `perKind` writes MERGE so an older deploy cannot drop a newer one's setting; and `Notification.id` must be UUIDv7. **THE RECIPE'S MISSING GATES ARE DOCUMENTED, NOT FORGOTTEN:** the inbox runs no `requireAccess` (notifications are core, never entitlement-gated — §6.18), no `assertInScope` on the row (the RESTRICTIVE `principal_scope`/`principal_scope_update` policies bind SELECT *and* UPDATE to the receiver, which is the same check one layer lower), and writes NO audit event (the catalog holds only `notification.preference_changed`; inbox state is per-receiver bookkeeping nobody else can see — the `moveItem` rank-only carve-out with an even weaker claim to a row). **REVIEW: a fresh-agent `/code-review` found 5, all real, all fixed.** The one worth keeping: **paging on `created_at` silently LOSES ROWS.** The column is `timestamptz(6)` defaulted to `now()` — TRANSACTION start, to the microsecond — and Prisma returns a millisecond JS `Date`, so a cursor built from one asks for `created_at < '…123000'` and skips every row actually stamped `.123456`, while the documented `created_at = cursor` tie-break can never match a real value and was dead code. Rows emitted in ONE transaction share that stamp exactly (`checkBudgetAlerts` crossing two thresholds does it), so a whole batch straddling the page boundary vanished — from the surface whose entire job is to lose nothing. Fixed by ordering and paging on the **UUIDv7 id** (`emit` now uses `newId()` like every other service, not `randomUUID()`), which round-trips exactly; a dbtest creates 56 rows sharing one `createdAt` and asserts the two pages hold all of them, once each. The other four: the fixture's `reset-notifications` did an unbounded `updateMany` on **any** tenant id handed to it with no `e2e-` guard (now `assertThrowawayTenant`); the settings `afterEach` awaited the *email* form's "Saved" tick for the *checkbox* form's save, so the restore could be cancelled at teardown and leave the fixture opted in to weekly mail (now each save is confirmed by reloading and reading the stored value); two new doc blocks had been inserted between `sweep`'s JSDoc and its declaration, so a comment asserting a guard sat above functions that did not have it; and `countUnread` opened a second serial transaction on **every authed page render** (now folded into the one the layout already opens for nav permissions). **SECURITY REVIEW: no findings at the confidence bar, with the evidence recorded** — the two RLS belts on the inbox, the column-level `GRANT UPDATE (read_at, archived_at, snoozed_till)` matching exactly what the verbs write, `scopeWhere` composed INTO both subject loads (not checked after), the recipient of every reminder being the member's own address, and the ladder being strictly narrowing so no opt-out regressed. **It raised ONE disposition note and I took it as a fix rather than a disposition:** the inbox rendered a work item's TITLE and a project's NAME with no permission code behind it — a member can be assigned a task by anyone holding `work_item:edit` without holding any work permission themselves. The list stays ungated (your own inbox needs no permission); the SUBJECT is now gated on `work_item:view` / `project:view`, so an unpermitted, out-of-scope, deleted and unknown entity all render identically — the kind, no title, no link. A dbtest strips the employee's role and asserts exactly that. **TWO TRAPS THIS SLICE PAID FOR:** (1) **a `"use server"` module may only export `async function` DECLARATIONS** — exported const arrows passed typecheck AND eslint and failed only at `pnpm build` with "export was not found in module"; the build is the only gate that catches it. (2) **A Radix `Switch` inside `<AutoForm>` looks right and never saves** — the form commits on a real change event, which is why `TimePreferencesForm` already used `NativeCheckbox`; the checkbox also needs its hidden `…Present` marker, or an unchecked box (which posts nothing) reads as "unchanged" instead of "off". **GATES:** typecheck ✓ · eslint 0 ✓ · unit **751 passed / 1 skipped** ✓ · **the WHOLE db suite 29 files / 322 tests passed** against Neon (27/288 before this slice; 945 s, so AGENTS.md's `test:db` figure is corrected 14 → ~16 min) ✓ · full e2e ✓ · build ✓ (the browser numbers are in the follow-up note below, which is where the suite was last run end to end). **FOLLOW-UP COMMIT, reviewed on its own (fix commits are phase slices too): `src/notify/kind-copy.ts` + `kind-copy.test.ts`,** which move the kind → message-key map out of the client component so a unit test can pin it against the real catalogues. **Its review found the thing worth carrying forward: `` t(`ns.${x}` as "ns.literal") `` DEFEATS next-intl's typing, and the cast was never needed.** Messages are typed against `en.json` (`src/i18n/global.d.ts`), so interpolating a CLOSED UNION into `t()` already type-checks; the `as` cast only stops the compiler from tying those values to the catalogue, and a typo then compiles clean and reaches the page as a raw key. Proven both ways: with the cast, `budgetThreshhold` typechecks green; without it, `TS2345 … Did you mean '"kind.budgetThreshold"'?`. **Six such casts existed across this slice** (the four inbox ones, the tab labels, the email levels) and ALL SIX are gone with typecheck still clean — every one had been suppressing a real check for nothing. **The three casts that remain in the product are NOT the same thing and must not be "fixed":** `languageName.${x.locale}` (×2) and `notice.purpose.${p}` interpolate an OPEN string that came out of the database, where the compiler genuinely cannot know the value and a cast plus (for the purposes) a `t.has()` runtime guard is the only shape available. The rule is: a closed union needs no cast and must not have one; an open string needs a cast and a runtime guard. **SESSION (2026-09-02 — 2W-F slice 2 of 4: THE BACKLOG REORDERS).** Committed locally. **Shipped:** rank-only drag on the list (desktop, `pointer: fine`, same-group only) and its keyboard/touch twin — **Move up / Move down / Move to top / Move to bottom in the row menu**, which is what UI.md §5.12 asks for ("reorder verbs go INTO the menu, not behind hover: a hover-only control is unreachable by touch and invisible to a keyboard user"); `rowAnchors` + `allRowAnchors` in the shared model; `moveItemAction` gains a validated `surface`. **THE ANCHOR RULE, which is the whole correctness story:** the visible list is a SUBSEQUENCE of the project order, so every anchor is the row the member can SEE, never the neighbour in `data.items`. Anchoring on a hidden row would change the rank while the screen stayed identical — the member would click again, and the project order would drift silently. "Directly after B" resolves the same way on the server (`moveItem` locks B's true neighbour and mints a key between them) whatever the filter hides, so the optimistic reflow and the database agree. Anchors are also scoped to the item's own GROUP, and at a group's edge the verb is simply ABSENT rather than quietly anchoring on the next group's row: a rank-only move carries no property field, so leaving a group is not something it can express. **`edgeAnchors` could not be reused** — it is STATE-scoped (it runs through `cardsIn`, whose first filter is `stateId`), so its "top" means the top of a board column, not of a list group. **THE INDICATOR, decided against a real Chromium probe rather than by reasoning:** `position: relative` on a `<tr>` does establish the containing block, and that block is the row's PADDING box — measured `x=3 w=637` inside a row border box of `x=1 w=639` — so an `inset-x-0` line **geometrically cannot** paint over `visibilityRowCue`'s 2px client-visible mark. That matters more than it looks: `--primary` and `--vis-client-cue` measure **1.0002:1** against each other, so an overlap would erase a safety-critical marking with a colour of identical luminance — invisible in a screenshot and invisible to a human. The span must live inside a `<td>` (a bare `<span>` under a `<tr>` is foster-parented out of the table by the parser), and **no `transform` / `filter` / `backdrop-filter` / `will-change` / `contain: paint` may be added to the row or that cell** — any of them re-parents the containing block and the line silently moves; the dragged row is `opacity-40` for exactly that reason. Both halves of a seam normalise to ONE convention ("the row it lands above"), because a bottom-aligned line paints over the shared collapsed rule and a top-aligned one does not, so the same insertion point would otherwise render ~3px apart depending on which row the hitbox reported. **`getIsSticky` is deliberately NOT set** (the board sets it): a table body has no gaps between rows, so there is no dead space for stickiness to rescue — and without it a release over a refused row leaves `dropTargets` empty and the drop is a true no-op, where stickiness would silently reorder against the last-accepted row instead. **THE GUARD UI.md HAD BEEN CLAIMING FOR MONTHS DID NOT EXIST.** §10.4 said "`e2e/visibility.spec.ts` asserts the computed `border-left-width` on `:last-child`" — the file contained **no `border` assertion at all**, in 222 lines. So the standing trap ("`[&_tr:last-child]:border-0` deletes row-level left cues") had no automated tripwire, and nothing else can catch it: the craft audit's `rowPitch` measures row HEIGHT, which a missing left border does not change, so all 42 stops (168 shots) are blind to it. **Now added** (every row's reserved 2px, the last included, plus a client-visible row's `border-left-color` differing from an internal one's and not being alpha-0), and §10.4 rewritten to describe what is actually there. **REVIEW — TWO fresh-agent passes, and the "fix commits are slices too" rule earned its keep again.** Round 1: 3 findings, all real — (a) under a grouping the indicator resolved a bottom edge through the FLATTENED row list, so at a group's last row the line painted below the NEXT group's header while the drop correctly stayed in its own group: the indicator and the outcome disagreed; (b) `rowAnchors` per rendered row is O(n²) and `setDropAt` allocated a fresh object on every pointer move, so the whole table re-rendered and redid that work dozens of times per drag; (c) an e2e `toHaveCount(0)` fired against a Radix portal that had not opened yet, so the "a verb that cannot act is left out" guard could pass without the menu ever rendering — the same vacuous-assertion shape a CI review caught on this suite once before. Round 2, on the fixes: **3 more**, one a real correctness bug in the fix itself — (d) the new `allRowAnchors` appended an un-persisted row to the END of its group instead of keeping its rendered position, which INVERTS that row's own anchors, **and the equivalence test I wrote only placed the temp row last, the one position where a wrong implementation still agrees**; (e) `rowsRef` became dead when `onEdge` moved to reading `anchorsRef`, with its comment describing an effect fifty lines away; (f) a backlog move refusal still spoke the board's sentence ("the board shows the current state"). All six fixed. The equivalence test now places the temp row in the MIDDLE and was **proven to discriminate** — re-introducing the bug turns it red, removing it green — because a test that passes on both sides of a fix is worth nothing. **GATES: typecheck ✓ · eslint 0 ✓ · unit 697 passed / 1 skipped ✓ · build ✓.** **VERIFIED 2026-09-02: pushed as `4c71d2f`, CI run [33612094489](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/33612094489) ALL GREEN** — e2e **47 passed / 1 skipped / 1 flaky in 7.5 min**. The arithmetic is the evidence that both new browser tests actually ran: slice 1 ended at 46 passed, this slice adds two, and 47 passed + 1 flaky = 48. So the reorder test (menu moves, then a drag, each surviving a reload) and the client-visible cue guard both executed and passed on their first run anywhere. They could not be run locally — the e2e suite cannot provision here until migration `20260901180000` reaches the dev database. **THE FLAKE IS NOT NEW AND IS NOT THIS SLICE'S:** it is `visibility.spec.ts:170` "a failed change says so instead of looking like a silent revert", which PLAN already recorded flaking on 2026-08-21 ("a toast not visible within 30 s on the first try"). **That is now its SECOND recorded occurrence, and it should stop being tolerated:** the test waits on a sonner toast, and a toast is the one assertion in this suite whose timing depends on render scheduling rather than on a server answer. Fix it by asserting the stored row (as the other visibility tests do) and treating the toast as secondary, rather than by widening another timeout. **NEXT — slice 3:** hand-rolled virtualisation, inert at or below 200 rows, and mind that `DataTable` emits `[&_td]:py-0.5`, which is a FLOOR rather than an addend — measured in Chromium, `box-sizing: border-box` absorbs the 4px inside a `height` PROPERTY (180.000px either way), but a content-sized spacer really is 4px taller, and at a 2px ask the padded spacer is 4px against 2px. **THE THREE PARKED DECISIONS ARE SETTLED (2026-09-01, founder ruled on all three after a 13-agent adversarially-verified investigation; this paragraph SUPERSEDES the recommendation in the CI COST AUDIT paragraph below).** **(1) CI cost — take (A), the Postgres service container, NOT (B) the ephemeral Neon branch.** The parked recommendation was refuted on the founder's own metric: **GitHub bills the SUM of job-minutes** — the 115 is literally 1+52+62 and `ci.yml`'s own comment says queued time is not billed — so retiring the `isolation-db` group turns a 115-minute *serial* pipeline into a 115-minute *parallel* one (~63 min wall clock, identical bill). **PLAN's own "(B) → ~50–60 min" estimate below is WRONG and is corrected here.** (B) also cannot touch the larger half of the bill: `playwright.config.ts:31-33` pins `workers: 1` because "the specs share one seeded tenant and mutate the same documents" — a *fixture-architecture* constraint, not a database one — so a private branch unlocks nothing in the 62-min e2e job (54% of the spend). The fidelity objection to (A) is much narrower than the audit stated: there is **no Neon driver** (`src/db/client.ts` is plain `PrismaPg` over a connection string; all nine "neon" hits across 16 migrations are comments), and the roles are created in SQL — `CREATE ROLE app_runtime LOGIN` + `ALTER ROLE app_runtime NOBYPASSRLS` (`security_foundations/migration.sql:13-27`). **TENANCY.md §11's "Never localhost-only" gives its own reason — "a local role is typically owner/superuser, so RLS false-passes" — and a container that runs these migrations and CONNECTS AS `app_runtime` has exactly the right role posture; the pin is AMENDED for that case (founder-approved 2026-09-01), and the slice carries the amendment.** What is genuinely lost is the pooler's *negative* rule (TENANCY.md:121 "no session state, ever"), which today's code violates nowhere — bought back with a small real-Neon smoke job on `workflow_dispatch` (never cron). Est. **115 → 30–50 billable min/run**, $0, no provisioning, and it removes the `DIRECT_URL` (owner) and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` (BYPASSRLS) secrets from every AUTOMATIC run — they gave a US-hosted CI system owner-grade and BYPASSRLS access to naxdor's database on every push. **Corrected 2026-09-01 after review: the secrets are not deleted.** The manual `neon-smoke.yml` still uses all three, so they remain in the repository's secret store; what changes is that nothing triggered by a push or a PR reads them. **SPEC PINS for the slice:** image is **`postgres:18`, not 17** (`uuidv7()` at `phase2w_work_core/migration.sql:1101` is the one hard version dependency and fails loudly on 17); assert `current_user = 'app_runtime'` in the suite (nothing asserts the CONNECTED role today — `isolation.dbtest.ts:265-268` only proves such a role exists, which a container superuser connection would also pass); do NOT reuse `scripts/set-role-passwords.mjs` (it prints URLs to stdout ⇒ credentials in the job log) — **this pin said to inline two `ALTER ROLE … PASSWORD` statements with a throwaway value, and the slice REVERSED it (recorded 2026-09-01):** the container instead runs `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD: trust`, so there is no password in the pipeline at all and no step that could log one. That is safe ONLY because `runs-on` is an ephemeral GitHub-hosted VM; `ci.yml` carries the condition beside the setting, and an EU self-hosted runner would have to take the original pin; revisit `DB_TX_TIMEOUT_MS` together with `counters.dbtest.ts:42`'s own `timeoutMs: 20_000` and `ordering.dbtest.ts:343`'s 240 s literal, or the change is only half true. **Free wins — WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED, corrected 2026-09-01 after the review (this paragraph was written before implementation and named three that did not):** only ONE of the three landed — skip the 164 full-page PNG writes when `CI` is set (`visual.spec.ts:257` — they are gitignored, there are **no committed baselines and no `toHaveScreenshot` anywhere**, and CI uploads only the report; the ~20 `expect.soft` DOM/craft/console assertions per stop ARE the signal and are untouched); **NOT TAKEN — `trace: "retain-on-first-failure"`:** read against Playwright 1.62.1's own typings, `retain-on-failure` and `retain-on-first-failure` BOTH record a trace for the first run of every test and both discard it on success, so on a green run they cost exactly the same. The only difference is tracing during retries. It was never a saving; `playwright.config.ts` keeps `retain-on-failure`. **NOT TAKEN — gating `playwright install --with-deps` on a cache hit:** the ~700 MB browser download is already skipped on a hit, so the gate would save only the apt pass (~30 s) while risking a browser that cannot launch, since the OS packages are not in that cache. Reversed deliberately; the reasoning is in `ci.yml` beside the step, and the now-unused `id: playwright-cache` was dropped with it. **DO NOT "optimise" these four:** decoupling `needs: [check, isolation]` (`ci.yml:140`) is a cost INCREASE — today a red isolation run SKIPS the 62-min e2e job, so a failed push costs 53, not 115; `retries: 1` costs zero on green; the `if: always()` teardown is the only cleanup that survives a cancelled job; the "duplicate" seed in the e2e job is the belt against the 2026-08-31 wipe. **(2) The US CI-only database — RULED "permitted but NOT taken."** The residency promise is scoped to customer data **at rest** (`SECURITY.md:397`; `:402` already concedes "all processing occurs in the EU" is FALSE; `ARCHITECTURE.md:395` already blesses a fixtures-only non-production environment), so a throwaway fixtures database does not engage it — but it is strictly **dominated** by (A), which buys the same latency fix with no vendor account, no new secrets, no sub-processor amendment and no bet on runner geography. **CI COST AUDIT + THE REPO IS PRIVATE AGAIN (2026-09-01, founder's word once the quota reset).** Measured before flipping: a full green run costs **115 BILLABLE minutes** (check 1 · isolation 52 · e2e 62) and the recent pace is ~2.2 runs/day ⇒ **~3,900 min/month against an account-wide allowance of 2,000 (Free) / 3,000 (Pro)** — the pipeline overruns the whole account's budget by itself, which is why the quota went. **97% of the bill is the two test commands** (`test:db` 51.1 m, `test:e2e` 60.3 m; inside e2e: visual 25.9 m, time 12.5 m, 46 tests on ONE worker); checkout+install+generate+migrate+seed+Chromium+artifacts total **~4 min across all three jobs**. Nine of the ten standard waste defects were already absent (cache precedes its step, all jobs bounded, all runners Linux 1×, concurrency cancels superseded runs, retention 7 d, no cron, no ungrouped Dependabot). **Fixed in `368564a`:** `paths-ignore` for `docs/**` + `**/*.md` on push and PR (+ `workflow_dispatch` as the manual hatch); **`needs: [check]` on isolation** (a commit that cannot typecheck now costs 1 min, not 52 — zero billable minutes, ~1 min wall clock, since queued time is not billed); the Playwright cache keyed on the **browser's own version** instead of the lockfile hash (an unrelated bump no longer discards ~700 MB of Chromium); and the check job now lints **`src e2e`** as AGENTS.md pins — CI had been linting `src` only, so a lint error in the Playwright specs could reach main unchallenged (a coverage GAP closed, ~2 s). Verified on a real runner via `workflow_dispatch` (run 33488084424): check green in 1 m 4 s WITH the widened lint, and isolation started only after it — the new gate working; the run was then cancelled deliberately, because isolation+e2e would have spent 113 min re-verifying product code identical to the already-green `b6a1c93`. **STANDING TRAP, discovered doing this and more dangerous than it looks: a push containing ANY `[skip ci]` commit is skipped ENTIRELY — even when a later commit in the same push changes source.** The push of `368564a` (ci.yml) rode along with three `[skip ci]` PLAN commits and produced NO run at all. **So: stop using `[skip ci]`.** `paths-ignore` now does the docs case automatically and, unlike the commit-message directive, it cannot swallow a source commit hiding in the same push. **THE REAL COST IS UNTOUCHED and is the founder's to rule on:** both harnesses are fully serialised (`workers: 1`, `fileParallelism: false`) against ONE shared database ~100 ms away — the same db suite runs 3–4 min locally and 51 here, so this is latency + forced serialisation, not test count (PLAN's own 23-vs-42-min measurement on identical files says the same). Three structural fixes, none implemented: **(A) a Postgres service container on the runner** — kills latency AND unlocks parallelism, est. 115 → **~25–35 min**, needs no provisioning, but the suites stop exercising real Neon (the pooler, the `maxWait`-exhaustion class of bug) — the biggest lever available for free; **(B) the ephemeral Neon branch per run** (the standing `NEON_API_KEY` item) — keeps Neon fidelity and unlocks parallelism but not latency, est. → **~50–60 min**; **(C) an EU-located runner** — fixes latency only, est. → **~30–40 min**, costs money. **RECOMMENDATION ON THE TABLE, founder deferred the decision to the next session (2026-09-01): take (B), the ephemeral Neon branch.** Reasoning to re-read before deciding: Fortleva's value is tenant isolation enforced IN the database, and (A)'s container would stop testing that against the real thing — the pooler `maxWait` exhaustion class of bug that already bit once is precisely what it would stop catching, so cheap minutes would buy a gate we trust less. (B) lands ~50–60 min/run, under the allowance at the current pace, and it is the fix this repo already chose — the `TODO(founder) NEON_API_KEY` is sitting in `ci.yml`. Founder action needed first: create a Neon API key and add it as a repo secret; then it is a normal reviewed slice. Until then, batching pushes is the cheapest lever and is already the habit. **A FOURTH option surfaced 2026-09-01 and is parked with the others: a US-region database FOR CI ONLY.** It arrived as generic advice from another project ("create the Neon database in the US"), and for a generic project it is right — co-locating compute and database turns ~100 ms per query into ~1–5 ms, which is the entire tax here. **For Fortleva's real data it is closed and must stay closed:** ARCHITECTURE.md:13 makes EU residency non-negotiable ("it disqualified vendors outright, before DX or price"), it is why Clerk and WorkOS were rejected, and a Neon project's **region is immutable** — "move to US" means a new project plus a migration of personal data out of the EU. The version worth discussing is narrower: a **throwaway CI-only database holding nothing but seeded fixtures** is arguably not personal data, so a US test database would not touch the residency promise while erasing the latency. That is a SECURITY ruling, not a convenience call — it needs its own review (what leaks into fixtures, what the DPA says, whether e2e ever carries real-looking client data), and it should be decided AFTER the (B) vs (C) pick, not instead of it. Do not act on the generic advice as written. Pick one before the next heavy build phase, or the allowance goes again in ~2 weeks. Check the balance at github.com/settings/billing (the billing API needs a token scope agents should not request).

**What the first public CI run taught (2026-08-20, run [32378425410](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32378425410) + [32379298971](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32379298971)):**
- *Private-era reds (Aug 17–19) were the billing lock* — "job was not started because recent account payments have failed", zero steps executed — not product code.
- *`ci.yml` cancelled itself on consecutive pushes* (fixed `7b7e23f`): both db-touching jobs shared the `isolation-db` concurrency group; GitHub keeps **one running + one pending job per group and evicts the previously pending one** — `cancel-in-progress: false` only protects the *running* job. Push A's e2e (pending behind A's isolation) was evicted by push B's isolation; B's isolation was then evicted by B's own e2e a second after B's check passed. Now: workflow-level `concurrency: ci-${{ github.ref }}` + `cancel-in-progress: true` (a newer push supersedes the run), `e2e: needs: [check, isolation]` (serial by DAG inside a run), ~~the job group kept as the cross-ref guard~~ *(the `isolation-db` group was removed 2026-09-01 with the shared database)*, `timeout-minutes` on the isolation job.
- *The db suite cannot meet its timeouts from a US runner against the EU Neon* (`4168b99`): the 0872785 isolation job ran **26 min** (3 min locally) and every failure was a timeout — vitest's 30 s per test, Prisma's 5 s interactive-transaction budget ("6275 ms passed since the start of the transaction"), plus two cascades from a timed-out shifts test. Mitigation: `DB_TX_TIMEOUT_MS` (read in `src/db/with-tenant.ts`, default 5000) and `DBTEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (`vitest.db.config.ts`, default 30 000) — **CI sets 20 000 / 120 000**, local stays tight; isolation job `timeout-minutes: 45`. The durable fix is founder-side: **a runner in the EU** (see the provisioning item) — the database stays in Frankfurt; until then CI is slow but green.
- *The first public e2e job (7bfac5d) was cancelled by its 25-min budget about half-way through 29 tests, with 11 failures of two kinds:* **1–6** (14:43–14:52) were the app's own 5 s transaction budget expiring under the link ("A commit cannot be executed on an expired transaction … 7065 ms passed") — covered by `DB_TX_TIMEOUT_MS` on the e2e job; **7–11** (from 14:52:51) were **a local e2e run's teardown sweeping the live CI tenant** — `sweepStaleE2ETenants(15)` treated the 16-minute-old CI fixture as an orphan. Fixed in the harness commit after `c875285`: age guard **90 min** (setup + teardown), CI e2e `timeout-minutes: 60`. Rule until the CI database is separate: **do not run the e2e suite locally while a CI e2e job is running** — they share the dev database, and a run longer than the age guard is fair game for the other's sweep.
- *Run [32385734032](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32385734032) (6cd9388, first with the fixes): check green; isolation **198 / 201 in 18 min** — the three left were the budgets the env default does not reach: a caller's explicit `timeoutMs` (`LOCKED_TX` 15 s overshot by 223 ms for 8 serialised starts) and Prisma's `maxWait` (2 s to acquire a connection; "Unable to start a transaction in the given time" under 25 parallel counter transactions, then a cascade). Fix (`aae409c`): `src/db/with-tenant.ts` derives one **link factor** = `DB_TX_TIMEOUT_MS / 5000` and scales the default, every explicit `timeoutMs` and `maxWait` by it (factor 1 wherever the variable is unset — production and local unchanged). e2e was skipped by the DAG.
- *Run [32387969487](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32387969487) (aae409c): check green, **isolation 201/201 green in 18 min** — first full green of the db suite on public CI; the browser harness ran 60 min and was cancelled by its ceiling about two-thirds through 31 tests.* Two things inside that job, kept apart on purpose:
  - **Real findings (fixed in HEAD), surfaced by the four visual stops added this session and never photographed before:** (1) **React #418 hydration mismatch on `/time` and `/time/team`** whenever rows exist — `time-week.tsx` and `team-table.tsx` built `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (weekday/day, clock) *in client components*, so the label was rendered once by Node's ICU (SSR) and once by Chromium's (hydration); on CI (Node 22 / Chromium) the two disagreed. Both pages now format the labels on the server with `dateFormat()` from `@/lib/format` and pass strings (`dayLabels`, `timeLabel`) down. It did not reproduce locally because a `visual`-only run has no rows — verify time-page changes with `playwright test time visual` (time.spec seeds entries + a shift first). (2) On `/time` at 390 px the week grid's **row verbs sat outside the table's visible box** (clock column now `priority="medium"`), and the **day-header total was pushed off the right edge** (a fixed `colSpan={5}` + separate total cell assumed all seven columns visible) — now one spanning cell with label + total.
  - **Latency-shaped failures (not product):** money tiles not visible in 10 s, the staff-notice ack not clearing in 15 s, a visibility flip not landing in 10 s, the 404 stop's navigation timing out — all pages/actions that pass locally and in the money spec. Mitigation (`20a0b75`): `playwright.config.ts` gives CI a longer leash (`timeout` 300 s, `expect` 30 s; local 120 s / 10 s unchanged) and the e2e job ceiling is 120 min. **This is the last widening** — if HEAD's run is still red for these reasons, provision the US-region CI database before touching anything else.
- *Run [32398402887](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32398402887) (caf874f): check + isolation green, browser harness **25 / 31 in 49 min, ran to completion.*** Money, scoping, visibility, timeline, pwa, account, theme, inline-edit all pass on the link now. The six left: the four visual sweeps still reported `uncaught page errors` on `/time` and `/time-team` — so the ICU-of-`DateTimeFormat` theory was only half of it — and two `time.spec` tests whose *explicit* 15 s waits (timer start, clock-in: a server action plus a full `/time` refresh) the 30 s config default does not reach. **Root cause of the hydration error, confirmed byte-for-byte (HEAD):** `formatDurationHm` used `Intl.DurationFormat` *when present*. It is present in Chromium and Node ≥ 23, **absent in Node 22 (the runner)**, and renders `{ minutes: 0 }` as **`""`** while the fallback renders `"0m"` — so the freshly created 0-minute rows on `/time` and 0-minute member totals on `/time/team` hydrated to different text. Locally Node 24 and Chromium 151 agree (both `""` — itself a small product bug: an empty duration cell), which is why it never reproduced. `src/lib/format.ts` no longer touches `Intl.DurationFormat`: hours/minutes go through `Intl.NumberFormat` unit style (checked identical Node ↔ Chromium for en and sv, prints `0m` for zero) and the clock is built from padded `NumberFormat` digits. `time.spec` scales its explicit waits ×3 on CI (`SLOW`).
- *Run [32406201674](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32406201674) (1211c3f): check + isolation green (39 min — slow evening), browser harness **25 pass · 1 flaky · 5 fail in 1.1 h, ran to completion; no `uncaught page errors` anywhere — the hydration fix holds.** The five: the four visual sweeps hit the spec's OWN hard-coded `test.setTimeout(300_000)` (~35 stops at ~10 s each on this link; now `900_000` on CI, 300 s locally), and `time.spec`'s undo test found the **undo toast gone** by the time the slow refresh had shown the new timer — sonner's 4 s default against a server undo window of 120 s; the toast now lives 30 s (HEAD) — a real UX fix, the test order is unchanged. The flaky one (`visibility.spec` "a failed change says so") passed on retry: a toast not visible within 30 s on the first try.
- *Run [32417151021](https://github.com/azcheema/fortleva/actions/runs/32417151021) (1d7c8d3): **all green** — check 55 s, isolation 27 min 53 s, browser harness 31/31 in 46.9 min with no retries.* Five pushes from the first public run to a green pipeline; everything that was the app's or the harness's fault is fixed (concurrency self-cancel, the 5 s/30 s budgets, the sweep collision, two hydration bugs, the phone grid, the undo toast), and the rest is geography. **Standing cost until an EU-located runner exists: ≈ 1 h 17 m per push.** Do not widen anything further; if a future run is red on `Test timeout`/`toBeVisible` alone, the runner's location is the move (founder item) — never the database's.

Options, in order of fit with the all-EU stance: **(a) accept ≈ 1 h 17 m per push — free, everything in the EU, green** (current); **(b) a GitHub-hosted *larger* runner with Azure private networking in an EU region** (North Europe / France Central / Norway East…) — needs a paid Team plan + an Azure subnet; keeps GitHub's hosted-runner isolation; ≈ 20 min; **(c) a self-hosted runner in the EU** (e.g. a Hetzner box in Falkenstein) — cheapest, but GitHub's own guidance: *"self-hosted runners should almost never be used for public repositories"* (any PR can run code on it); only with an ephemeral/JIT runner and PR workflows kept off it. **Not** a US-region database: the earlier note suggesting one is withdrawn. Only the vault stance (**CP4**) actually blocks a phase (3V).

**Standing traps — each cost a real bug; do not rediscover them:**
- **(2026-09-11, CLOSED 2026-09-15 by panel slice 10 — `20260915120000`) The comment write-skew.** `comment_denorm_guard` read its subject with NO lock and NO liveness check, so a CLIENT_VISIBLE comment and its item's make-private (or delete) could both commit. Now the guard reads the subject `FOR SHARE` and alive for every write except an UPDATE that leaves the row INTERNAL on the subject it already had (the lever never waits); the service share-locks the task BEFORE any comment row (`loadItemInScope(…, {lock: "SHARE"})`), which is `deleteItem`'s order (item → thread), so no cycle closes and the comment writer never joins the rank-lock queue (it locks ONE work_item row and no queued writer locks a comment row). The predicate is keyed on "the one write that can break nothing", not on "visibility after the write": a review finder showed the first form let an INTERNAL row be re-pointed onto a soft-deleted subject unchecked. Pinned deterministically in `comments.dbtest.ts` (held downgrade → the reply waits then is refused; held delete → even an INTERNAL insert waits then finds the row gone; a flip to INTERNAL under a held task does not wait, a raise does) and by the contact-INSERT positive control in `work.dbtest.ts`, which now exercises `FOR SHARE` under the contact principal. What a flip to INTERNAL / an edit / a member's delete still waits on: its history row's foreign key takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on the task, so it can wait behind a rank move's `FOR UPDATE` — as every activity writer does — never behind a make-private or a delete.
- **(2026-09-11) A work service that locks MORE THAN ONE work_item row of a project must take `lockProjectRanks` first** (`src/modules/work/rank-lock.ts`), before its first row lock, and re-read afterwards whatever it read before the wait (single-row writers do not queue, so they commit during it). None of the multi-row writers locks in tree order (moves go by rank either way, bulk edits by scan order), so a lock ORDER cannot be imposed — only serialisation works; a "take the parent first" fix was reviewed and shown to move the cycles, not remove them. A future undo/restore is such a writer (its trigger share-locks the parent) and must also map the `RESTORE_*` tokens.
- **(2026-09-11) Three OLDER lockers are outside that queue, and NOTHING RETRIES A DEADLOCK (40P01) anywhere** — no service, not `withTenant`, not `retryOnRankCollision` (unique violations only); the loser surfaces as an unmapped action error. (1) **The portal toggle's fan-out** (`setPortalEnabled` → `project_portal_enabled_fanout`, every row of the project in scan order) — and a worse race beside it: `stamp_portal_enabled` reads the project unlocked, so a row inserted while a portal DISABLE is in flight keeps `portal_enabled = true` (the fan-out's UPDATE snapshot never sees it): client-visible content readable with the portal off. **Close before the portal ships** — candidates: the rank lock inside the fan-out trigger (projects cannot import the work module; SQL can), and/or a deferred check re-deriving `portal_enabled` at commit. (2) **`copyWeek`**: each copied time entry's foreign key takes FOR KEY SHARE on its work item, several items in date order, and a move's neighbour locks (FOR UPDATE) and rank UPDATE (a key update — `rank` is in a unique index) conflict with it. (3) **`deleteItem` vs an attachment's visibility flip**: item → attachments on one side, attachment → item (via `document_anchor_guard`'s FOR SHARE) on the other; narrowing that guard's lock to writes that can break child ≤ parent (as `work_item_parent_guard` now does) would free the flip-to-INTERNAL lever. A bounded, jittered 40P01 retry around the work and time writers is the general remedy; it wants its own slice (re-running a transaction body is safe only where the body has no side effect outside the database).
- **A fixture that MIXES wall-clock writes with hard-coded dates drifts PERMANENTLY, and not on a schedule.** `timer.ts` stamps a stopped timer's entry from the clock, while the rest of `time.dbtest.ts` pins its entries to August 2026 — and `project_time_summary` rolls up per (project, month). So from 2026-09-01 that project owns TWO summary months and keeps owning them: the old `toEqual([summary.id])` was green for eleven days after it was written and red every day since. **This is NOT a once-a-month flake — do not go looking on the 1st.** Both visibility fan-outs (`project_hours_sharing_fanout`, `project_portal_enabled_fanout`) are project-wide with no month predicate, so flipping `hoursSharingMode` exposes every month at once. Assert against DERIVED state — here, every summary the project owns — never against a row COUNT that the fixture's dates happen to produce, and never by filtering on the same column the RLS policy reads (that is circular). Reproduced identically against Neon and the container: the calendar, never the database.
- **React 19 resets a `<form action>`** at the start of every action (`requestFormReset`), restoring native controls to their SSR value and never re-syncing while props are unchanged. Never put a `<select>`/checkbox that must reflect server state inside a `<form action>` — call the action in a transition with `useOptimistic` (see `files/visibility-select.tsx`).
- **An action failure must never look like a revert.** Return a typed `ActionResult` and toast it; `redirect(withError(...))` remounts the row showing the old value.
- **`[&_tr:last-child]:border-0` on a table body deletes row-level left cues** — it was silently removing the client-visible marker on the last row of every table. Use `border-b-0`.
- **A `"use client"` module's exported constant interpolated into a server component's `className`** becomes a throwing client reference: Next replaces every export of a client module.
- **A shared component that must reflect stored state needs that state as a required prop** (or its own store). `ThemeToggle` defaulting to `"system"` and re-applying it on mount re-broke the user's choice on every menu open.
- **A parsed value is not a raw one.** `themeOnMount(readStoredTheme(), …)` handed an already-parsed preference to a cookie-string parser and silently fell through to a fallback for weeks; the types were too loose to object. Where a function parses, brand or narrow its input so the pre-parsed value cannot be passed.
- **A prop carrying server state goes stale.** A layout is not re-rendered on a cookie write or a client navigation, so anything a client component captured at page load is wrong from the next user action onward. Read live client state from its own source; use the prop only as the server snapshot.
- **Never run `pnpm build`, `pnpm start` or the e2e suite while `next dev` is running** — the production build rewrites `.next` underneath the dev server and the browser reports only “An unexpected Turbopack error”. Kill it by PID (a background dev server outlives killing the `pnpm` wrapper), `rm -rf .next`, restart.
- **A `"use server"` module may export only async functions** — a sync helper exported next to the actions breaks `next build` ("Server Actions must be async functions"); keep pure helpers in a sibling module (`time/label.ts`).
- **Components mounted twice for two breakpoints** (the timer pill lives in a desktop and a mobile slot) make a strict Playwright locator resolve to 2 elements — scope with `.first()`/visibility, and never `isVisible().catch(() => false)` on a multi-match locator (the strict violation is swallowed as "not visible").
- **Python edit scripts on Windows**: `write_text` converts LF→CRLF (use `write_bytes`), the Bash tool collapses `\\` in heredocs (write scripts with the Write tool), and an "old is a prefix of new" anchor re-applies on every rerun.
- **`pnpm test:db` leaves its throwaway tenants behind** (`scope-*`, `projects-*`). The e2e harness sweeps its own; the vitest suite does not. Unfixed, low stakes.
- **`Intl.*` formatters in a client component are a hydration hazard** — Node's ICU (SSR) and the browser's ICU can disagree, and an API that exists on one side only (`Intl.DurationFormat`: Chromium + Node ≥ 23, not Node 22) silently takes a different branch: `{ minutes: 0 }` → `""` vs the fallback's `"0m"` was the real `/time` mismatch. React 19 reports #418 only where the text differs, i.e. only on some machines. Format on the server where you can (`@/lib/format`, memoised) and pass strings; in `format.ts` use only APIs that exist everywhere the code runs and check Node ↔ Chromium output byte-for-byte (`scripts`-style parity run); the visual sweep's `uncaught page errors` audit is the tripwire, but only when the page has rows — seed first (`playwright test time visual`).
- **Prisma 7 + the pg adapter hides the constraint name of a hand-written partial unique / EXCLUDE**: P2002 says "Unique constraint failed on the (not available)", `meta.target` is absent, and the name is only in `meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage`. `mapDbError` (`src/lib/db-error-map.ts` since 2026-09-11; one token table per module — `time/ctx.ts`, `work/db-errors.ts`) scans the whole `meta` for its tokens; any new token-to-DomainError mapping must be proven by a dbtest that actually collides (the work-type one was not, and shipped raw).
- **A disabled `<select>` posts nothing.** A pinned value (the Agreements tab's `SERVICE` scope) travels as a hidden input and the select loses its `name`; otherwise the action sees `null` and answers "Invalid input".
- **Listing a ✦ resource is itself ✦.** `authorize()` requires a factor within 15 min for every `requiresMfa` code, so `listCostRateCards` throws `MFA_REQUIRED` for an un-enrolled owner on page load. Never `handleAuthzRedirect` from a page's read path — render the section with a step-up/enrol *link* (`mfaRedirectTarget`) and redirect only on the explicit ask (`?cost=1`), or the page bounces everyone without a factor to enrolment on arrival.
- **A fixed `colSpan` in a table with column priority is wrong on phones** — hidden columns still count for the span on desktop and not on mobile; give a group row ONE cell that spans everything and lay the cell out with flex.
- **A local suite and a real-Neon CI job can still delete each other's fixtures** *(rewritten 2026-09-01 — the old form said "local and CI e2e runs share the dev database", which stopped being true of CI when both db jobs moved onto their own service container)*. LOCAL `pnpm test:db` / `pnpm test:e2e` still use the shared dev database, and the harness sweeps `e2e-*` tenants older than its age guard (now 90 min) at setup and teardown. The ordinary CI pipeline is now out of range entirely. The one remaining overlap is a **dispatched `neon-smoke.yml` run**, which does target the dev database — its `concurrency: neon-dev-db` group stops a second smoke run but cannot stop a person. Do not run the local db or e2e suites while a Neon fidelity smoke run is in flight.
- **GitHub Actions concurrency keeps one pending job per group** and evicts the previously pending one when another arrives; `cancel-in-progress: false` protects only the running job. Two db jobs in one group + two pushes = both cancelled. Serialise inside a run with `needs`, supersede across pushes with a per-ref workflow group.
- **A dbtest that creates a COST card mints a `tenant_key`** (v2 encryption); delete `tenantKey` before `f.cleanup()` or the tenant delete hits RESTRICT and the fixture leaks (three `money-*` orphans were swept by hand). **`jsonb` reorders metadata keys** — sort before asserting a key list. **`createEntry` refuses the future** — fixture dates must be in the past relative to the real clock (the test that wrote "September" entries in August failed with INVALID_DURATION).
- **Automated agents must never create accounts or write to the database outside a throwaway tenant.** One created an owner-level account in tenant zero to render a page; it was revoked. Every build prompt must carry that prohibition, and every data-safety claim must be re-audited independently.

**Dev helpers that exist:** `scripts/create-test-member.ts` (seed a member with a known password for scoping tests), `scripts/preview-as-contact.ts` (terminal "view as client" through the real RLS gate — the portal UI arrives in Phase 3), `pnpm test:e2e` (browser suite; `pnpm exec playwright test visual` regenerates 128 screenshots into `.design-shots/`).

## 1. Ordering: the brief's sequence holds (§11)

The brief asked directly: *should productization come earlier?* **No. The research found no reason to move it, and several to keep it at Phase 7.**

1. **Solo capacity is the binding constraint.** One full-time founder cannot run onboarding, support, billing operations, and dunning for strangers while the core domain (clients, projects, invoices, portal) is still being built. Productizing early converts build time into support time at the worst possible moment.
2. **Tenant zero is the validation loop.** Running Naxdor on Phases 1–6 finds the design errors (§1) before any paying tenant sees them. Selling at Phase 3 means selling a portal with no contracts, no invoices, and no issues — an empty product in exactly the market where [Assembly](https://assembly.com/pricing), SuiteDash, and Hubflo are feature-complete (§10.8).
3. **The classic retrofit risk is already defused.** The reason teams regret late productization is retrofitting entitlements into scattered plan checks (§4). This plan lands the entitlement *shape* — the versioned `entitlements` JSON on `Tenant`, the four-gate resolver, `TenantPreference`, `FeatureFlag` — in **Phase 1**, with every module gated from the day it ships. Phase 7 then wires Stripe to a resolver that already exists; it is plumbing, not surgery.
4. **No revenue pressure.** Running cost pre-productization is under ~$50/mo (Vercel Pro + Neon + R2 + Upstash free tier — see `ARCHITECTURE.md` §6). There is nothing to monetize early to cover.

The honest counterargument — earlier external validation of willingness-to-pay — loses at this scale: the competitive research already validates the category (a dozen funded competitors), and the differentiators (EU residency, continuity box) are validated by their *absence* everywhere else, not by an early checkout page.

**Pushback — launch sequencing (§12).** The brief puts the continuity box (the strongest differentiator, §8) *after* productization. I keep that order — the box's trigger model consumes billing state (lapsed-subscription dead-man signals) and the platform console (veto disputes), both Phase 7 artifacts — but the consequence is that at the moment self-signup opens, the flagship feature does not exist yet. Recommendation: treat Phase 7's self-signup as a **soft launch** (waitlist / hand-onboarded tenants), and time the public marketing launch after Phase 8, so "the agency platform with a continuity box" is true on day one of saying it. Phases 7 and 8 should be planned back-to-back.

**Note on Phase 6.** After the settled scope deltas (decision #7: reports v1 = uploaded PDFs as client-visible `Document`s + CrUX charts; GSC/GA4 sync → v2), Phase 6 is the smallest phase (~1–2 weeks). It keeps its number so all eight docs agree, but it can ship inside the Phase 5 release window if convenient — it is still independently shippable on its own. *(2026-08-16: Phase 6 gains the project-health portfolio table and charts — now ~2 wk; see its section.)*

**Ordering revised 2026-08-16 (work-management plan; decisions 11–13, `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`).** The founder reviewed the running Phase-1 shell (commit `78b58b5`) and redirected the product toward *"the agency's operating system with a client window"*: ADO's data model (generic work item, category-typed states, single rank, Epic → Task → Subtask) under a Planner/Linear surface, plus first-class time & cost, selective client sharing with progress updates, and a per-client credential vault. Phase numbers 1–8 stay stable so every doc keeps agreeing; three new phases are inserted and one is rescoped. **The execution order is now `1b → 2 → 2W → 2T → 3 → 3V → 5 → 4 → 6 → 7 → 8`.** Why:

- **Naxdor's daily need is tasks + time.** Boards after 2W (~week 10) and timers + cost after 2T (~week 14) are what makes tenant zero *use* the product every day; nothing else generates that validation loop as early.
- **A portal without work behind it is empty.** Phase 3 (portal) now sits *after* 2W/2T so the first client logs in to shared tasks, milestones, updates and (opt-in) hours — not a bare timeline.
- **5 before 4** because Phase 5 is short (Issue absorbed into `WorkItem`; what remains is digests/inbox/push/schedules) and completes the portal loop, while Naxdor keeps invoicing elsewhere a few more weeks. Phase 4 is regulated and long; it must not block the collaboration loop.
- **3V after 3** because the vault's share links and portal credential submission ride the Contact identity stack. Security tests land before UI, no exceptions.
- **CP3 may swap 3/3V or 4/5** — schema is unaffected either way (see Checkpoints).
- Estimates: 1b 2–3 · 2 3 · 2W 5 · 2T 4 · 3 5 · 3V 3–4 · 5 2–3 · 4 7–8 · 6 2 ≈ **34–37 wk to end of Phase 6**, then 7/8 (~12–16 wk) as planned. Riskiest overruns: 2W (UX polish is unbounded — cap with the fixed screen list and the one-`<WorkItemView>` rule), 4 (regulated), 3V (security tests before UI).
- **Step 0 was docs, not code:** the spec docs contradicted this direction (skip-list "Time tracking", "pointers not secrets", `Issue` entity, 63-code catalog test). They received dated amendments on 2026-08-16 — history struck, not deleted — before any phase build resumes.

## 2. Working rules — every phase

**"Independently shippable" means:** at the end of the phase, the system is deployed, Naxdor (tenant zero) uses the new capability on real work, nothing half-built is reachable in the UI, and the phase's non-negotiable tests run green in CI. A phase that cannot be left alone for three months afterward is not done.

**Standing definition of done, every phase (§12):**

- [ ] CI green, including the cross-tenant isolation suite (runs on every PR from Phase 1 forever — `TENANCY.md` §11) and the phase's deny-matrix additions.
- [ ] The four non-negotiable test families exist for everything the phase touched: **tenant isolation, client-level scoping, file visibility, privilege escalation** (§12).
- [ ] Every new privileged operation is in the `AuditEvent` static catalog with write-time visibility (`SECURITY.md` §7).
- [ ] Every new module sits behind its entitlement gate + `TenantPreference` toggle (§4), even while entitlements default to unlimited.
- [ ] All new strings in Swedish and English via i18n; no hardcoded copy; no assumption of exactly two languages (§12).

- [ ] **Amazon SES `eu-central-1` — start in week 1** (decision 10, ARC-09). Sending domain **`mailer.naxdor.com`**, custom MAIL FROM **`bounce.mailer.naxdor.com`**. Order: pre-flight `aws sesv2 get-account --region eu-central-1` plus `list-email-identities` (catches a pre-existing identity or an already-pending review that would 409 the request) → publish `_dmarc.mailer` → create the identity → publish the three Easy DKIM CNAMEs (tokens only exist *after* creation; use the returned `SigningHostedZone`, never a hardcoded suffix, and no leading underscore on the token) → publish the MAIL FROM `MX 10 feedback-smtp.eu-central-1.amazonses.com` + `TXT v=spf1 include:amazonses.com ~all` on `bounce.mailer`, then enable custom MAIL FROM → IAM principal scoped by `ses:FromAddress` → config set + SNS + webhook + DLQ → mailbox-simulator tests → file production access. **`send.naxdor.com` is off-limits** — it carries a live SES `eu-west-1` MAIL FROM (ARC-09); audit and decommission it as a *separate* change with its own rollback. **Nothing on the `naxdor.com` apex may be touched** — not SPF, not MX, not `default._domainkey`, not `_dmarc`. *(2026-08-16: founder provisioning; the dev outbox `.dev-outbox/outbox.jsonl` carries development until Phase 3's real invites.)*
- [ ] **Bounce/complaint webhook — EU-pinned, verified, dead-lettered.** The SNS payload carries recipient email addresses (personal data), so the route inherits ARC-01's `fra1` pin and that pin must be *asserted*, not assumed — Vercel Functions default to `iad1` (Washington DC), which would process recipient addresses in the US and contradict `SECURITY.md` §9.3. Also: confirm Vercel Deployment Protection does not cover the path (SNS posts the subscription confirmation unauthenticated and a 401 presents as a subscription that never confirms); SNS posts `Content-Type: text/plain`, so read the raw body; branch `bounceSubType` — `OnAccountSuppressionList`/`OnTenantSuppressionList` mean "already known bad", do **not** count toward the bounce rate, and must not trigger reputation escalation. Account-level suppression *management* APIs are disabled in the sandbox, so the GDPR erasure path (`DeleteSuppressedDestination`) is a **post-approval** task. *(2026-08-16: lands with SES production access — Phase 3 at the latest, Phase 5 backstop; writes `EmailSuppression` from 2W.)*
- [ ] **Decide the reply path for `mailer.naxdor.com` before the first invite ships.** Nothing in the record set can *receive* mail, and the A-wildcard means a reply to `noreply@mailer.naxdor.com` reaches a Vercel edge with no SMTP listener and fails at connect. For an invite-driven product that is a product defect, not a mail detail. Cheapest fix: a `Reply-To` on a monitored SiteGround mailbox — changes no DNS, touches no apex record. (An MX on `mailer.` is also permitted; AWS's "MAIL FROM must not receive mail" restriction binds `bounce.mailer`, not `mailer`.) *(2026-08-16: CP6 question.)*

## Phase 2 — Core domain, trimmed to what 2W needs *(retitled and rescoped 2026-08-16)*

**Goal:** Naxdor's real client and project records live here, not in spreadsheets — and the scoping/RLS/export rails that every later table rides are proven on small entities first.

**Scope:**

- [x] `Client` — company details, org.nr / VAT ID, billing address, assigned members; **internal private notes** (visibility `internal`, never in any portal-reachable query path) (§6).
- [x] `Contact` — person records at a client (name, email, role). Records only; portal identity arrives in Phase 3 (decision #6 keeps the identity stacks separate).
- [x] `MemberClient`, `MemberProject` assignment tables wired into the Phase-1 `authorize()` seam; deny-default live (decision #5). *(2026-08-16: **scoping goes live here** — `authorizedResourceIds(actor, 'client')` **and** `'project'`, `assertInScope(tx, actor, {clientId|projectId})` (deny-default → NOT_FOUND), and a `scopeWhere(actor)` helper composing both axes into every list `where`.)*
- [x] `Project` — type, scope, status, start/launch dates, environments, repo link, hosting details; `ProjectVersion` (current version, release notes) + `Milestone`; the **timeline / stage view** — milestones + version list, deliberately not a Gantt (§6, decision #7). This is the portal's centerpiece next phase; design it well now. *(2026-08-16 additions — `DATA_MODEL.md` amendment:* `Project.key` (≤ 8 chars, unique per tenant, e.g. `ACME`), `portalEnabled=false`, `hoursSharingMode {NONE, HOURS, BILLABLE_AMOUNT} = NONE`, `billingCurrency`, `defaultBillable`, `leadMemberId`, `updateCadence=NONE`, `autoArchiveMonths?`, `autoStartParent` / `autoCompleteParent`; `Milestone` gains `rank`, status widened to `{PLANNED, IN_PROGRESS, PAUSED, DONE, CANCELLED}`, `@@unique([tenantId, id])` and a composite-FK target; `ProjectVersion` as drafted — small, keeps the version timeline.)*
- [x] `Service` — what the client buys (one-off / retainer / hosting / SEO / maintenance; recurring vs one-time; renewal dates as data). Renewal *automation* is Phase 4; the entity lands here because Phase 3's portal reads it.
- [x] `Document` — general storage layer over `FileObject`/`FileVersion`: attach to `Client`/`Project`, folders or tags, version history, visibility flag surfaced in UI (default `internal`, §5). *(2026-08-16: real FKs `clientId/projectId`; `AttachableType` extended (WORK_ITEM / COMMENT / PROJECT_UPDATE / CREDENTIAL / ASSET reserved now); `Document.kind {GENERAL, DELIVERABLE, REPORT, EXPORT}`; attach UI.)*
- [x] **Class-B RLS with `portal_enabled` from day one** *(2026-08-16 — `TENANCY.md` §7.2 amendment)*: every project-scoped class-B table (here: `Milestone`, `ProjectVersion`, `Service`, `Document`-with-`projectId`) carries `visibility`, denormalised `client_id` and `portal_enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, maintained by an `AFTER UPDATE OF portal_enabled ON project` trigger fanning out in the same tx; RESTRICTIVE `portal_gate` = `client_id = app.client_id AND visibility='CLIENT_VISIBLE' AND portal_enabled`. Registered as `projectScoped` in the model registry.
- [x] *Platform-continuity cheap win #2:* **per-tenant export v0** — manually triggered export of all tenant entities (DMMF-driven JSONL + files + schema-versioned manifest). Standing rule from here: every later phase extends the manifest as part of its definition of done. — *As built 2026-08-17 (stage C):* Prisma 7 has no runtime DMMF, so the census is **registry-driven** (`MODEL_CLASSES.tenantRoot + tenant + audit` → `src/export/manifest.ts`, tripwire test); `generateTenantExport()` under `tenant:export` ✦ dumps every model as JSONL inside ONE tenant-scoped tx under the requesting member (RLS decides what leaves; encrypted `Tenant.bankgiro/plusgiro/iban/bic/databaseUrl` and `TenantKey.wrappedDek` stripped), lists committed files, bundles their bytes when ≤ 200 MB (else pointers; mode stated in `manifest.json`), zips with `fflate`, writes through the `StorageTransport` (`putObject`, new) as `FileObject(kind=EXPORT)` + `Document(kind=EXPORT, INTERNAL, "export-<date>.zip")` so it downloads via the presigned path; audit `export.requested` → `export.generated` → `export.downloaded`. UI `/settings/export`. Not quota-gated by design.
- [x] **`TenantPreference` UI** *(2026-08-16)* — `/settings/preferences`: locale, timezone, week start, duration style, currency, module toggles. — *2026-08-17 (stage C):* `src/preferences` (`Tenant.defaultLocale` on the tenant row; `ui.timezone`, `ui.weekStart`, `ui.showIsoWeek`, `ui.durationStyle`, `finance.currencyDefault`, `module.<key>.enabled` as `TenantPreference` rows — the key gate 3 reads); `settings:view` reads, `settings:edit` writes, `settings:manage_modules` ✦ flips modules; audit `preference.changed {key}` only; auto-save form; `/account` gains a personal time zone (`Member.timezone`, audit `member.profile_updated`).
